Sikorski said: “I expect an attack on Russian territory under a false flag, to which Putin will ‘respond’.”



Putin has himself warned: “They understand that retaliation will follow. I think everyone understands this, or should understand it.”

News.title: Seven key details missing from Netflix’s Toxic Love Story doc from sordid sex tape to Angela Diaz’s life after prison
News.content:
THE Netflix documentary A Toxic Love Story stunned viewers with the bizarre tale of a love triangle that spiraled into a shocking criminal case.

The film explored how couple Angela and Ian Diaz were accused of framing his former fiancee, Michelle Hadley, in an elaborate cyberstalking hoax.



The scheme involved fake online accounts and threatening messages.

They fabricated evidence designed to make it appear Michelle was targeting Angela, including a disturbing Craigslist “rape fantasy” plot in which Angela claimed a stranger had been encouraged to attack her.



Michelle was arrested in July 2016 and spent 88 days in a California state prison after being accused of a crime she insisted she did not commit.

The charges were eventually dropped, and the investigation took a dramatic turn when authorities accused Ian and Angela of orchestrating the harassment campaign themselves.

Angela later pleaded guilty to multiple felony charges, including conspiracy and falsely reporting crimes, and was sentenced to five years in prison.

Ian, a former U.S. Marshals Service employee, was also later convicted for his role in the scheme.

He initially pleaded not guilty to federal charges including conspiracy to commit cyberstalking, cyberstalking, perjury and obstruction of justice before a jury found him guilty.

He is serving more than 10 years behind bars in Texas.



While the documentary revealed the shocking downfall of the couple, there were several details from court records, civil lawsuits and witness statements that were not included.

Those include Angela’s alleged history of deception, the outcome of the bitter dispute over the couple’s Anaheim condo and the wider events that led Michelle to spend nearly three months in jail.

Here, The U.S. Sun breaks down seven key pieces of the puzzle left out of the film.

Angela’s web of lies

The film features an interview with Angela’s ex-boyfriend from before she met Ian, who revealed she had lied about suffering from Stage 4 cancer.

Later in the doc, Ian also revealed she had faked being pregnant with twins.



But divorce filings, court records and witness statements described what prosecutors portrayed as an even broader pattern of alleged deception.

During the criminal case, Angela was accused of fabricating major parts of her personal history, including aspects of her education, employment and background.

Prosecutors argued the scheme targeting Michelle was not an isolated incident, but part of a years-long pattern of manipulation and fabricated stories.

They alleged Angela repeatedly created false narratives involving pregnancies, illnesses and personal crises, and used those claims to gain sympathy, financial help, and gifts.



Secret sex tape allegation

One of the most disturbing allegations involving Ian emerged from a civil lawsuit Michelle filed against her ex.

In the complaint, Michelle alleged he repeatedly pressured her into taking part in a sexual encounter with another man while he watched.

She claimed that on Valentine’s Day 2014, while she was sick and taking cold medication, she “finally gave in” after Ian “arranged for a stranger from Craigslist to come over, gave [Michelle] three shots of whisky, and set up cameras in their bedroom.”

Michelle alleged in the suit that Ian watched from another room while the encounter was recorded.



She later told BuzzFeed News she asked him to destroy the footage, but claimed he refused, telling her, “No one put a gun to your head.”

Michelle said the incident left her traumatized and was part of a wider pattern of controlling and manipulative behavior during their relationship.

The allegations were made in civil court filings and were never the subject of criminal charges against Ian, who denied wrongdoing.

The civil lawsuit was later settled before it went to trial.



The condo dispute

Ian and Michelle bought the Anaheim condo together in June 2015 while they were engaged, taking out a mortgage of nearly $460,000 on the property.

According to court records, Michelle contributed $14,401.20 toward the down payment, although both she and Ian were listed as owners.

After the couple split in August 2015, Michelle moved out while remaining responsible for half of the monthly mortgage payments, even though Ian continued living in the condo.

In late 2015, the former couple hired real estate attorneys and reached an agreement that Ian would become solely responsible for the mortgage beginning in June 2016.



If he failed to make the payments, the condo would be sold and the proceeds divided between them.

The condo dispute later became significant when federal prosecutors alleged it provided a financial motive for the conspiracy.

They argued that Ian sought to pressure Michelle into giving up her ownership stake in the property.

Disney job

In a 2019 interview with BuzzFeed News, Michelle opened up about what she described as a controlling dynamic during her relationship with Ian, months before their split.

Michelle told the outlet that Ian pressured her to leave her job as a marketing support manager for a risk services company in Orange County and accept a position at Disneyland Resort, where he had previously worked.



She said the move came with a major financial sacrifice, claiming the Disneyland job paid around $20,000 less than her previous role.

Michelle told BuzzFeed News she felt the career change also made her more vulnerable, saying she believed Ian wanted her working at Disneyland because his former colleagues could keep an eye on her.

She alleged the move was part of a wider pattern in which Ian attempted to exert control over different areas of her life.



The botched investigation

Michelle maintained from the beginning that she had been framed and denied sending the threatening messages and online posts.

She told authorities she believed evidence pointed away from her, but she was jail before prosecutors dismissed the charges.

Michelle later sued the City of Anaheim and members of the Anaheim Police Department asking for more than $25,000 in damages.

She accused investigators of overlooking evidence that could have cleared her and failing to properly investigate whether she had been framed.

Anaheim denied wrongdoing and argued officers had probable cause for the arrest based on the information available to them at the time.



The department never publicly admitted it mishandled the investigation or apologized for Michelle’s wrongful arrest.

The lawsuit was settled in 2021 with no admission of liability from the city.

Sources told TMZ this week that she settled for around $1.8 million.

Ian’s life behind bars

Ian, a former Deputy U.S. Marshal, was convicted in 2023 for his role in the scheme.

Unlike Angela, who pleaded guilty, the 48-year-old fought the charges at trial and was convicted by a federal jury of conspiracy to commit cyberstalking, cyberstalking, perjury and obstruction of justice.



He was sentenced in 2023 to more than 10 years in federal prison.

The former law enforcement officer, who once investigated crimes as part of his job, is currently housed at the Federal Medical Center (FMC) Fort Worth in Texas.

The facility has also housed Joe Exotic, real name Joseph Maldonado-Passage, who rose to fame through Netflix’s Tiger King documentary.

Exotic is serving a 21-year federal sentence after being convicted of attempting to arrange the murder of Carole Baskin and wildlife violations.

Angela’s new career

After pleading guilty to multiple felony charges connected to the scheme, Angela was sentenced to five years in prison.



She was released in July 2020 after serving around three years of her sentence.

The U.S. Sun previously revealed she now goes by Angi Connell, her maiden name, and has moved to Arizona where she has built a new career focused on peer support, mental health and criminal justice issues.

Connell is listed as Director of Peer Counseling at Exhale Pro-Voice, a nonprofit that provides text-based support services.

The organization’s website states that after spending time in prison, Connell pursued a master’s degree in Psychology and Justice Studies.

She is also working toward a doctorate in psychology with the goal of becoming a licensed psychologist.



In a November 2025 interview with VoyagePhoenix, Connell spoke about rebuilding her life after prison and claimed she had been “wrongfully convicted.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

She described the experience as “harrowing and tragic” and said it transformed her life.

However, there has been no court ruling overturning her conviction, and her guilty plea remains part of the official record.

News.title: How ‘woke’ court ruling sparked explosion of thousands of migrants storming EU border at ‘weak spot’ Spanish enclave
News.content:
THOUSANDS of migrants storming a Spanish enclave’s borders will be emboldened by a “woke” court ruling protecting them.

Migrants intercepted while swimming to Ceuta or Melilla are not subject to immediate expulsion per a Supreme Court ruling three weeks ago.



It found that entering by sea does not involve crossing a physical land border, making “hot returns” inapplicable to existing immigration laws.

The decision has been exploited by people-smuggling gangs and brought with it a wave of undocumented migration.



Police in Ceuta have warned that they risk operational collapse as they lack manpower to deal with such a massive influx.

A Guardia Civil spokesperson said: “It has been a slow trickle since the Supreme Court’s ruling, but today has been an explosion.”



It has vowed to deport migrants who were seen sprinting along beaches and onto the street past the EU’s only land border with Africa.today

Spain‘s socialist government stands out for its pro-migration stance.



It has recently received a huge influx of applications after launching a scheme to provide legal status to 500,000 undocumented migrants.

Authorities in Ceuta have also asked the government in Madrid to declare a national emergency and to send the army in.

The President of Ceuta, Juan Jesus Vivas, was quick to declare a total humanitarian and social emergency in response.



He said: “In the past few days more than 1,500 migrants, both adults and minors, have come to Ceuta by sea.

“The reception centres are saturated – there is no more room for anyone in them and according to yesterday’s figures the number of people entering is more than 200 a day.”

Videos from Tarajal beach show crowds of people, mainly Moroccans, rushing across the sand attempting to make it to the road.

The majority are young men but several whole families, including young children, can also be seen.

They had managed to jump over the border fence separating the city from Morocco, according to Spanish state news agency EFE.



Some could be heard chanting “Viva Espana!” – Long Live Spain – as they walked past.

Ceuta sits between Morocco and Spain at the northwestern tip of Africa.

Along with Spanish autonomous city Melilla, it is the European Union‘s only land border with Africa.

Spain’s interior ministry said several ministries are “acting in coordination to respond with the utmost speed and efficiency to the situation in Ceuta”.

The Moroccan government also promised it would work “faithfully and permanently with Spain” in regards to the ongoing crisis.



They said: “Moroccan security forces are preventing the arrival of numerous people who are trying to reach Ceuta from Morocco.”

Morocco and Spain have reportedly agreed to return migrants who entered Ceuta during the latest surge, according to Hespress.

Vivas said 60 bodies had been recovered at sea in recent months with several washing up to shore in Ceuta.

He has warned the humanitarian crisis will only worsen while migrant centers are so full as hundreds of people will be forced to sleep on the streets.

He added that housing units for minors were now operating at 2,400 per cent capacity.



Back in 2021, 8,000 migrants swam from Morocco into Ceuta over a few days.

The arrivals also included the largest ever number of migrants in a single day, thought to be 6,000.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Ceuta residents had locked themselves indoors as the army rounded up migrants fleeing Morocco, La Vanguardia reported.

Hundreds of migrants risk injuries or even death every year while trying to jump over fences, hide inside vehicles or by swimming around breakwaters that extend into the Mediterranean Sea.

News.title: Beachgoers stunned as bags packed with £600,000 in cash wash up on holiday island shore
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment stunned beachgoers discovered £600,000 in cash washed up on the shore of a holiday island.

Extraordinary footage shows holidaymakers lifting the lid of a shopping bag to reveal bundles of banknotes stacked inside.



One curious onlooker even pulls out a couple of wads of cash before quickly putting them back.

The remarkable discovery was made at Casuzze, a seaside resort on Sicily’s southern coast.



Beachgoers gathered around several bags stuffed with cash after they were allegedly thrown into the sea from a stranded speedboat.

Italian investigators said the 18ft vessel had been travelling from Malta when it reportedly suffered engine trouble.



After running out of fuel, it drifted towards the shoreline carrying three men and a boy believed to be about 13-years-old.

According to investigators, three of the four people on board jumped into the water as the boat continued drifting towards the beach.



As officers closed in on the vessel, they claim the only person left aboard was seen throwing sealed bags into the sea.

The current carried several of the floating bags ashore, where beachgoers helped retrieve them.

Authorities recovered almost all of the money, which is estimated to total between £500,000 and £600,000.

The four occupants were taken in for questioning, while the speedboat was towed to port for forensic examination.

Ragusa Police Commissioner Salvatore Fazzino said the vessel was intercepted only because of its unexpected mechanical failure.



He said: “An engine failure stopped the boat.

“If everything had gone smoothly, we would not have intercepted it.”

Fazzino added that the Coast Guard is believed to have recovered all of the cash.

Investigators have since revealed the boat was being driven by a man of Maltese origin.

The identities of the other three occupants remain unknown.



They are now trying to establish where the money came from and why such a large amount of cash was being transported on the route between Malta and Sicily.

Authorities are examining several possibilities, including money laundering, drug-related payments, currency smuggling and counterfeit banknotes.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Fazzino said: “We need to understand who the person is, where it came from, and reconstruct the movements.”

The four people have since been released pending further investigation and remain on police bail.

News.title: Suffolk fire live: Nuclear plant monitors ‘unprecedented’ wildfire destroying rare bird habitat
News.content:
Fire spans 100 hectares as crews from other areas called in

It is understood the fire now spans 100 hectares. Fire services from as far away as Essex are arriving to help with the emergency effort.

The smell of smoke occasionally fills the air with changing wind, as well as the sound of sirens from passing fire trucks and the whirring of a helicopter passing intermittently overhead.

At Westleton Village Hall, locals are banding together to help others, including holidaymakers, who have been evacuated from holiday lets and caravans near the fire.

Volunteers set up the makeshift rescue centre late on Wednesday night after the scale of the fire became clear.

They are helping evacuees to sort accommodation and giving away free food and drinks, including sandwiches, delivered from supermarket chain Waitrose, to the needy, including babies, families, elderly residents and some in wheelchairs.

Volunteers are also handing out pet food to animals evacuated.

Shortly before midday, they anlso unpacked bedding and pillows from a delivery van before moving them into the main hall.

Among the volunteers is Barry Banks, 52, who has lived in the village full-time for the past five years.

He told the Mirror: "We were made aware by the smell of smoke and sirens. We’re lucky we haven’t had too many fires in the past but it’s always in the back of everyone’s minds.

"By the time we got down here to open up there was already a strong team of volunteers ready to help in any way they could.

"We were fully open and operational for refreshments from about 10pm and then we heard that people were being evacuated from the campsites up until about midnight, 1am.

"We managed to get 47 people housed with the village. Everyone that turned up here was successfully housed.

"It was a mixture of accommodation, but I’d say about 80-90 per cent was people’s houses. It was a great effort. We’re very proud.

"We arrived this morning to cook a full breakfast for everyone that was housed overnight."

Barry added: "From the two updates we’ve had this morning, we understand things are still very fluid as far as the fire is concerned.

"The fire service are trying to slow the spread, but with the wind whipping up and due to change direction shortly, according to the forecast, it’s still a bit of the unknown.

"We understand there were possibly 18 to 20 fire appliances at its peak. It was constant through the night with sirens.

"It was amazing to see the response from everyone, emergency services especially."

News.title: 'Summer holidays quickly turned to horror in scenes from disaster movies as wildfire ravaged Suffolk'
News.content:
The smell of smoke fogs the air as sirens sound from passing fire engines and helicopters hover overhead.

The scene is reminiscent of a disaster movie, but it is all too real to residents and holidaymakers here in the area of Dunwich, rural Suffolk, where around 120 firefighters in 18 engines continue to tackle the 100-hectare blaze.

At least 47 people, including babies, as well as five dogs, a cat and a mouse, were evacuated from lodges and caravans at Cliff House holiday park, near Dunwich Heath, after the fire began at around 5pm on Wednesday night.

They were later taken two miles to a pop-up rescue centre at Westleton Village Hall, where dozens of kind-hearted locals fed and watered them before offering them lodging in their spare rooms.

‌



View 6 Images The scene of devastation as the wildfires spread (Image: SKY)

Among the evacuees was a mum-of-two on holiday from Southampton, who told how she and her family had to quickly evacuate their family-owned static caravan with their two young sons in their pyjamas with such haste they forgot to bring the children’s shoes.

The woman, who did not want to named, said: “It was scary. We just kind of grabbed them and left. They’re still in their pyjamas - no shoes.

"We first saw the smoke at around 7pm while eating our dinner. It very quickly with the change of wind took a very different direction. As soon as we left the caravan, we were straight out into the smoke."

‌



Other evacuees included midwife Jude Bayly, 73, from north London, who slept in her car after evacuating her caravan.

View 6 Images Families have been evacuated from homes and a caravan park (Image: Newsquest / SWNS)

She said: “I’ve never done such chaotic packing in my life. You don’t have any sense of order. I tried to sleep but we could just see the plumes of smoke getting nearer and nearer. You could see the red sky and the flames licking higher and higher. It was really, really scary. It’s so devastating as it’s such a beautiful area."

Rob Gordon, 56, from Spalding, Lincolnshire, was also among those evacuated alongside his wife and dog. The couple had been enjoying their holiday when police warned them they may have to leave.

‌



The delivery driver said: “Unfortunately, I’d had a couple of beers so I couldn’t drive us away. On site, we couldn’t see the smoke that much, but when the police escorted us out, the late evening sun was catching the smoke, which turned it bright red. It was apocalyptic.”

View 6 Images Evacuees were kept safe at a local village hall (Image: Humphrey Nemar/ daily mirror)

Evacuees were tonight being fed and looked after by volunteers at Westleton Village Hall. Among them was Barry Banks, 52, who has lived in the village full-time for the past five years.

He said: “We were fully open and operational for refreshments from about 10pm on Wednesday night and then we heard that people were being evacuated from the campsites up until about midnight, 1am.

‌



“We managed to get 47 people housed with the village. Everyone that turned up here was successfully housed. It was a mixture of accommodation, but I’d say about 80-90% was people’s houses. It was a great effort. We’re very proud.

“We arrived this morning to cook a full breakfast for everyone that was housed overnight.”

The fire has overtaken "a sizeable chunk" of the nearby RSPB Minsmere reserve, but officials last night played down fears it could reach the nearby Sizewell B nuclear power station.

View 6 Images The large heathland blaze on the Suffolk coast still rages (Image: Joe Giddens/PA Wire)

‌



However, they warned the fire is still travelling through forestry and admitted they are facing a challenge to put it out, which they expect could continue for between 24 to 36 hours.

Residents are now being told to keep their windows and doors closed and to stand by in case further evacuations are needed.

Suffolk Fire Service Chief Fire Officer Jon Lacey appeared at the rescue centre, where he spoke to residents and evacuees.

He admitted: "It's a very dynamic and fast-paced incident. I wouldn't say the fire is surrounded and we're on top of it because it moves faster than we're able to deal with it. It's very challenging. The flames are quite high."

‌



View 6 Images Smoke can be seen from miles with a major incident declared (Image: Billy Rogers / SWNS)

"The fire in terms of its size isn't getting significantly bigger, but it's travelling. We have seen it grow a little bit, with the warm conditions and the daylight conditions with the wind and it depends where the wind goes and what is in front of it as to how much bigger it will get."

Mr Lacey admitted it is too early to establish what started the fire and he cannot say when residents and holidaymakers may be able to return to their properties.

He added: "I'm devastated for the people who have had to relocate. I know it's really scary and quite worrying. We're flooding it with resources to do the very best we can for them.

‌



"At this rest centre you can really feel the community spirit and see how everyone is pulling together to help."

News.title: Egypt struck by explosive drones as yet more countries are dragged into Iran war
News.content:
Egypt struck by explosive drones as yet more countries are dragged into Iran war

Energos Winter, a US-owned floating storage and regasification vessel was targeted at the Mediterranean port of Damietta in Egypt sparking a blaze that spread to a neighbouring Greek-owned tanker

View 2 Images The fire that broke out aboard two energy vessels at Damietta Port was due to a drone, Egypt's government said (file photo) (Image: Damietta Port Authority/AFP via Getty Images)

A fire that broke out on two ships at the Mediterranean port of Damietta in Egypt was caused by a drone strike, the country’s government said.

‌



"No party has claimed responsibility," for the attack on the key liquified natural gas (LNG) hub, a statement said today.

‌



Investigations were continuing and authorities would "take the necessary measures to preserve Egypt's interests and national security," it added.

‌



A US-owned floating storage and regasification vessel, Energos Winter, was reportedly hit by a drone. The vessel caught fire with the blaze spreading to a nearby Greek-owned LNG tanker, the GasLog Salem.

Donald Trump drags Egypt into Iran war as US blitzes Tehran military targets READ MORE :

View 2 Images Iranian missiles on display above a banner depicting US President Trump at Azadi Square in Tehran (Image: ABEDIN TAHERKENAREH/EPA/Shutterstock)

Egypt’s oil ministry said no one was injured in the fires.

‌



The Egyptian Cabinet said today in its statement: “After the fire that affected two vessels at Damietta Port on July 29, 2026, was brought under control, preliminary investigations by the relevant authorities found that the incident was caused by a drone.”

Black smoke could be seen rising over the port in videos posted on social media. While there has been no confirmation where the drone came from or who was behind the attack, suspicion has fallen on Iran.

Iran and its allies have carried out similar attacks on tankers in the Gulf and the Red Sea as well as targeting energy infrastructure in neighbouring countries since the start of the war with the US and Israel.

‌



If Iran is behind the attacks this incident would be the first time Egypt has come under attack from the country. Implying that Iran or its proxies were responsible, US President Donald Trump told reporters on Wednesday: "It's a little more of the same. But it's going to be straightening out."

The strike on the US-owned vessel came hours after air strikes were launched by the US and Saudi Arabia on Iran-backed armed groups in Iraq accused of launching drone attacks on Saudi oil facilities.

At least 20 members of the Popular Mobilisation Forces (PMF), Iranian-backed Shia militias, were killed in the strike, the group said.

Article continues below

The killings came as the US carried out what it called a "heavy wave of strikes" over the course of Wednesday night.

News.title: Crete wildfires live: Rethymno in flames amid mass evacuations on Greek islands
News.content:
Flames are tearing across Greek Islands, forcing the evacuation of entire villages on Crete, Paros and Andros as wildfires continue to sweep across Europe

Raging wildfires have taken hold across several Greek islands, forcing villages to be evacuated as firefighters struggle to contain the flames.

Wildfires in the Rethymno region of the south of Crete are burning "out of control on all fronts", with firefighting aircraft unable to be deployed due to strong winds. Thousands of people, including tourists, were evacuated overnight. Urgent evacuation orders have also been issued for parts of Paros and Andros.

Three firefighters have died in Greece, with two becoming trapped in a vehicle while tackling the flames in Rethymno. Meanwhile, Europe's emergency response chief warned that the entire continent could be engulfed as wildfires rage in France, Spain and Portugal.

"Italy will face risk at the beginning of August, and we will need to see what will happen with the Iberian Peninsula, because if [it is] there as well, we will have all Europe on fire," Maria Zuber, head of the EU's Emergency Response Co-ordination Centre, said yesterday.

News.title: Tributes pour in for woman with 'kind soul' found dead in suitcase in Athens
News.content:
Tributes pour in for woman with 'kind soul' found dead in suitcase in Athens

Lisa Jane Ross was found dead inside a suitcase at a derelict building in Athens before police revealed her phone was being used in an attempt to cover up her death

View 5 Images Lisa Jane Ross was found dead at a derelict building in Athens (Image: Facebook)

A Scottish woman whose body was stuffed inside a suitcase and dumped at a derelict building in Greece has been remembered as a "kind soul".

‌



Elisabeth Jane Ross, also known as Lisa, was found by a homeless man in the neighbourhood of Kypseli, Athens, around 1pm on July 18.

‌



Police said texts were sent from the 38-year-old's mobile phone in the days after her death up until she was identified by media.

‌



Lisa's father, from Edinburgh, is believed to have been receiving messages from July 15 to 29 - almost 10 days after she was discovered.

Greek police said there were no visible wounds of any clear signs of struggle on Lisa's body, and that she had been dead for approximately eight days.

Detectives are now trying to establish whether Ms Ross's death was the result of a "criminal act", with a police spokesperson confirming toxicology tests are being carried out.

‌



Chilling last texts sent from phone of Brit woman found dead in suitcase in Athens READ MORE :

View 5 Images Lisa, 38, is believed to have been born in Scotland (Image: Facebook)

The spokesperson said there was no evidence on either the body or the suitcase that would enable them to identify a third party, reports the Daily Record.

Heartbroken friends and family have since paid tribute to Lisa on social media, describing her as having a "beautiful heart."

‌



Pauline Hood wrote: "I am totally devastated. One of the kindest souls I've ever met. Lisa would have done anything for anyone.

"She went that extra mile. She had a beautiful heart. I've got a lot of good memories of Lisa. Thinking of her friends and family at this most difficult time."

Jem Wren said: "Lisa was a lovely girl, I went to school with her. I just can't believe someone could do this to another person. Bless her and her family. RIP."

‌



View 5 Images Loved-ones described Lisa as having a 'beautiful heart' (Image: Facebook)

Anne Morrison added: "I hope they find out who did this! Sending condolences to Lisa's family and friends!"

Ms Ross couldn't initially be identified by police at the scene because she reportedly had no identification on her.

‌



She was described as being around 30 years old, 5ft 4in tall, with reddish hair tied in a bun.

Lisa was wearing a T-shirt and black shorts with a French university insignia on them when she was discovered.

The rough sleeper who found her is understood to have seen a human limb from outside the suitcase after noticing a foul smell at 7 Evelpidon Street - a derelict building which had been unoccupied for two years.

‌



According to local media, Ms Ross had travelled to Greece from Edinburgh on June 29, and initially stayed with friends in the town of Keratsini, in the suburbs of Athens, before meeting American friends in Kypseli on July 15.

View 5 Images Her body was found at a derelict building in Athens (Image: Google Maps)

On July 15, texts were sent to Ross' family claiming that Elizabeth "needed some time to herself". They went on to say that she "wanted to be alone for a while".

‌



A message sent after her death on July 18 to a Greek friend, who she had known "for years" and had been staying with before her body was found, said: "I need some time - I'm going to a Greek island."

The phone remains missing and was active in the Athens area until around 24 hours ago when Elisabeth was formally identified. It's believed that her father, from Edinburgh, had been receiving messages from July 15 to 29.

A Greek officer said: "The phone was being used. Text messages were even sent obviously with a view to making people believe she was still alive. We are treating the building as a crime scene."

‌



An autopsy is due to be carried out in the coming days.

View 5 Images Lisa travelled to Greece on June 29 (Image: cretalive.gr)

Interpol and US investigators have been called in by the Greek authorities to assist with the probe.

‌



Lisa is understood to have travelled to Greece on June 29 via Cyprus after coming from the US.

One local who lives near the scene previously told Greek media outlets the building where Elisabeth's body was found was used by rough sleepers. The resident added that one man stayed there regularly but that he had not been seen for a number of days.

Police Scotland are in contact with authorities in Greece regarding the investigation.

Article continues below

Officers are also providing support to her family in Scotland. No suspect has been identified at this time.

A Police Scotland spokesperson said: "We are aware of the death of Scottish woman in Athens and are liaising with authorities in Greece. Officers are providing support to her family in Scotland."

A UK Foreign Office spokesperson said: "Our thoughts are with Elisabeth's family during this difficult time. We are providing consular support and are in contact with the local authorities."

News.title: Donald Trump drags Egypt into Iran war as US blitzes Tehran military targets
News.content:
Donald Trump drags Egypt into Iran war as US blitzes Tehran military targets

After a pause in fighting in the Middle East, the US has launched large-scale strikes across Iran, blitzing military outposts as Tehran wanrs of retaliatory attacks in the coming days

View 3 Images Donald Trump points as he boards Air Force One (Image: AP Photo/Alex Brandon)

The US military launched wide-scale bombing runs against Iran for the first time in days overnight as the crisis spread wider in the region - dragging in Egypt for the first time.

‌



A fire broke out on a US-owned vessel in an Egyptian port last night after it was struck in a drone attack, marking the first time the country had been hit during the crisis. But Tehran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps warned the US “will be punished today” following its targeting of dozens of Iranian military sites.

‌



The escalation on the port of Damietta happened as Saudi Arabia also carried out joint strikes with the US on Iranian proxies in Iraq, after months of Riyadh resisting the conflict.

‌



America’s response to a previous targeting of one of its bases in Jordan was described as a ‘heavy wave of strikes” in retaliation for Tehran’s assault. Explosions were heard across southern Iran, including embattled Bandar Abbas, Kish and Qeshm Island, according to Iranian state media.

Furious Donald Trump issues Iran a chilling threat with foul-mouthed outburst READ MORE :

View 3 Images Explosions as US launches large-scale strikes on Iran (Image: CENTCOM)

US Central Command said its strikes, which lasted two hours, had struck military command centres, missile and drone facilities, coastal surveillance and defence sites, and maritime capabilities.

‌



It accused Iran of an attack overnight on Tuesday, but insisted that all Iranian missiles were successfully intercepted. Iran said US strikes killed three of its soldiers Thursday as the latest round of attacks threatened to engulf more countries in the region.

Jordan said it intercepted Iranian missiles for a second consecutive day, while Kuwait said a strike there killed one person. Reports from within Iran suggested US forces bombed a building on Iran’s Qeshm Island, killing a couple and their two-year-old child.

Talks with Omani officials are ongoing in Tehran over the Strait of Hormuz, the Iranian Foreign Ministry says. Israeli forces killed at least four Palestinians, including two children, and wounded dozens more in attacks on Gaza.

‌



View 3 Images Pperations enforce the naval blockade against Iran (Image: US Central Command (CENTCOM)/AFP via Getty Images)

In a statement directed to Jordan, Tehran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said its fighters targeted the al-Azraq airbase, which hosts US F-35 fighter jets. It said the attack was in response to the US strike on Qeshm Island, which killed the three family members.

The IRGC also claimed responsibility for an attack on the US Ali al-Salem military base in Kuwait. Earlier, Kuwait said that one worker had been killed in an Iranian attack on a building of a Chinese company in the north of the country.

Article continues below

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) says the US will be "punished today" after America's latest wave of attacks. It had earlier released a statement warning countries helping the US of a harsh response if they "do not correct their behaviour".

The IRGC reaffirmed its claim over the Strait of Hormuz, saying it's "our land" and its sailors have "full control over it". A stranger who has come from thousands of kilometres away will not be allowed to interfere," the corps added. "The Strait of Hormuz cannot be reopened as long as the American authorities' exaggerations and threats and their interference in maritime movements in the region continue."As we reported at 3:27, the US completed a "heavy" wave of strikes on Iran, saying it was in response to Tehran's "attempted missile attacks" on US bases.

News.title: Reckless Porsche driver mounts kerb to pass bin lorry - as bosses warn lives are at risk
News.content:
Reckless Porsche driver mounts kerb to pass bin lorry - as bosses warn lives are at risk

EXCLUSIVE: Waste management company Biffa has warned impatient motorists are putting lives at risk as they reported 1,095 incidents in the last year, with 272 in the last three months

Reckless driver of a £100K Porsche mounts the kerb to pass a bin lorry

This is the moment the driver of a £100,000 Porsche mounts the kerb to pass a bin lorry - as bosses say it is a matter of time before someone is killed.

‌



The footage is among hundreds of shocking incidents across the UK, in which impatient motorists are accused of putting lives at risk by mounting pavements. In one incident, a loader was taken hospital after he broke his leg.

‌



Waste management company Biffa has reported 1,095 incidents in the last year, with 272 in the last three months. And now they're warning that the offence is becoming widespread across the UK - not only putting their workers at risk, but also children and the elderly.

‌



Woman dragged from car and punched in face in Tesco car park gang attack READ MORE :

View 3 Images Shock footage shows the Porsche veer onto the pavement and drive across the grass in a bid to dodge the bin lorry (Image: Biffa)

The worst offenders are in Biffa's west region, which covers the areas from and including Cornwall, South Warwickshire, Anglesey and The Wirral, with 653 incidents in the last 12 months, followed by the south with 214 cases, the Midlands with 88 and Leicester with 42.

The impatient and reckless drivers, which includes cars, vans and delivery couriers on motorcycles, have all been caught on the cameras on the Biffa trucks. The problem is now so widespread that Biffa is working with the police to stamp it out.

‌



And they've plastered some of their trucks with a giant slogan saying: "Watch Out - Driving on pavements is illegal and can kill." A National Police Chiefs' Council spokesperson said: "We all have a personal responsibility for keeping everyone safe on the roads and any behaviour which compromises this is unacceptable.

"Driving without consideration for other road users, whether pedestrians, vehicles or cyclists is incredibly dangerous and impatience can lead to serious consequences."

View 3 Images Waste management company Biffa released the footage in a bid to highlight the dangers facing their employees (Image: Biffa)

‌



Driving on the pavement is a criminal offence and a conviction can lead to significant penalties. Offences of careless or inconsiderate driving - if driving on the pavement to bypass traffic or squeeze through a tight spot - can result in a charge of driving without due care and attention, carrying three to nine penalty points and a fine.

If mounting the pavement puts pedestrians at risk, offenders can be charged with dangerous driving, resulting in an unlimited fine, a driving ban and potentially a prison sentence. Tony Jones, 52, a Biffa driver loader of 12 years from The Wirral, says he witnesses dangerous driving on a daily basis and said recently a loader he works with has been hit by a vehicle, suffering a badly broken leg.

He said: "We get people in vehicles who will try and get round the wagon and will literally drive on the pavement just to get past us. It's impatient people who don't want to wait an extra minute or two for the wagon to move out of the way.

‌



"I've got to look out for my two loaders to make sure they are safe and that they are doing their job and also look out for members of the public, making sure they are not around the wagon.

“We are in one of the most hazardous jobs in the UK, so there's a lot of things I've got to look out for but when a vehicle tries to drive past on the pavement, it is putting everyone at risk, especially children and the elderly."

View 3 Images Biffa worker Tony Jones, 52, says he witnesses dangerous driving on a daily basis (Image: Biffa)

‌



Recalling one incident where a food delivery motorcycle was driving dangerously, Tony said: "There's a road we do that's a one-way with parked cars either side of it - we were driving down the middle of the road and there was a queue of cars behind me, I then see a motorcycle driving across the pavement just feet from front doors and literally anything could have happened. The motorbike delivery guys are the worst.

“We do have schools on our route and there's been quite a few incidents around schools with people driving on pavements, we have kids who, when they see us love to stop and wave at us, and whether they're on the street or outside the front of the house or with the mum and by the cars and obviously, you don't want any incidents happening, especially with the kids."

Tony says Merseyside Police have been very supportive and have taken action against dangerous drivers. he added: "We have had letters from offenders who have written to apologise for their actions once the police have spoken to them so we are thankful for their support.”

Article continues below

Tony said: "Please think twice and I know it can be frustrating to be stuck behind a wagon but don't try to overtake and drive on the pavement as it will cause an accident and we will catch you on the cameras that are on the truck and we will report it to the police."

Gary Carvell, Health & Safety Director at Biffa, said: “Most people would be shocked to see just how often drivers mount pavements to get around bin lorries. What might seem like a quick shortcut can put our crews and members of the public at serious risk.

"Our teams are out there everyday providing an essential service and they deserve to do their jobs safely. By highlighting these incidents, we want to raise awareness of an under reported road safety issue and encourage all drivers to think twice before making a dangerous manoeuvre that could have devastating consequences.”

News.title: UK heatwave to remain until September with fears of more drought and death toll set to be highest on record
News.content:
UK heatwave to remain until September with fears of more drought and death toll set to be highest on record

The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) reported that the number of excess deaths caused by heatwaves so far this year is already more than double the number for the whole of last year

UK weather: Fourth heatwave to bring temperatures of up to 35C

Britain's extreme weather is set to persist throughout August - and is set to lead to the highest number of heat-associated deaths on record this year.

‌



The Met Office says August is likely to be hotter and drier than usual. The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) reported the number of excess deaths caused by heatwaves so far this year is already more than double the number for the whole of last year.

‌



Water minister Emma Hardy said: “Our climate is changing, droughts are becoming increasingly common, and we need to be prepared for this new normal.

‌



“We’re delivering long-term change in the water industry and driving record investments in infrastructure, including nine new reservoirs.

“We expect water companies to follow their drought plans, to go further and faster to reduce leaks, and to ensure supplies are not disrupted even in the driest of weather.”

UK heatwaves warning as nearly 3,000 people dead in just two months of hot weather READ MORE :

UK weather maps show new 34C heatwave within days as 15 counties hit 32C or more READ MORE :

View 7 Images The record temperatures of June saw a steep rise in the number of heat-related deaths (Image: Press Association Images)

‌



Drought declared across whole of Wales

UKHSA's new report estimates there were 2,877 heat-associated deaths during the heatwaves in May and June this year, with an estimated 753 deaths associated with the May heatwave from May 24-27.

Report author Dr Ross Thompson, of UKHSA, said: "While the figures are interim, they suggest that, if we experience more periods of hot weather this summer, we could see the highest number of heat-associated deaths on record."

He added: "These figures highlight the significant danger that very hot weather can pose to people's health. This is particularly true for those who are more vulnerable including older adults and people with underlying medical conditions." The expert said as the climate becomes warmer, Brits can expect periods of hot weather to become longer, more frequent and more extreme, adding it is vital the country is prepared to deal with higher temperatures. Drought has now been declared across the whole of Wales, with this month on course to be the driest July in Wales since records began 190 years ago, Natural Resources Wales said.

‌



View 7 Images Cricket pitches at at Bramcote Hills Park in Nottingham are scorched (Image: Jacob King/PA Wire)

Bleak statistics released

Parts of the UK have this week sweltered through another heatwave which peaked on Wednesday, with temperatures reaching 35.2C in Writtle, Essex. Cooler conditions and some rain are forecast this weekend, but likely not in the driest areas There were another 2,124 deaths in the heatwave between June 21 and 28. Imperial College London, the Met Office, and the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine projected 2,700 excess deaths in a separate report this year.

That report warned that two fifths of those deaths were due to the extra heat caused by climate change.

‌



View 7 Images Parkland near Hornchurch, Essex, ablaze due to the dry conditions

Major incident declared after Suffolk wildfire

The grim prediction came as firefighters tried to contain a large wildfire that broke out on Dunwich Heath in Suffolk.

A major incident has been declared due to the size and complexity of the blaze - now about the size of 140 football pitches - with the RSPB saying it could take 25 years for the heathland to recover

‌



Homes and 200 caravans have been evacuated. Residents were alerted by a 'hammering on the door' and told to evacuate immediately on Wednesday night.

Suffolk Fire and Rescue service said Sizewell B nuclear power station was not at risk from the fire, due to the distance from the fire and the direction it was travelling, but said it was a "live and dynamic situation".

August could be hotter and drier than usual, according to the Met Office, with warmer, drier conditions predicted beyond next month so we may have to wait weeks until for the rain needed to recharge supplies.

‌



View 7 Images Sun worshippers in Devon, which has seen some of the highest temperatures this summer (Image: PA)

Huge concern for vulnerable people

NHS Alliance director Ruth Rankine, said there had been a marked increase in the number of GP appointments in June compared with the previous month and they were up by more than 10% from the same time last year.

She said: "It's possible this could reflect the impact of sustained high temperatures which can increase health risks for vulnerable people and have unfortunately led to a sharp jump in deaths linked to heat.

‌



"Great credit is due to GPs and primary care colleagues for the way they are rising to the exceptional challenges of this summer season. They are doing all they can to help people as quickly as possible."

Health Secretary Yvette Cooper said of the heat-related death toll: "My thoughts are with all those who have lost loved ones as a result of the long and intense heatwaves in recent months.

"And my heartfelt thanks go to the NHS staff, care workers and emergency responders who have worked tirelessly through these exceptionally busy and challenging months to protect and care for people affected by the heat."

‌



View 7 Images Yvette Cooper became Health Secretary last week (Image: Getty Images)

Record-breaking temperatures

Wednesday was the seventh day of 2026, during which temperatures reached 35C or warmer. Before this year, the record was five days in which temperatures were at or above 35C, set in 1976 and matched in 2020.

Record temperatures have become the norm with heatwaves bringing new highs for May and June. Some 23 million customers are under hosepipe bans, and around 1,400 businesses have had to stop abstracting water.

‌



View 7 Images A shoot grows from the dried bed of Howden Reservoir in the Peak District (Image: ADAM VAUGHAN/EPA/Shutterstock)

Dry, hot conditions have hit river flows and wildlife, as well as affecting crops and livestock. The harvest has come early. Cereals are experiencing poorer yields, and livestock farmers are using winter feed due to poor grass growth.

Even those with on-farm reservoirs are likely to run out of supply during August in drought-stricken areas, experts say. Hard-baked earth will cause issues when harvesting crops such as potatoes and carrots.

‌



Farmers are calling for efforts to make agriculture more resilient to climate change, including making it easier to build on-farm reservoirs and flexible abstraction licences so farmers can take and store water when it rains.

View 7 Images A firefighting aircraft releases fire retardant over pine trees in Lanton, France (Image: Getty Images)

Wildfires continue to rage across Europe

In response to the heatwaves and wildfires hitting much of Europe, the UK and Spain have issued a joint statement warning that climate change is "a national security emergency" threatening people's way of life.

Article continues below

Following a meeting between Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband and Spain's foreign minister José Manuel Albares Bueno, the countries put out a joint statement.

They stated thatt addressing the climate crisis was an urgent priority, to tackle the cost of living, protect health and wellbeing, and to ensure European economic and energy security.

They agreed that this summer's wildfires demonstrated that climate change was now a "national security emergency facing Europe and threatening our way of life". The 2,877 excess deaths in the UK this year represents a significant increase on the 1,504 excess deaths observed in summer 2025 Dr Thompson, who is Principal Environmental Public Health Scientist at UKHSA, added that we need to prepare to deal with higher temperatures to protect the most vulnerable in society.

News.title: European nations to boycott World Cup if Fifa goes ahead with investment plan
News.content:
European football's 55 member associations have voted to boycott World Cups if the sport's governing body proceeds with a plan to sell stakes in its competitions to private investors.

The decision was made at an emergency meeting called to discuss the proposal announced earlier this week by Fifa, which oversees world football.

Uefa, which governs European football, had already made its opposition clear by releasing two damning statements - and that strength of feeling has been reaffirmed.

"The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product," it said on Thursday.

"It is one of football's greatest sporting legacies. It has been built over generations by players, national teams and supporters across every continent. No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale."

Uefa's boycott would cover all Fifa competitions, including the men's and women's World Cups and Club World Cup, and be triggered if Fifa president Gianni Infantino's proposals are voted through by member associations.

The first time this stance will be tested at a senior tournament is in October, when the Women's World Cup play-offs are due to be held.

It is understood FA chairwoman Debbie Hewitt and chief executive Mark Bullingham were among those to speak during Uefa's meeting, with the atmosphere described as venomous, such was the strength of feeling against the proposals.

Despite being one of eight Fifa vice-presidents, Hewitt had no knowledge of the discussions that Infantino had been having regarding the proposals.

Concacaf, which governs football in North and Central America and hosted this year's World Cup, also met on Thursday and said its 41 member associations have "rejected" Infantino's proposal.

Sources say the 41 Concacaf nations are losing faith in Infantino.

News.title: Thousands evacuated in Crete as wildfires threaten tourist resorts
News.content:
Thousands of people have been evacuated on the Greek island of Crete as wildfires fanned by strong winds menace tourist resorts and villages.

Two firefighters died on the island on Wednesday when they became trapped while tackling a fire near Krya Vrysi in the Rethymno region. A third firefighter died on the Greek mainland, near the port town of Gytheio in the Peloponnese.

As gusts reached 125km/h (77mph) on the island, around 8,000 people were evacuated from their homes overnight but were later allowed to return.

Greece is among many European countries facing devastating fires and drought.

Several fires have continued to burn in Spain and Portugal, although Spanish Prime Minister Pedro SÃ¡nchez declared an end to the national emergency for wildfires in the Ãvila and Madrid regions.

In south-west France some residents have been able to return to their homes after a major wildfire in the Gironde region.

The fire raging in Crete broke out in the Rethymno region on Wednesday and has since spread rapidly, destroying homes and agricultural land. It remains one of the biggest fires currently active on the island and is still burning out of control.

News.title: Drought declared across whole of Wales as conditions 'deteriorate'
News.content:
Richard Anthony, whose farm stretches over the Vale of Glamorgan and Bridgend county, said the ground on his land was as hard as a "rock" and had "no moisture at all".

The dry land has left Anthony unable to plant his crops, who added he had "never ever been in this situation" before.

"As soon as we've harvested the one crop, we plant in the next crop, but we can't do any of that now," he said. "I've never seen it as bad as this."

Our wheat deals are down between 20% and 30%. That is massive. we'll have to cope, we will survive, but the knock-on effect is huge."

Anthony said he is concerned that once the rain comes it will not stop, leaving him unable to plant next year's crops.

"It'll go from this to being too wet", he added.

National Farmers Union Cymru president Abi Reader has warned that the cost of the continuing dry and hot weather will have a financial impact on farmers.

"We're going to see costs for these farms rising, because they might be having to buy in extra feed for their livestock, or they might be spending a lot of money carting water," she said.

"We've been in this a long time now, and it's going to take a long time to recover, and absolutely everybody needs to remember that food security starts with water security," she added.

News.title: MP Diane Abbott readmitted into Labour Party after suspension
News.content:
MPs Diane Abbott and Joani Reid have been let back into Labour, following suspensions from the party.

In a statement, a Labour spokesperson said both women would also be readmitted into the parliamentary party, meaning they can sit as Labour MPs once again.

News.title: British Airways flight called mayday on approach to Heathrow
News.content:
A British Airways flight issued a "mayday" distress call on its approach to Heathrow Airport earlier this month, according to a statement from France's accident investigation authority.

The call was made on an Airbus A320 flying from Dusseldorf airport in Germany on 6 July following two stall warnings on the aircraft, before it landed without further incident.

The UK's Air Accidents Investigation Branch (AAIB) said it was "investigating a serious incident".

A British Airways spokesperson said the airline was assisting the AAIB with its investigation and was not legally able to comment further at this stage.

The French Air Safety Investigation Authority, the BEA, said that as the plane approached Heathrow, there was a data system failure which triggered a stall warning.

The crew then flew the aircraft in a different mode called "alternate law", which removes some automated flight protection systems. Another stall warning then occurred at 3,000 feet - which experts say was likely to have been just miles away from the airport.

The urgency call the crew had already made was upgraded to mayday, indicating imminent danger.

The BEA website attributed the statement to the AAIB, but the AAIB would not confirm it was from them.

They issued the following statement: "The AAIB is investigating a serious incident involving a commercial aircraft which occurred on 6 July on approach to Heathrow airport."

It said the investigation would be a correspondence investigation, meaning that no team would be sent to carry out field investigations.

Aviation safety investigator David Gleave said there are different forms of mayday calls, and to send an urgency message was "not unusual".

"You could have sick passengers on board who need urgent medical attentionâ¦ so it's up to the captains' discretion as to what they call, but its very unusual for it to be a significant failure on board the aeroplane."

News.title: Man impaled by a hiking pole treks 10 miles down mountain
News.content: David Cifaldi was hiking Montanaâs Granite Peak with friends when he slipped and was impaled by his trekking pole. Remarkably, the pole missed all major organs. Rather than call for a helicopter rescue, Cifaldi hiked 10 miles down the mountain on foot. As a wound care nurse, he immediately shifted into professional mode, assessing and managing his injury throughout the ordeal.

News.title: Burnham says he told Trump UK will be pragmatic about North Sea oil
News.content:
Although the government has not made any announcements on the issue, Trump has praised what he perceives as a change of stance by the UK government.

In a social media post, published the day before Burnham became prime minister,, external Trump wrote: "The People of Aberdeen, in Scotland, are dancing in the streets because the new Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, has stated that he will be opening up, all the way, the invaluable North Sea Oil!"

This week, when asked about his conversation with Burnham, Trump said: "He said he's going to open up North Sea oil.

"If he does that, you're going to be a wealthy country."

He later added: "You buy a lot of your energy, as you know, from the North Sea. You buy from Norway and Norway gets it from the North Sea... Norway's got trillions of dollars in the bank."

"Scotland has a better part of the North Sea."

Asked about Trump's comments, Burnham said: "I indicated in the phone call that we had a week last Monday that I would take a pragmatic approach when it comes to the North Sea, and that is my intention as we go forward from here."

In response, Green Party leader Zack Polanski said: "Our country is burning. Crops are failing. Thousands have been killed by extreme heat.

"Allowing new oil and gas drilling in the North Sea will worsen the climate breakdown putting more lives at risk and doing untold damage to our economy.

"It's not too late for Burnham to do the right thing and commit to leaving dangerous fossil fuels in the ground."

The Conservatives and Reform have urged the government to approve more drilling in the North Sea, arguing it would reduce energy prices.

Last year, Tory Party leader Kemi Badenoch said it would be "absurd" for the UK to leave "vital resources untapped".

Some Labour MPs have expressed unease about more drilling, with Rachael Maskell urging the government to "follow the climate science because we have got a climate emergency".

Simon Francis, from the End Fuel Poverty Coalition, said: "No household struggling with their energy bills will see a penny come off by drilling more from the North Sea.

"Gas is sold at the global market prices, so whatever is pumped out is sold to the highest bidder, not handed to British billpayers at a discount."

Sir Keir's government had already made concessions, allowing "tie-backs" - production in unlicensed areas close to or connected to already licensed areas.

Currently, the debate over North Sea drilling has focused on two oil and gas fields - Rosebank and Jackdaw, located in Scotland.

In 2022 and 2023, regulators approved drilling at the sites, but that was overturned in 2025 following a legal challenge.

The legal process is ongoing, but the government will at some point have to decide whether to permit companies to produce oil in the two areas.

Other oil and gas licences have been approved in recent years but remain largely undeveloped.

If he wanted to encourage more drilling in the North Sea, Burnham could also opt to scrap the Energy Profits Level, also known as the windfall tax.

News.title: Palestine Action ban to be reviewed by Supreme Court
News.content:
The controversial ban under terrorism legislation of the protest group Palestine Action will be reviewed by the Supreme Court.

In a major blow to the Home Office, the court confirmed on Thursday that it had given the group's co-founder permission to appeal the ban which came into effect in July 2025.

While the full details of the reasons for the appeal are yet to be published, the BBC understands they relate to Huda Ammori's argument that the ban breaches human rights.

Officials at the court say the appeal will be expedited - which means it will be heard after the summer break. The eventual outcome of the case could have major implications for terrorism legislation in the UK.

The decision comes weeks after the end of the first major trial of members of the group which had caused more than Â£1m of damage to a defence firm near Bristol with an Israeli parent company. Four members of that break-in team were jailed, with one also sentenced for causing grievous bodily harm on a police officer who was hit with a sledgehammer.

Separately, more than 2,000 people are facing potential trial for protesting against the ban by declaring their support for a proscribed terrorism group in mass demonstrations.

The battle over the banning of Palestine Action has now gone on for more than year.

Former Home Secretary Yvette Cooper banned the group on advice from the police and security officials after an escalating spate of break-ins targeting Elbit, an Israeli-owned defence firm.

The High Court initially ruled that the ban was unlawful - but five judges on the Court of Appeal then overruled it, unanimously deciding the home secretary had acted lawfully and within her powers to proscribe Palestine Action.

That decision by the Court of Appeal will now be reviewed by the Supreme Court.

News.title: Greens review social media operation as Polanski row rumbles on
News.content:
The current row began after Polanski shared a single post on Instagram that contained a carousel of 20 pictures.

The re-post was shared to Polanski's 713,000 followers, because he accepted a request to tag him as a collaborator, which on the platform makes him a "co-author," placing it on his page and into his followers' feeds.

Polanski said he had not noticed the offending image among the others on the post.

According to him, he had accepted collaborator tags for eight other posts from the same event in Bristol alone.

Reform UK leader Farage claimed the t-shirt amounted to incitement to murder and his party reported it to the police.

Neither the Metropolitan Police nor Avon and Somerset Police say the incident meets the threshold for further action.

But the political row has continued with Reform UK MP Robert Jenrick calling Polanski a "nasty piece of work", at a news conference earlier on Thursday.

Inside the Green Party, there has been some criticism of Polanski's behaviour online.

He has attracted positive and negative attention for the rate at which he posts, comments, likes and replies across multiple platforms including X, Bluesky, Facebook and Instagram.

And this is not the first time a quick reaction has attracted controversy; last month he had to apologise to police after posting about their response to the Golders Green attack.

One senior party source said it was clear that due diligence had not been done on Polanski's social media output, and that moving forwards he needs "tight controls" to stay credible, while keeping a similar tone of engagement with his followers.

They pointed out that the speed and number of Polanski's interactions came with a "small upside" but a "colossal downside", and with the latest incident he had "shot himself in the foot at precisely the wrong time".

It comes as recent polling suggests the Green Party has lost ground to Labour, following Andy Burnham's election as Labour leader, and down from a peak earlier this year.

They added their concerns about a wider problem with the party's vetting on social media and of candidates, including around antisemitic posts in recent months.

Several candidates in recent elections have stood down over their social media activity, with two candidates arrested during May's local elections, and another suspended after being elected.

But Green Party peer and former deputy mayor of London Baroness Jones said the criticism of Polanski's Instagram re-post seemed to be "mainly from our opponents, not internal discussions".

She said that her party leader had "made a mistake", adding "we've all done it and got flak."

But she added: "His online presence is what makes him relatable".

Along with relatability, comes popularity: Polanski is the second-most followed UK leader on Instagram after Nigel Farage. The Greens surpassed other parties to become the most popular on the platform this year.

It is also seen as where a good portion of their voters spend time, as they are the most popular party among the under-30s, according to pollsters YouGov.

News.title: Bank holds interest rates but says it is ready to raise them if Iran war escalates
News.content:
The Bank of England has kept interest rates unchanged for the fifth meeting in a row but has indicated it could raise them if the Iran war escalates.

It expects inflation - the rate at which prices rise - to pick up due to volatile oil and gas prices caused by the Middle East conflict, although the peak will be slightly lower than previously thought.

The Bank voted to hold interest rates at 3.75% at its latest meeting.

Bank of England governor Andrew Bailey warned the future of UK interest rates depended on whether the US led war against Iran continues.

While major uncertainties remain because of the war, the Bank predicts the UK economy will grow this year by more than previously forecast.

Bailey told the BBC: "If we get a continuation of this conflict going on and oil prices stay above $100 a barrel... the odds are that interest rates will have to go up higher."

But he also said if a ceasefire, and memorandum of understanding, is established and sticks that would make a difference.

"So it depends on how the events in the Middle East, frankly, unfold. And sadly, we all know this is highly unpredictable," Bailey said.

"What goes on in the Gulf is not, I'm afraid, under our control."

Three members of the Bank's nine-member rate-setting committee voted for a hike, one more than the previous meeting - with that member explicitly citing the collapse of the US-Iran memorandum of understanding for their vote to raise rates.

However, speaking at an earlier news conference, Bailey said the Bank was not currently moving towards raising interest rates.

"Please do not leave this room thinking that the Bank of England is edging towards a hike, because frankly, there's nothing in what I said, and I think any of us have said along those lines," he told reporters.

If the Iran war continues and oil prices hover around $100 a barrel, then a rate rise seems likely. But many in the markets expect tensions to subside in the coming weeks, ahead of crucial elections across the US in the autumn.

News.title: Virgin engineer died after explosion in fuel tank
News.content:
A Virgin Atlantic engineer died of a traumatic brain injury after an explosion as he worked inside a plane fuel tank, an inquest heard.

Aircraft technician Georgie Buxton, 23, was injured during the incident at Heathrow Airport on 11 June and underwent various surgeries to his head and neck. He died at St Mary's Hospital on 7 July.

Senior coroner Lydia Brown opened and suspended an inquest into his death at West London Coroners' Court on Thursday, as she is waiting to see if any criminal charges are brought.

A criminal investigation has been launched by the Metropolitan Police who are working with the Health and Safety Executive. The coroner said she had no details of any potential charges.

Buxton was one of two Virgin Airlines' technicians who were examining a fuel leak on a Boeing 787 900 on 11 June at about 08:45 BST.

A spokesman for Aviation Policing told the court: "Both technicians wore breathing apparatus to protect them from any residual fuel fumes whilst inside the fuel tank."

The spokesman said there was "a non-combustion explosion" while Buxton was inside the fuel tank.

He added: "Georgie Buxton took the impact of that explosion to his head and torso causing him to lose consciousness and suffer catastrophic injury."

A forensic post-mortem examination, carried out at the request of the police, found Buxton had suffered a traumatic brain injury â a craniofacial trauma.

News.title: Four people die after busiest day for small-boat crossings this year
News.content:
Four people died trying to cross the Channel overnight after the busiest day for small-boat crossings so far this year saw 752 arrivals in the UK.

One man died after a vessel capsized off France's northern coast late on Wednesday, local officials said, with a one-year-old child among those hurt.

Seven hours later, three people were found dead aboard a small boat after launching from Dunkirk overnight, some 100km (62 miles) up the coast.

French officials confirmed their deaths as the Home Office reported that Wednesday saw the highest number of crossings in a single day this year, with nine boats reaching the UK.

Local authorities in France said the first boat capsized off the coast at Hardelot around 23:30 local time (21:30 GMT) on Wednesday.

The man is thought to have been in his 30s or 40s, officials added. Six other people including the child sustained minor injuries.

Local officials said the vessel was a "taxi" boat - which cruise along the coast and pick up their paying customers who are waiting in the sea.

Security officials "neutralised" the boat and an investigation into the incident has been launched.

The second boat launched from the Dunkirk area overnight was spotted near a breakwater off the coast at 06:00, the French coastguard said.

Search and rescue officials subsequently found three unconscious people aboard. Their deaths were later confirmed by emergency medical personnel.

A UK government spokesperson said: "Every death in the Channel is a tragedy and a stark reminder of the dangers posed by criminal gangs exploiting vulnerable people for profit."

Prime Minister Andy Burnham, speaking separately about small boat crossings on Thursday, said the UK had made "significant progress" on reducing the number of arrivals.

But, asked by reporters about US President Donald Trump's remark that the UK had a "huge immigration problem", Burnham said there was much still to do "to get those numbers right down".

News.title: Homes flooded and residents evacuated after quarry 'incident'
News.content:
Residents of a village on the outskirts of Cardiff have been evacuated after a flood on Thursday afternoon.

Roads have been shut in Gwaelod-y-Garth, with reports of water up to 5ft (1.5m) deep in some homes.

Emergency services are at the scene and people have been advised to avoid the area.

The Breedon Group confirmed there had been an "incident in its quarry".

"Our teams are working closely with the relevant authorities while engaging with the local community as we respond to the situation," the company said.

News.title: England on track for record heat-related deaths this year, UKHSA estimates
News.content:
England is on track this year for the highest number of heat-related deaths since records began, according to estimates by the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA).

In a preliminary assessment, it said there were an estimated 2,877 heat-related deaths during the May and June heatwaves, almost double the figure for the whole of last year.

An estimated 753 deaths were associated with the 24-27 May heatwave and a further 2,124 with the one from 21-28 June. Definitive figures are expected in early 2027.

Both spells broke Met Office UK monthly temperature records, with 35.1C (95.2F) recorded at Kew Gardens on 26 May and 38.0C recorded at Lingwood, Norfolk on 26 June.

The current record for heat-related deaths was set in 2022, when 2,985 deaths were recorded.

Report author Dr Ross Thompson, from the UKHSA, said "while the figures are interim, they suggest that, if we experience more periods of hot weather this summer, we could see the highest number of heat-associated deaths on record".

Thompson added: "These figures highlight the significant danger that very hot weather can pose to people's health.

"This is particularly true for those who are more vulnerable including older adults and people with underlying medical conditions."

He said "as the climate becomes warmer, we can expect periods of hot weather to become longer, more frequent and more extreme", adding that it is vital the country is prepared to deal with higher temperatures.

Earlier this week parts of the UK sweltered through another heatwave that peaked on Wednesday, with temperature reaching 35.2C in Writtle, Essex.

Cooler conditions and some rain are on the way for some on Thursday and into the weekend, but likely not in the driest areas.

News.title: Missing child, 5, dies after being found in water
News.content:
A missing five-year-old child has died after being found in a body of water.

West Mercia Police said officers had responded to reports of a missing child in Badsey, Worcestershire, on Wednesday evening.

The child was found unresponsive in the water and a short time later was pronounced dead.

The force said they were believed to have drowned and called it "an incredibly tragic incident", adding there was no third-party involvement in the death.

Officers said they would not be identifying the child's sex out of respect for the family.

West Midlands Ambulance Service said they were called at 18:50 BST, sending an ambulance, two paramedic officers and the Midlands Air Ambulance Critical Care Car to the scene.

A spokesperson said: "On arrival we discovered one patient, a young child.

"Ambulance staff and police worked quickly to treat the patient, but sadly, it became apparent nothing could be done to save them and they were confirmed dead at the scene."

News.title: Suspected Kinahan gang leader faces extradition
News.content:
Suspected crime boss Daniel Kinahan is to be extradited back to Ireland, BBC News NI understands.

He was arrested in Dubai under a warrant issued by the Irish courts in April but has fought attempts to extradite him.

However, his appeals have been unsuccessful and he is due to be flown back to Ireland within weeks.

GardaÃ­ (Irish police) now expect authorities in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) to sign his extradition which will formally commence the extradition process.

GardaÃ­ expect this will take place very quickly.

Bringing the suspected gang leader back to Ireland will now be the subject of a major security operation between the gardaÃ­ and the Irish Defence Forces.

The US government imposed sanctions on him in April 2022 after he and other members of his family were identified as leaders of the Kinahan organised crime cartel.

Kinahan also had ties to the world of sport via his now defunct boxing management company MTK Global, which represented more than 100 boxers including Tyson Fury and Carl Frampton.

However, Kinahan is now expected to face the Irish courts in the coming weeks and has previously been named as the head of the drug cartel.

The Irish authorities are expected to prosecute him for his involvement in leading an organised crime group.

An extradition agreement is in place between the UAE and Ireland and it was used to extradite Sean McGovern, a "senior lieutenant" in the organised crime group.

He was sentenced to 24 years in prison last month for directing the activities of a criminal organisation.

News.content:
