While there is cautious optimism that a deal can now finally be agreed, it is not a guarantee that the EFL will accept the Premier League’s offer, with sources suggesting it sees the proposal as being very similar to one that was mooted in 2023 but ultimately never approved by Premier League clubs. Both sides say they remain committed to ongoing dialogue.

Sports.title: Fifa’s sales pitch revealed: more tournaments, more debt … but no mention of women’s game
Sports.content:
Fifa’s sales pitch to persuade members to approve the sale of the World Cup’s commercial rights clearly states that its plans for financial growth will be achieved by staging more tournaments, having higher ticket prices and debt financing.

A 25-page sales deck titled “Fifa Forward Enterprise Member Materials”, that has been seen by the Guardian, makes the case for the creation of a new company to run Fifa’s commercial operations, 20% of which would be sold to Joshua Kushner, a US investor who is the brother of Donald Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner.

The prospectus has been produced by JP Morgan, the US bank that was also behind the failed European Super League breakaway five years ago.

In addition to the previously reported $20m (£15m) sign-up payment Fifa has offered to all 211 member associations, which could be made available as soon as January, the document projects that the four-year Fifa Forward payments would increase to $24m for each member by the 2035-39 cycle.

JP Morgan makes clear in the sales deck that such growth will come from “a growing tournament portfolio”, “third party sources of capital and debt financing”, and prioritising “high yield” partnerships and events.

There is also a reference to more than doubling the number of global tournaments held each year, from 200 to 450, which if followed through would put a huge strain on player workload.

Staging the World Cup more frequently would be the most obvious way of raising revenue, with Gianni Infantino having previously proposed making it a biennial tournament five years ago.

The bank also raises the prospect of TV coverage of the biggest events such as the World Cup being sold to subscription channels or streamers, by referring to a lan to “expand and optimize media rights monetization”.

JP Morgan claims that Fifa is “undermonetized” but significantly makes comparisons with other sports leagues with the revenue figures based on club or franchise earnings, rather than with comparable governing bodies.

Fifa’s stated annual revenue of $3.6bn therefore compares unfavourably with the NFL’s compared revenue of $21.2bn, Major League Baseball’s $13.1bn and the NBA’s $12.5bn.

The document was sent to all 211 member associations on Wednesday night and immediately provoked a strong reaction.

One senior figure queried why Fifa, which has cash reserves of around $4bn and accumulated revenues of $15bn over the current four-year cycle, would need to take on debt.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Another highlighted the odd comparison of a world governing body with private, member-run leagues, while JP Morgan’s proposed timeline for completing the deal was also questioned.

According to the document “Investors will be given access to a term sheet and select materials” in August before a vote of Fifa members has taken place.

Significantly there is little mention of the investor group elsewhere in the prospectus, with no reference to its identity, projected returns or exit terms.

There is one more major omission in the document, as there is not a single mention of women’s football anywhere across the 25 pages.

Fifa was approached for comment.

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership returns with McInnes adding new twist to Old Firm rivalry
Sports.content:
Only residents of cloud cuckoo land can hold the firm belief that Scottish football will emerge promptly from a summer of discontent. The onset of a new domestic season, ordinarily a cause for excitement, instead gives reason to ponder the grim realities of what came before.

That it is unsurprising there has been no detailed explanation or plan from the Scottish Football Association following a lamentable World Cup does not prevent the scenario from being so deflating.

Mike Mulraney, the president, was last seen peeking out from the crowd behind Gianni Infantino and the US president at Trump Tower. Ian Maxwell, the Scottish FA’s chief executive, bemoaned “hysterical commentary” around his country’s World Cup performance during a brief media appearance after Steve Clarke had resigned. These executives had all but spurted with laughter when it was suggested handing Clarke a four-year contract immediately before Scotland set sail for the United States was perhaps a needless dalliance with risk.

Perhaps Mulraney and Maxwell are too engrossed in the sourcing of Clarke’s replacement to speak out on the overall state of the national sport. It is only fair to give them the opportunity to appoint a coach who can oversee much-needed transition in a geriatric Scotland squad.

The nation’s leading clubs have been moot on a big picture they wilfully ignore but that was exposed at a World Cup. The problem is that lingering and legitimate anger over Scotland’s showing on the biggest stage – despite all rationale behind it – mirrors so much broader sentiment as the Premiership returns. This has scope to be a troublesome, toxic campaign.

Celtic’s supporters remain irate at the custodians of their club, whom they perceive as complacent and out of touch. In Derek McInnes, Rangers have a new manager who is deeply unpopular on the other side of the city. Nobody should underestimate the lingering resentment that exists among followers of Hearts over the way the campaign of 2025-26 concluded.

The most reprehensible element of that arrived on 11 June, when the Scottish Professional Football League published the outcome of a disciplinary process into the pitch invasion that forced the ending of Celtic’s title-clinching clash against the Edinburgh club.

View image in fullscreen Celtic fans run on to the pitch after their team went 3-1 up against Hearts in the title-deciding game. Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PA

Snuggled in alongside wrist tickles for Hamilton Academical, Inverness and Stenhousemuir was a meagre fine for Celtic and a suspended, paltry ticket reduction. Rangers fans, who need little encouragement to rail against officialdom, were subdued until McInnes was slapped with a touchline ban for comments made against a refereeing decision.

Rangers have criticised elements of an independent report into the chaos which followed their March Scottish Cup loss to Celtic. Motherwell are speaking with lawyers due to objection to a Scottish FA fine for a video posted on social media.

A 2-0 European qualifying first-leg defeat in Kosovo last week was rightly sufficient to send Hibs fanatics into the internet’s version of orbit. Such results stopped being a shock long ago.

Certain clubs do actually have reasons to be cheerful. Celtic’s signing of Kasper Høgh for a club record fee not only demonstrated the kind of fiscal muscle-flexing that supporters wish happened more often but provided the most intriguing transfer arrival of the close season. Scepticism exists over the ability of players to perform outside the perennially successful environment of Bodø/Glimt.

Without such doubts and at a fee which even many Championship clubs would think little of, Høgh would have moved long ago. The 25-year-old, though, has a physical profile and direct style that should succeed in Scotland.

Celtic’s challenge is to replace existing first-team performers – Arne Engels and Alistair Johnston the prime examples – should irresistible bids arrive without posting the kind of net profit that makes balance sheets look more important than trophies. Fans have rightly welcomed the Høgh signing but need more.

Rangers, in contrast to their oldest foes, have burned through extraordinary amounts of cash in recent years while generally watching others lift trophies. This has fuelled rage in and reputational damage from the stands, which an American ownership has curiously opted not to challenge.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

In McInnes, Rangers – who kick off the season at Dundee United on Friday – have a manager whose knowledge of club and culture looks better placed than most before him in recent years to lay gloves on Celtic. Vanja Dragojevic looks a smart midfield signing from Partizan Belgrade. Rangers need attacking spark yet it should be no surprise that McInnes’s first act was to implement a stronger core. He lacks nothing in motivation or work ethic in the job he has always craved. This version of Rangers should be much improved. Yet on the simple basis of course and distance specialism, Celtic remain the title favourites.

View image in fullscreen Motherwell’s recent success offers a template for other top-flight clubs to follow. Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PA

Nobody linked to Hearts should have been expected by now to fully process the circumstances in which they came within minutes of a first title win in 66 years, only for that dream to be snatched away. McInnes’s departure for Rangers, the completely new style implemented by Wouter Vrancken and a palpable raising of expectations all contribute to a period of upheaval.

Hearts’ tilt at glory came earlier than anyone could anticipate. The club remains on the minds of people who previously had no interest in the Scottish game. A comprehensive Champions League qualifying defeat by Sturm Graz showed the scale of work Vrancken has ahead of him. Patience, however, would be wise.

Motherwell’s work with and post the management of Jens Berthel Askou proved those below the Premiership’s biggest fish needn’t only cling on for dear life. The football was superb, the attendance figures boosted and a broader market was impressed. Motherwell’s sales of Elijah Just and Elliot Watt for multimillion pound fees completely justify a club model that thinks outside the box.

St Mirren have clear aspirations of introducing more young players and a more alluring brand of football. Kilmarnock displayed that at the end of last season under Neil McCann. Aberdeen will surely be a stronger force this time under Stephen Robinson.

Only one artificial pitch remains in Scotland’s top flight, which provides cause for celebration.

Football remains a Scottish obsession. It is also undeniably a sick patient. The dawning of a fresh season should appeal only if there is a glimpse of fresh thinking.

Sports.title: Why Eddie Howe could NOT carry on: CRAIG HOPE reveals the moment in Greece when Newcastle boss was 'all in' before midsummer U-turn, Joelinton's wish to leave, World Cup medical that did not happen and coup that shattered Saudi illusion
Sports.content:
Why Eddie Howe could NOT carry on: CRAIG HOPE reveals the moment in Greece when Newcastle boss was 'all in' before midsummer U-turn, Joelinton's wish to leave, World Cup medical that did not happen and coup that shattered Saudi illusion

Unlock more from Craig Hope inside the Newcastle camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

It was during a family holiday in Greece in the final week of May that Eddie Howe decided, after much contemplation, that he was ‘all in’ on the season ahead with Newcastle United.

His future in the days and weeks before was uncertain. Not because he was about to be sacked. He had been given assurances by the Saudi-led owners of their commitment to him in late April.

He, in turn, had searched for every reason to reaffirm his own commitment. He wanted to stay. He wanted to believe that all inside the club were aligned. He wanted to feel re-energised after the most draining 12 months of his managerial career. His relationship with those at the top has always been and remains good, but he also had to be on good terms with himself.

There were days when he was in. There were days when he was out. After a 2-1 home defeat by Bournemouth in April, he felt in, despite a growing expectation he could go. ‘F*** them, I want this job,' was his resolve in the days after.

But then, following the final game of the season, a lame 2-0 defeat at Fulham, he felt out. So bad was the performance, he wondered whether this really was the end. Did the team need a new voice?

Eddie Howe has left Newcastle United after four-and-a-half years in charge

He guided the club from 19th in the Premier League to their first major domestic trophy in 70 years, as well as two seasons in the Champions League

Howe flew to Greece hours later and knew, if he was to be fair to Newcastle, that he had to make a decision while there.

Finally free of a season that began amid the stifling humidity of the Far East and the trauma of Alexander Isak’s protracted sale, and grew ever more suffocating as the team inevitably suffered and finished 12th in the Premier League, Howe was able to clear his mind.

The picture suddenly became less complicated. He loved Newcastle. His desire to get the team back on track was stronger than the doubt that this could all veer off course. His focus was on recruitment and a summer rebuild. Leaving Greece, there was optimism.

By the time he sat in the Miami Stadium and watched Bruno Guimaraes play for Brazil in the World Cup against Scotland on June 24, that renewed enthusiasm was being tested. A few days earlier, Newcastle had missed out on the signing of Spain winger Victor Munoz.

With club staff in place in Dallas to complete the player’s medical, Liverpool hijacked the deal at the 11th hour. It was a dark hour for the club. Losing their top target to replace Anthony Gordon cast an unwanted shadow over the summer in front of them, and that only lengthened when Switzerland midfielder Johan Manzambi then chose Aston Villa over the Magpies. Was it happening again?

A year on from the transfer window that will forever rank as a disasterclass in football-club ownership, when No 1 targets such as Hugo Ekitike and Joao Pedro and several others rejected moves to an organisation without a sporting director or chief executive, there was a fear that Newcastle’s reputation and processes had not recovered to the level needed to succeed. To be fair to new executive arrivals, this felt as much a legacy issue.

Bruno Guimaraes could be the next high-profile star to leave, with Arsenal ready to pounce

Newcastle have seen a host of major departures this summer, including Sandro Tonali to Tottenham for an initial £92.5m

Anthony Gordon joined Barcelona for £70m earlier in the window

In the background, Guimaraes was making moves to find a new club, as revealed by Daily Mail Sport the day after Howe had seen him play in Florida.

To lose his captain - the team's driving force on the pitch and emotional leader off it - would have been close to unthinkable. Guimaraes will join Arsenal if they make a formal offer above the £75million mooted by intermediaries and his departure, we are told, is more likely than not.

We can also reveal that his compatriot Joelinton told Newcastle of his wish to move to Saudi Arabia in the weeks after the season closed. That offer is yet to materialise. Gordon had gone to Barcelona and Sandro Tonali was in the process of moving to Tottenham.

To Howe, each of these was a blow. The team he cherished was being dismantled, in part out of necessity because of Premier League and UEFA spending restrictions, but also because these players had doubts as to the speed, direction and delivery of the club’s ‘Vision 2030’ project, a stated ambition to be among the best in the world. Blurred Vision 2030 feels more appropriate right now.

Incoming, meanwhile, were four players of high potential - three 20-year-olds and an 18-year-old - but with a low guarantee of impacting this season. Howe supported each signing and understood the need for a shift in transfer policy.

But there was enough evidence from last season to realise that supporters, especially online, might not be so understanding if results suffered.

For all of that, transfers are not the reason Howe has decided to stand down. In fact, there is no one reason. There has been no fallout. He leaves on good terms with sporting director Ross Wilson, chief executive David Hopkinson and all others. This is not a knee-jerk reaction to any one incident.

The frontrunner to replace Howe is Al Ahli boss Matthias Jaissle, who won the Asian Champions League twice with his current club and previously managed Red Bull Salzburg

This, you suspect, has been building for the best part of two years. In that time there has been the internal coup to oust his allies Amanda Staveley and Mehrdad Ghodoussi, the destabilising appointment of sporting director Paul Mitchell and delays to key off-field developments which have harmed the optics around the club.

This, more than anything, is a sad tale of mismanagement at ownership level. There is the mitigation of Profit and Sustainability Rules, but they do not limit care, engagement and infrastructural investment.

The owners won the lottery when appointing Howe as their first manager in November 2021, and have since proceeded to tear up the ticket. They left Howe to fight fire after fire until their head coach was burnt out.

On the eve of returning to pre-season training on July 13, the 48-year-old told Wilson that he felt the time was right for him to take a break. It was best for the squad if a new manager arrived with fresh energy and ideas.

The club disagreed and wanted Howe to lead the team this season. The timing was also far from ideal. Available managers had come and gone and, within a few days, someone had to take training. Howe agreed to stay on until his replacement was found. The players were not informed.

Kieran McKenna (second right), whose Premier League relegation with Ipswich Town was confirmed at St James' Park last year, was spoken about as a potential Howe replacement

Meanwhile, a very small number of candidates were considered and Matthias Jaissle, of Al Ahli, agreed to take charge. Kieran McKenna was spoken about, but he is taking a career break. Jaissle’s contract is currently with lawyers and the 38-year-old will join the squad in La Manga in the coming days. Howe would have travelled to Spain had news not broken of his impeding exit.

Now, there will be sadness. There will be fatigue. In recent days, weeks and months, a couple of analogies have been put to me to describe Howe’s predicament. One, like a boxer who should have admitted his fight was done but kept on swinging. The other, like a man pushing back against the rock that has been trying to crush him and the club. The second of those feels most pertinent but fails to capture the stones that were falling from within.

To understand why Howe has decided to stop now, we must first rewind.

An illusion. That is the word we have used for two years. The job Howe did in taking Newcastle from 19th in the Premier League, twice into the Champions League and delivering a first domestic trophy in 70 years was always at odds with reality. The reality, rather, was that Howe, his staff and his players were over-performing (they had the eighth-highest wage bill in the Premier League last season).

Recruitment - from Isak to Guimaraes to Gordon and Kieran Trippier - was exceptional. The football operation was the head of the club, while the tail - the business operation - was lagging behind. No new training ground. No new stadium or St James’ Park upgrade. Sponsorship and commercial deals that were improved but still not up to speed with the head-start Howe had given them. Broken promises to players. Broken relationships.

Mehrdad Ghodoussi (left) and Amanda Staveley (right) were the glue that kept the club together. Crucially, they recognised the value of Howe and stuck to him more than anyone

When I wrote in August 2024, ‘This is all starting to feel a bit Mike Ashley’, it was met with astonishment, on Tyneside and especially beyond. This came in the months after the Machiavellian plot to get rid of Staveley and Ghodoussi, led by non-football senior staff who argued that the minority owners cut across too much of their own responsibilities.

This was true, but it was also true that Staveley and Ghodoussi did a better job than those they were cutting across. They were the glue that kept the club together. Crucially, they recognised the value of Howe and stuck to him more than anyone.

Mitchell arrived within weeks and, on the part of the club, it felt like an act of vandalism. With an alarming absence of humility, he told players and staff on his first day that he was elite and they should go on a journey with him.

It left them feeling abandoned by the club at the parachuting in of this abrasive outsider. It then caused mayhem when he told some players they weren’t wanted and they believed that instruction had come from Howe, which they later discovered it had not. The tumult led to Isak - and more - wanting to go. Howe, somehow, managed to keep his squad together, and he did that alone minus Staveley and Ghodoussi.

Forget that the couple stood on the toes of others, when the Saudis listened to the plotters, they as good as blew their own feet off. For all the good PIF had done in the first two-and-a-half years of their ownership, this was a bad error of judgement at a pivotal moment.

Howe's exit adds to a turbulent summer and pre-season, with Newcastle losing 4-1 to Bristol City on Wednesday

Paul Mitchell (right) arrived as sporting director within weeks of Staveley and Ghodoussi's exit and, on the part of the club, it felt like an act of vandalism

The day they went marked day one in the unravelling of the illusion. This was not really a well-run super club destined for the top. It was a magic carpet given flight by Howe, its supporters and the power of Newcastle Re-United.

Still, they had enough elevation to win the Carabao Cup in 2025 and, even last season, there was a return to the semi-final of that competition and a Champions League last 16. Today, though, that carpet is well and truly grounded. The mirage, the magic, it has all been exposed by Howe deciding he could not go on. To repeat, he did not want to feel like this.

Yes, there is the lingering impact of the pneumonia that hospitalised him in the weeks after the Carabao Cup win. He came back too soon and is still learning how best to manage his workload.

But even allowing for that, he was ready for this season when he left Greece in early June and later headed to the United States with his family. Influenced by his heart, he made his mind believe that it could work. In the end, he had to be true to himself and true to the club.

The truth is, he has made the right decision. The truth is, the club are infinitely worse off for that. The truth is, the reality of Newcastle United has long since been something of a lie.

Sports.title: England and fellow UEFA nations set to unanimously BOYCOTT World Cup after FIFA's plans to sell shares to private investors
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

England and other UEFA nations have unanimously decided to boycott FIFA competitions amid Gianni Infantino's plans to sell shares in the World Cup.

UEFA held crisis talks virtually on Thursday after proposals to generate £3.1billion in private investment for FIFA tournaments, most notably the World Cup, faced widespread opposition.

Member associations were described to Daily Mail Sport as 'outraged' with more than 40 federations providing testimony, as UEFA coordinated their response to FIFA's proposals.

Daily Mail Sport also understands there was 'total unanimity' on the call with associations fuming that FIFA had left them in the dark - unilaterally developing plans to transform football governance.

One international football insider told Daily Mail Sport: 'This is at the nuclear button end of the spectrum, which is impressive'.

In a statement, cosigned by all 55 UEFA members, European football's governing body said: 'UEFA and its national associations will not participate in FIFA competitions.

'UEFA and its 55 member associations stand as one. We unanimously and unequivocally reject FIFA's proposal to transfer ownership interests in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions to private investors.

'The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product. It is one of football's greatest sporting legacies. It has been built over generations by players, national teams and supporters across every continent. No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale.

'It is both irresponsible and indefensible that a proposal of such significance for football was conceived in secret and brought to the brink of approval without any meaningful consultation with those entrusted with stewarding the game. This is not merely a profound failure of leadership, but an abdication of FIFA's duty as the custodian of world football.

'National associations around the world are now presented with an ultimatum: accept the irreversible capture of football's greatest competitions or bear the consequences. This is not a 'democratic decision', but governance by intimidation – an act of coercion unworthy of an institution entrusted with the stewardship of the global game.

UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin has condemned FIFA's plans to allow private investors a share of the World Cup

'But our opposition goes far beyond process,' the UEFA statement continued.

'The moment external investors acquire ownership interests in FIFA competitions, football changes forever. Commercial return becomes a permanent obligation. Investor expectations become a daily pressure. From that moment onwards, every decision on the international calendar, every decision on competition formats and every decision shaping the future of football is no longer driven by what best serves the game, but by what best serves shareholders.

'This model has no place in world football. Football's future cannot be dictated by the expectations of those whose first duty is to maximise financial return. Nor can the interests of national associations, leagues, clubs, players and supporters become subordinate to investor returns. Football cannot mortgage its future for financial gain.

'Europe's position is clear. We will never lend this model our legitimacy. No one has the moral authority to sell what they merely hold in trust for the next generation.

'As a result of today's discussion, no UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership.

'Nobody should be in any doubt: UEFA and its national associations will oppose these plans with absolute determination.

'There are moments when institutions are judged not by what they are prepared to accept, but by what they refuse to compromise. This is one of those moments.

'Some things are simply too important to sell. The FIFA World Cup belongs to football. It always will. And so long as Europe has a voice, it will never be for sale.'

An FA spokeswoman added: 'We stand shoulder to shoulder with our European colleagues and fully support the collective view. We oppose FIFA's plans - the FIFA World Cup belongs to football and always will.'

UEFA's decision to boycott tournaments could force FIFA to abandon its plans, just as they did when the continental confederation used the same tactic to compel FIFA to scrap a 2021 proposal to turn the World Cup into a biennial tournament.

Gianni Infantino has been widely criticised for his decision to put the World Cup 'up for sale'

Football Association chief executive Mark Bullingham came under pressure to take action

Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy said: 'This is a principled decision that we strongly support. Football belongs to the fans, not billionaire investors. Enough is enough. It's time to take a stand to protect our game.'

Reform UK Leader Nigel Farage was among the political class to support UEFA.

'Football is for the people,' Farage posted on X. 'UEFA are right to take a stand and Gianni Infantino must resign.'

FIFA are hoping to raise £3.1bn of private investment in a new company responsible for the commercial and operational aspects of tournaments.

Investment bank J.P. Morgan is FIFA's financial advisor on the project while Joshua Kushner's Thrive Capital is expected to lead the proposed investor group. Kushner is the brother of Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared.

Infantino tried to force FIFA's associations to decide on the proposal by September 19, while explaining the financial benefits in a letter to all 211 FIFA members.

UEFA, however, accused FIFA of trying to bribe associations into agreeing with the proposals, which could see them receive up to an additional £15million in revenue.

In another blow to the plan, the president of the Asian Federation Sheikh Salman wrote of his 'great concern and disappointment' in FIFA's decision to prepare the plans without consultation.

CONCACAF, which represents 41 countries in North and Central America and the Caribbean, is another federation to express early scepticism in the wake of the bombshell plans and are set to meet at 5.30pm.

The effects of the boycott could be seen in as little as 37 days, with the women's Under 20 World Cup set to kick off in Poland. The tournament features six European teams, including England.

Meanwhile, the UEFA play-offs for the Women's World Cup are scheduled for October, with England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales all in action.

Sports.title: Eddie Howe to LEAVE role as Newcastle boss in bombshell news as turbulent summer at St James' Park continues - with his replacement already lined up
Sports.content:
Newcastle United boss Eddie Howe has stood down after five years in charge and will be replaced by German coach Matthias Jaissle.

The 48-year-old has been contemplating his future in recent months and has now come to an agreement to end his St James' Park tenure with immediate effect. He took time at the end of last season to consider the best way forward for him and the club but decided to carry on.

However, Howe informed the hierarchy of his belief that the time was right to part ways earlier this month. There has been no falling out and he agreed to remain until a replacement was found.

Jaissle, currently in charge of Saudi club Al Ahli, is now set to join up with the Newcastle squad when they travel to La Manga for a pre-season training camp this weekend.

His contract was with lawyers last night and, barring any late hitches, he will become the second appointment of the club’s Saudi-led ownership. The 38-year-old was previously in charge of Red Bull Salzburg between 2021 and 2023 and has since managed PIF-owned Al Ahli, where he won the Asian Champions League in 2025 and 2026.

Eddie Howe is set to leave his role as Newcastle United manager in bombshell news

Howe led Newcastle to their first major trophy in 70 years in 2025 and also took them to the Champions League on two occasions

The timing of Howe’s departure has rocked Tyneside, even though it has not come as a surprise on the back of a turbulent 12 months.

After losing star striker Alexander Isak last September, England winger Anthony Gordon and Italy midfielder Sandro Tonali have been sold to Barcelona and Tottenham respectively this summer.

Captain Bruno Guimaraes wants to join Arsenal and, should the Premier League champions present an acceptable offer north of the £75million mooted by agents, the expectation is the Brazilian will leave.

Joelinton told club chiefs at the end of the season he wanted to move to Saudi but no offer has materialised.

Newcastle have bought four players this window but all are aged 20 or under and, while transfers are not the sole reason for Howe’s exit, the likelihood of a testing season with diminishing supporter patience is thought to have been a factor.

They have opened pre-season with a 1-1 draw against non-League Gateshead and a 4-1 defeat by Championship side Bristol City on Wednesday night.

Howe said after that match that the focus was the opening game of the season against Liverpool, but the wheels were already in motion for his departure. A club statement will follow confirming the end of his hugely successful period in charge.

His exit continues a turbulent summer at Newcastle after the exits of Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali

Al-Ahli boss Matthias Jaissle is an early contender to replace Howe at St James' Park

The former Bournemouth boss arrived in November 2021 with the team 19th in the Premier League on the back of the Saudi takeover the previous month.

After leading them to survival, Newcastle qualified for the Champions League the following season and were beaten in the final of the Carabao Cup.

In 2025, Howe became the first manager in 70 years to win a domestic trophy for the Magpies when they beat Liverpool in the Carabao Cup final at Wembley. They also qualified for the Champions League for a second time.

However, last season was a struggle and, despite making the last 16 of the Champions League and the semi-final of the Carabao Cup, a 12th-placed finish was reflective of the drop-off in performance.

Howe met with the club’s owners during a summit at Matfen Hall in April and the intention was to remain going into this season. But after careful thought in recent weeks, he will now take a break from football.

Sports.title: Senne Lammens cuts short his holiday after World Cup to rejoin Manchester United training - as new signing Youri Tielemans arrives at Carrington
Sports.content:
Senne Lammens cuts short his holiday after World Cup to rejoin Manchester United training - as new signing Youri Tielemans arrives at Carrington

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Senne Lammens cut short his holiday to return early to pre-season training with Manchester United ahead of the new campaign.

The goalkeeper had been due to report back to Carrington next Monday following his participation in the World Cup with Belgium, according to ESPN.

Lammens had been part of the Belgium squad that reached the quarter-finals, before falling to a 2-1 defeat by eventual winners Spain.

The 24-year-old had been Belgium's second choice goalkeeper behind established No1 Thibaut Courtois.

Lammens was called into action in the quarter-final after Courtois sustained an injury, with the Real Madrid shot stopper forced to be substituted.

Lammens was ultimately at fault for Spain's winning goal, with the goalkeeper spilling a shot from distance into the path of Mikel Merino, who scored on the rebound to send Spain into the last four.

Senne Lammens cut short his post World Cup holiday to join Man United's pre-season training

Lammens was expected to report back next week after his World Cup involvement with Belgium

New signing Youri Tielemans was also pictured at Carrington after joining from Aston Villa

Lammens was pictured arriving at Carrington on Thursday, four days before he was due to report back to Man United.

The goalkeeper arrived alongside his international team-mate Youri Tielemans, who signed for Man United from Aston Villa in a £35million move earlier this month.

ESPN reported that Lammens has been keen to get back to club football following the World Cup.

Lammens had enjoyed a superb debut season at Man United after signing from Royal Antwerp in an £18.2m move last September.

After joining in a deadline day move, Lammens made his Man United debut in October in a 2-0 win over Sunderland.

Lammens remained an ever present in goal for the remainder of the season, with the goalkeeper playing a key role in helping the Red Devils qualify for the Champions League.

He was voted as the Premier League's transfer of the season in May following an online poll of fans.

Lammens made his international debut for Belgium last November, with his impressive form for Man United contributing to him being named in their World Cup squad.

Man United are next in pre-season action on Saturday when Michael Carrick's side face Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

Sports.title: Fulham bag £8.5m bargain from Real Madrid, Brentford close in on £41m deal for Mamadou Sangare - and Man City's talks over Ayyoub Bouaddi reach crucial stage: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Fulham bag £8.5m bargain from Real Madrid, Brentford close in on £41m deal for Mamadou Sangare - and Man City's talks over Ayyoub Bouaddi reach crucial stage: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

From Benfica to Bournemouth for £21.6m

Benfica defender Antonio Silva is expected to complete his move to Bournemouth following tonight's Europa League qualifier against St Gallen.

The 22-year-old starts for Marco Silva's side against the Swiss tonight but is then due to link up with his new teammates at Bournemouth in a £21.6million move.

Newcastle close in on Hornicek

Newcastle United are pressing ahead with their move for Sporting Braga goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek.

Daily Mail Sport revealed Newcastle's interest last weekend and he was left out of Braga's Europa Conference League squad for tonight's clash with Zeleznicar Pancevo amid talks.

Confirmation of the Czech keeper's departure for his £25m release clause is expected tomorrow once their game is out of the way.

Brentford set for £41m Sangare deal

Brentford have agreed a £41million deal to sign Lens midfielder Mamadou Sangare.

The 24-year-old is preparing to travel to the UK for a medical after a meeting with club officials in Paris.

A sell-on is due to be included also while his former club Rapid Wien are also due a percentage.

Daily Mail Sport revealed on Tuesday evening how Brentford had stepped up their interest to sign the Mali international as it became apparent they would be agreeing to mutually terminate Jordan Henderson's contract and pave the way for him to join Chelsea.

Brentford had a long-held interest in Sangare but had to fend off competition from two other English clubs including Crystal Palace.

Wednesday's Daily Mail carried news of Brentford's move for Sangare

Stones set for Inter switch

Inter Milan are expected to confirm the signing of England defender John Stones later tonight.

The 32-year-old left Inter's headquarters earlier this evening after having his medical and agreeing a two-year contract ahead of his free transfer from Manchester City.

"Sono entusiasta di essere qui". John Stones è arrivato a Milano ⚫️🔵 pic.twitter.com/Xp2rS66VL9 — Fcinter1908 (@fcin1908it) July 30, 2026

Meanwhile, talks between Manchester City and Lille are reaching a crucial stage over the transfer of Ayyoub Bouaddi.

The 18-year-old Morocco international is ready to make the move now though his club have been keen to keep him in France for another season as part of negotiations.

City are ready to use him this season with Rodri a target for Real Madrid while interest is building in Nico Gonzalez and Tijjani Reijnders.

City have lost Bernardo Silva and also have interest from Tottenham in Omar Marmoush and Savinho.

Bouaddi was valued around £60m before the World Cup but is now considered to be worth around £80m.

City also want to add another goalkeeper to replace Leeds-bound James Trafford with Marseille's Geronimo Rulli one name under consideration. They also want to strengthen at right-back and on the wing with Chelsea's Pedro Neto and Paris St Germain's Ibrahim Mbaye among names discussed.

Daily Mail Sport reported on Wednesday that the teenage Morocco international is ready to make the move now, though the French club would prefer him to stay for another season.

City would want Bouaddi for this season with Real Madrid ready to push for Rodri who is keen to return to Spain for family reasons.

Though they have added Elliot Anderson, they have lost Bernardo Silva and could also sell Nico Gonzalez and Tijjani Reijnders who has interest from Galatasaray and earlier in the summer Atletico Madrid.

Foxes eye Brighton winger Watson

Leicester City have enquired about taking Brighton winger Tommy Watson on loan.

The 20-year-old, who was key to Sunderland's promotion to the Premier League 18 months ago, had a spell on loan at Millwall last season.

Tommy Watson helped secure Sunderland's promotion to the Premier League via the playoffs

Porto keep tabs on Spurs man Souza

Porto are the latest team to show interest in Tottenham left wing-back Souza.

The 20-year-old joined from Santos for £13m in January and made four Premier League appearances last season.

Hail Cesar as Fulham get their man from Madrid

Fulham have agreed to buy Cesar Palacios from Real Madrid for a bargain £8.5million.

The deal has a similar structure to the one they have agreed for Gonzalo Garcia with Madrid retaining a 30percent sell on clause and matching rights for the 20-year-old.

Fulham are also among the clubs showing interest in Arsenal winger Ethan Nwaneri and Southampton midfielder Shea Charles.

Nwaneri also has interest from RB Leipzig and AC Milan.

Cesar Palacios has been secured for a fee of £8.5million

Fredricson moves on

Manchester United defender Tyler Fredricson has agreed a permanent move to Swiss club Lausanne-Sport, subject to registration.

Fredricson made four first-team appearances since he was handed a debut against Wolves in 2025 – when he also won the reserve-team player of the year award – and was on the bench on a number of occasions last season.

United have inserted a substantial sell-on clause and a buy-back clause into the deal.

The 21-year-old, who joined United at Under-9 level, played in every round of United’s successful FA Youth Cup campaign in 2022 until illness ruled him out of the final against Nottingham Forest.

The club confirmed Fredricson’s departure in a statement on Thursday, saying: ‘Everybody at United thanks Tyler for all his efforts during his time with the club and we wish him all the best for the next chapter of his career.’

Fredricson joins United loanee Sekou Kone at the Swiss Super League side.

CHRIS WHEELER

Rashford says no to Roma

Marcus Rashford has no interest in joining Roma this summer as speculation regarding his future grows.

The 28-year-old is set to report to pre-season training with Manchester United in the coming days after returning from his loan spell with Barcelona.

Roma had been one of several clubs linked with a move for the England attacker, but Daily Mail Sport understands a move to the Italian giants does not appeal.

Fulham to spend big on Garcia

Fulham are closing on agreement with Real Madrid over a deal worth £35m for striker Gonzalo Garcia. The deal also includes £2m in bonuses and matching rights.

Madrid have been discussing a buy-back option and a 30 per cent sell-on clause as talks draw to a conclusion.

Fulham also working to add midfielder Cesar Palacios on loan from Madrid.

Gonzalo Garcia looks set to join Fulham from Real Madrid in a deal worth £60m

Hull's Nobel quest

Hull are advancing in talks for Rayo Vallecano defender Nobel Mendy.

As Daily Mail Sport reported yesterday, Hull had made enquiries and proposed a £15m offer for the 21-year-old who can play centre back and left back.

Rangers tried to sign Mendy a year ago from Real Betis but Vallecano got him for £2.5m and a 20 per cent sell-on clause.

Hull face competition from Ipswich for Burnley's Florentino Luis but have enquired about Augsburg's midfielder Mert Komur.

Coventry explore Hamer homecoming

Coventry City are exploring a deal to re-sign Gustavo Hamer from Sheffield United.

The 29-year-old midfielder has one year left on his deal at Bramall Lane.

The Brazilian made 132 appearances for the club scoring 19 goals which included a strike in the Championship play-off final against Luton Town at Wembley.

Atletico reignite Romero interest

Atletico Madrid have rekindled their interest in Tottenham defender Cristian Romero.

The Argentina international's agents held talks with Inter Milan last weekend and director Piero Ausilio confirmed interest but that the deal would be complicated owing to the financial package.

Atletico Madrid are exploring a potential move for Tottenham captain Cristian Romero

Atletico had interest last year and are exploring the figures involved in a deal for the 28-year-old Spurs captain again.

Inter are in the market for centre backs this summer, with one new recruit expected to be John Stones if all goes to plan in his medical today.

Sports.title: Mamadou Sangare travelling to UK for medical as Brentford close in on £41m deal for midfielder after Jordan Henderson's exit
Sports.content:
Mamadou Sangare travelling to UK for medical as Brentford close in on £41m deal for midfielder after Jordan Henderson's exit

Brentford are closing in on a deal to sign Lens midfielder Mamadou Sangare for £41million

The star will replace Jordan Henderson, who has left the Bees ahead of a move to Chelsea

How we reported Brentford's move in Window Watch online and in Wednesday's Daily Mail

Sports.title: Tottenham's 'bomba' signing: These are the two strikers they want, the game-changers they should be in for and the realistic targets that would fit perfectly with Roberto De Zerbi's style of play
Sports.content:
Trust Roberto De Zerbi to drop a bomb. Tottenham have already spent nearly £250million this summer, enough to give Daniel Levy the shakes, but the Italian made it clear Spurs were not done. ‘The transfer market, it’s not finished for sure,’ said De Zerbi. ‘We completed 60 per cent of our project in the transfer market. Now we have another bomba. Is it close? I hope, but it’s not finished for sure.’ Bomba. Both short for ‘bomba di mercato’, an Italian phrase meaning ‘market bombshell’, as well as a term used by Gen Z in online slang to mean a major surprise, a big piece of news, or a significant development. This is certainly one of those. ‘We have to increase the number of goals with the quality of the play, with the midfielders, with the attackers, but we have to bring players able to score goals. We have to consider set-pieces, we have to increase also the height, a lot of things.’ Roberto De Zerbi has promised Tottenham fans another 'bomba' signing in the forward line - and claims their already booming business this summer is only '60 per cent' finished They certainly need goals. They mustered 48 in the Premier League last season, fewer than most sides in the division. Eighteen of them came from corners, making up nearly 40 per cent of all their goals, by far the highest ratio in the division. So, perhaps, it’s not the set-pieces that need most of the attention. Spurs have completed huge deals for defender Jan Paul van Hecke for more than £50m and midfielders Mateus Fernandes for £85m and Sandro Tonali for £100m. They are in talks over signing winger Savinho from Manchester City but even he’s not believed to be the bomba. Whoever it is, it must be the man to bring them their much-needed goals. Daily Mail Sport assesses who De Zerbi’s mystery bombshell could be. Omar Marmoush De Zerbi is said to be a big admirer of the Egypt international and, despite making just eight league starts for Pep Guardiola last term, it’s easy to see why. As we saw with his use of Joao Pedro at Brighton, De Zerbi likes his strikers to drop deep and link up play, pulling defenders out of position to create space for wingers like Kaoru Mitoma or Simon Adingra to exploit and score goals. At Marseille, too, it was wide forward Mason Greenwood who finished as De Zerbi’s top scorer last season. That’s why Tottenham were so keen on Bournemouth striker Junior Kroupi before he was ruled out for up to four months with a foot injury. De Zerbi is a big admirer of Omar Marmoush (pictured), and it's easy to see why Bournemouth's Eli Junior Kroupi (right) has been a target all summer - but has been ruled out for months with a foot injury When Marmoush played up front for City last season, often alongside Erling Haaland in a front two, he was usually the player to drop in to collect the ball and allow players to run on ahead of him. He did just that against West Ham last season (see below) as he holds the ball with Haaland, Nico O’Reilly, Antoine Semenyo and Bernardo Silva sprinting ahead of him. Marmoush draws his marker, slips in Silva, and he dinks the ball over the keeper with a sublime finish. Marmoush drops deep to get on the ball - just as De Zerbi likes his strikers to do - before slipping Bernardo Silva in down the left That ability to create space for those around him is ideal for how De Zerbi wants his Spurs team to play. But that’s not enough for De Zerbi. He wants forwards who, once that’s done, can turn and attack the box to get on the end of any chances created by the wide players. Marmoush can do that, too. That was clear in his finish when he led the line on his own without Haaland against Wolves in January, bursting to get ahead of his defender and on to the end of Matheus Nunes’ cross. Against Wolves last season, City's Marmoush attacks the space in the box and scores from Matheus Nunes' cross Marmoush also gives De Zerbi the option to play him in that striker role or as a left winger, where he’s also flourished. Few City fans will forget his hat-trick against Newcastle. Dominic Solanke is already a superb operator when it comes to coming short to help bring his team-mates into play and Marmoush is a fine, explosive option down the left. He’s quick, too. His top speed of 21.9mph put him inside the 25 fastest players at the World Cup. Cody Gakpo Tottenham are also understood to be interested in the Liverpool forward. De Zerbi, happy to say all the quiet things out loud when proclaiming what he’s looking for, declared Spurs have to ‘increase the height’ of his team. At 6ft 4in, Gakpo would certainly do that. Gakpo is another that fits the De Zerbi profile as a forward who likes to drift in off the left and attack the box but who also can play down the middle. And, when he does, he is the kind of striker who can drop in to mix it up. This is Gakpo’s touchmap from Liverpool’s final Premier League game of the Arne Slot era, a home draw to Brentford, where the Dutchman started as the lone striker but had most of the ball closer towards the halfway line. Cody Gakpo's touch map from Liverpool's home match against Brentford last season shows how he is far from a No 9, rather a forward who drops in to get on the ball Gakpo also has the wherewithal to nip in behind high lines, as shown below against Fulham in another game where he started as the lone striker. He latched on the ball over the top and raced through but couldn’t find the finish. Gakpo can also play on the shoulder of the defender and make runs in behind Gakpo, a regular starter last season, found himself cast as the fall guy for Liverpool’s dismal title defence under Slot. He was frequently the subject of fan derision while a return of just seven goals and five assists from 32 starts did little to help that perception, especially when he’d notched 10 goals from 23 starts during the title-winning campaign. He fits De Zerbi’s profile but not many Spurs fans would, perhaps unfairly, see his arrival as the bomba they would want. Gakpo is a good fit for the profile of player De Zerbi wants - but would he be the bomba Spurs fans are craving? Dusan Vlahovic Can a free transfer be a bomba signing? Zlatan Ibrahimovic’s arrival at Manchester United in 2016 would suggest so. Vlahovic, 26, remains a free agent after his four-and-a-half-year stint at Juventus came to an end. Tottenham are said to be interested in the No 9 and, like Gakpo, he would fulfil De Zerbi’s desire for added height as he stands at 6ft 3in. His 68 goals in 168 games was a fair old return at Juve and he reached double figures in his last six campaigns, stretching back into his tenure at Fiorentina. His 20 goals in 24 games for them in 2021-22 earned his big-money move to the Old Lady. Last season, too, he ranked among the division’s leading goalscorers when he was on the pitch with his trusty left foot. That, however, was the problem. He barely was. He missed huge chunks of the season with adductor and calf injuries.

Your browser does not support iframes.

Tottenham already have two injury-prone strikers in Richarlison and Solanke. They don’t need another. Not to mention Vlahovic was the highest-paid player in the whole of Serie A last season. He might be free to sign, but he’ll be far from that to keep. And he would be a completely different style of striker to those that De Zerbi likes to use. He’s an out-and-out front man. He rarely drops deep, he’s not the best at linking up play. That, for De Zerbi, is surely not the bomba. Serbia striker Dusan Vlahovic, who is now a free agent after leaving Juventus, is another option for Spurs but has had plenty of injury problems Marcus Rashford Despite 14 goals and 14 assists in all competitions (and nine goals which helped fire Barcelona to the La Liga crown), the Catalan giants opted not to cash in their £25m option to make Rashford’s loan move permanent, so he returns to Manchester United. Rashford hasn’t featured for his boyhood club since 2024 and is unlikely to feature in Michael Carrick’s plans for the season. As a forward who shifts in off the flank into central areas and can also play up front, naturally there has been some speculation that De Zerbi's Spurs could be a good move for Rashford. He ranked behind only superstars Lamine Yamal, Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius Junior and Raphinha for the most shot-ending carries in La Liga last season. He proved that he can still make things happen when he’s on the ball, doing his best work in the channels.

Your browser does not support iframes.

De Zerbi, though, for all his desire to play up and down and through the lines, is not renowned for his speed in moving the ball upfield. His Brighton side in 2023-24 produced the fewest fast breaks of any side in the division. He likes his side to build up patiently but then slice open defences with splitting passes. That’s why he’s signed defenders like Van Hecke and Marcos Senesi and midfielders like Fernandes and Tonali. That doesn’t suit Rashford quite so much, nor does De Zerbi’s desire for constant pressing and off-the-ball work. Marcus Rashford is available after Barcelona refused the option to take him on a permanent deal from Manchester United Lautaro Martinez Now, this would be a bomba. The top scorer in Serie A last season with 17 goals for Inter, and third behind only team-mate Federico Dimarco and Como winger Jesus Rodriguez for open-play assists. Tactically, he’s ideal for how De Zerbi plays. He drops off the front line, dragging defenders with him, to combine with his team-mates and then attacks the space that’s vacated. His heat map from 2025-26 (below) shows how he covered every blade of grass in the opponent’s half, with many of the chances he created coming from deeper areas. Lautaro Martinez's heat map in Serie A 2025-26 (deeper colour, more touches) shows how he covers every blade of grass Martinez creates chances from deep, he is not just a six-yard box player Martinez will be hard to get, though, as he loves playing for Inter Milan and has gone public about it Good luck getting him, though. ‘If they (Inter) don’t kick me out, I’m staying,’ he said recently. 'No doubt I would like to retire at this club.’ Julian Alvarez How about another Argentinian in Julian Alvarez? Arsenal have already been gazumped on Morgan Rogers, could it happen on Alvarez too? The former Man City forward has declared his desire to leave Atletico Madrid this summer to ‘fulfil his dream’. He does have a €500m release clause, though, and Atletico have already rejected a bid of £129m from Real Madrid. Now, here is a player who really does fit the De Zerbi brief - and 20 goals and nine assists in all competitions for Atletico last season show why. His 10 goals in the Champions League put him behind just Mbappe and Harry Kane. Argentina striker Julian Alvarez is a player who really does fit the De Zerbi brief Not only does he drop in, drag defenders around, and link up the play, he presses like a midfielder too. During the World Cup, starting up front alongside Lionel Messi, Alvarez did the hard yards. His touch map against England (below) showed just how much of it he did. Alvarez's touch map against England shows how he too likes to roam around the pitch During his final season at City, Alvarez won possession in the final third more often than any other striker. Now, he would be a bombshell signing.

Sports.title: Next stop... Paris? Diamond Necklace could thrill French fans after sparkling in Goodwood sunshine
Sports.content:
Next stop... Paris? Diamond Necklace could thrill French fans after sparkling in Goodwood sunshine

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Diamond Necklace sparkled in the Goodwood sunshine to land the Group 1 Qatar Nassau Stakes and could be poised to strut her stuff in Paris this autumn.

Aidan O’Brien’s filly extended her unbeaten career record to six with a routine two-and-three-quarter-length defeat of Friendly Soul under Ryan Moore, encouraging her handler to dream of a tilt at the Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe in October.

O’Brien said: ‘Diamond Necklace is a lovely filly who has danced every dance. This was up to a mile and a quarter against older fillies, so we did not really know what was going to happen, but we wanted to put on pace to find out.

‘She has options now, whether she stays at a mile and a quarter and goes to the fillies’ race in France, or to Leopardstown or an Arc trial. She is a great cruiser and progressing well.

Diamond Necklace pulls clear at Goodwood to win the Qatar Nassau Stakes

SAM'S DAY 4 TIPS... 15.00 – Cerulean Bay each-way The loveable Cerulean Bay will be written off by many given he tackles this highly competitive handicap off a career high mark. That is an understandable take, but the profile of this race has changed a little in recent years with many of the lightly-raced three-year-olds which used to frequent this contest sold to race abroad. Although Cerulean Bay has been around a while he is only five and he returns to the South Downs looking to defend an unbeaten 2-2 record at the track so appeals as a sporting each-way play with Colin Keane booked. 15.35 – Jakajaro There wouldn’t be many quicker horses in training than Jakajaro and he may put that blistering early speed to good use in this exciting renewal. Trainer Robert Cowell is adept at finding improvement with maturing sprinters and the five-year-old has taken his form to another level this term, including when a fine third in a Group 2 event at the Curragh last time when the climb to the line found him out late on. This downhill track should play to his strengths ideally and he should go close to landing this for his owners who love a winner at this meeting. 6.10 Naqeeb each-way The son of Nathaniel has been a superb flagbearer for Julie Camacho and Steve Brown and it was agonising for the Yorkshire-based training operation that their versatile six-year-old was beaten a short-head in a Listed affair at today’s venue back in May. That narrow defeat meant his track stats now read 212 and the selection ran right up to his best in the Summer Mile at Ascot last time when a creditable fifth to Zeus Olympios, a race which has already thrown up a win for runner-up Holloway Bay.

‘It is possible (the Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe). I do not know how far we ask her to go, and it will depend on everything, but the next run will tell us where she is going to go after that.

Moore was equally enthusiastic about the daughter of St Mark’s Basilica: ‘That is the best Diamond Necklace has felt. She is improving with her racing.

‘I think 10 furlongs is probably her optimum, but with those classy horses, they do everything right, so there is a chance she would stay further.’

The combination recorded a double in the Markel Richmond Stakes when it proved more of a case of punters’ best friend than Man’s Best Friend with Moore steering the popular 11/2 chance to success in the Group 2 event.

The victory looked in doubt for much of the contest as the colt’s rider struggled to find a clear passage aboard the Ballydoyle-trained son of No Nay Never.

However, once in the clear the duo flew past the admirable Adaay Of Scarlett to score by a snug length and give his trainer a first win in the race since 2000.

If it’s not one O’Brien winning, it’s another and Aidan’s son Joseph got in on the action courtesy of the progressive Enceladus in the Group 3 Gordon Stakes.

The winner of Royal Ascot’s King George V Handicap took the step up to Group company in his stride, finding plenty for pressure from the furlong marker under Dylan Browne McMonagle to comfortably hold the challenge of Geryon by a length and a quarter.

Asked about stepping up in trip for the St Leger, Browne McMonagle said: ‘I am sure the distance will be no problem for him, but he is not short of gears either; he has plenty of gears for a mile and a half.

‘I think as he develops, it will be no problem going up in trip, which will open up options for him going forwards.’

Billy Loughnane, hero of day two for his exploits on Visit Qatar Sussex Stakes winner Bow Echo, came crashing back down to earth, quite literally, when his first-race ride Savvy Disco dramatically clipped heels at the furlong marker and came down.

Thankfully, both horse and jockey were absolutely fine and none the worse for the experience, so much so that Loughnane rose from the canvas to partner Avalon Queen to victory in the seven furlong maiden.

Over at Galway, Daniel King became the first jockey in 42 years to win both the Plate and the Hurdle when Putapoundinthejar followed hard on the heels of success for King Alexander 24 hours beforehand.

Sports.title: Arsenal close in on £80m Bruno Guimaraes transfer in major breakthrough for Mikel Arteta
Sports.content:
Arsenal close in on £80m Bruno Guimaraes transfer in major breakthrough for Mikel Arteta

Arsenal have been chasing a deal for Bruno Guimaraes for weeks and a deal to bring the midfielder to north London is now closer - even though Newcastle are reluctant sellers

View 2 Images Arsenal are moving closer to a deal for Bruno Guimaraes (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Arsenal are now said to be 'increasingly confident' when it comes to their chances of clinching a deal for the wantaway Newcastle captain, Bruno Guimaraes.

‌



The Gunners have been pursuing Guimaraes all summer, making the Brazil international a priority transfer target. He is wanted to beef up Arsenal's midfield as Mikel Arteta and Co attempt to enhance a squad which not only won the Premier League last season for the first time in more than 20 years but also reached the Champions League final.

‌



It has been an open secret that Guimaraes is keen on the opportunity to compete for major trophies with Arsenal, even though Newcastle have no desire to sell their captain.

‌



However, it now seems as though the 28-year-old will get his wish with BBC Sport reporting that multiple sources now expect Guimaraes to join Arsenal.

Eddie Howe told what made his Newcastle job 'unsustainable' before sudden departure READ MORE :

Five moments that defined Eddie Howe's rise and fall during Newcastle tenure READ MORE :

It's added that although Newcastle are still reluctant to admit defeat in their attempts to keep Guimaraes at St James' Park, Arsenal are hopeful of closing a deal worth around the £80million mark in the coming days.

The news will come as a major boost for Arteta, who has already seen the club miss out on their top target for the left-wing berth, Morgan Rogers.

‌



Guimaraes would become the latest high-profile player to depart the Magpies if Arsenal can strike an agreement with Newcastle, with personal terms already done and dusted.

View 2 Images It emerged on Thursday that Eddie Howe has left Newcastle

Alexander Isak effectively went on strike last summer to clinch a £120m move to Liverpool, while Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali have already been sold earlier in the current transfer window for significant fees to Barcelona and Tottenham respectively.

‌



Not only are Newcastle now likely to lose another talismanic player, but their head coach, Eddie Howe, is also moving on.

It emerged on Thursday morning that Howe had informed Newcastle's top brass that he wished to stand down from his role in order to take a break.

The former Bournemouth chief is poised to be replaced by Matthias Jaissle, the German coach currently in charge of Saudi Pro League outfit, Al-Ahli.

Sports.title: Rising star jockey makes history by completing huge Galway Festival double
Sports.content:
Rising star jockey makes history by completing huge Galway Festival double

Dan King, 21, who has been tipped to go all the way to the top, became the first rider for 42 years to win both the Galway Plate and Galway Hurdle

View 2 Images Dan King with his two Galway trophies (Image: Brian Lawless/PA Wire. Use subject to restrictions. Editorial use only, no commercial use without prior consent from rights holder)

Rising star jump jockey Dan King made history on Thursday when he completed a huge Galway Festival double.

‌



The 21-year-old, who has been tipped to go all the way to the top in his profession, underlined his potential by pulling off a feat that had not been done for 42 years.

‌



On Wednesday, King netted the biggest prize of his burgeoning career as King Alexander defied odds of 20-1 to give Willie Mullins a third victory in the Galway Plate. The combination moved effortlessly into the lead from long-time leader Nouvotic at the second-last fence and ground it out from fast finisher Conyers Hill to win by half a length.

‌



Less than 24 hours after that success he rode Putapoundinthejar to capture the Guinness Galway Hurdle

Saving ground the whole way on the 10-1 winner, who was giving trainer Tony Martin his fifth victory in the race, King and Putapoundinthejar led at the final flight to beat Thisistheway by three and a quarter lengths.

‌



“It was plain sailing the whole way round,” he said after emulating the late Joe Byrne who was successful aboard Master Player and Tara Lee in 1984.

View 2 Images Daniel King (centre) riding Putapoundinthejar celebrates as he wins the Guinness Galway Hurdle (Image: Brian Lawless/PA Wire. Use subject to restrictions. Editorial use only, no commercial use without prior consent from rights holder)

“He jumped savage the whole way round - he didn’t miss a beat. I took a chance going round the inside but when I wanted the gaps to open up they did.

Article continues below

“I’d never ridden a winner at the Galway Festival before but I was hopeful - I was coming here this week with a few nice rides. “When you get two of the biggest pots of the week, it’s class. “Dream stuff.”

Martin added of Putapoundinthejar: “He’s a big, old-fashioned horse. He was only coming to himself since Christmas and hopefully he’ll go on improving.”

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino MUST GO - FIFA chief has no way back after brutal response to World Cup plot
Sports.content:
Over the course of the World Cup, Gianni Infantino attended 45 matches and was captured by television cameras at every one of them.

Rarely was there a moment when he was not wearing a smug look. Record-breaking commercial income was on its way, stadiums were full and he had a $20billion trick up his sleeve - he was going to flog off the rights to the greatest sporting show on earth to private investors, dressing it up as a way of making extra cash for FIFA’s 211 member nations.

Well, 55 of those member nations have told him what he can do with his scheme. Ditch it. Or face not having a World Cup at all. Or a Women’s World Cup. Or a Club World Cup. Or any FIFA-organised World Cup.

Because without the European nations, there is no World Cup, of any kind. You can bet Gianni is not looking so smug today.

UEFA could not have been more unequivocal. A truly unprecedented statement read: “No UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership.”

UEFA statement in FULL as they boycott World Cup until FIFA abandon controversial proposal READ MORE :

England and UEFA nations WILL BOYCOTT World Cup in protest over Gianni Infantino sale plan READ MORE :

But the UEFA statement goes way, way beyond announcing a boycott of FIFA competitions, in itself a genuinely seismic decision in the history of football governance.

It lacerates Infantino’s integrity and morality. It lays his fitness for purpose to waste.

When talking of it being ‘irresponsible and indefensible’ that the FIFA proposal was ‘conceived in secret’, they are referring directly to Infantino.

When talking of a ‘profound failure of leadership’, they are referring directly to Infantino.

When talking of ‘an abdication of FIFA’s duty as the custodian of world football’, they are referring directly to Infantino.

When talking of ‘governance by intimidation’, they are referring directly to Infantino.

This is UEFA, the association whose teams dominate the World Cup. The powerhouse association of world football. The association who provided six of the eight quarter-finalists at World Cup 2026.

And in their landmark emergency meeting, they not only made sure Infantino’s outlandish scheme is dead in the water, they clinically and viciously dismantled the character of the man in charge of world football, the man who Donald Trump believes would make a good Secretary General of NATO.

Well, perhaps Trump can get his mate the NATO gig because his position as FIFA president is now untenable. Infantino’s thick skin is the stuff of legend but it is impossible to see how he can stay in his post after this evisceration.

The statement from UEFA is pretty grand in its own morality.

It concludes: “Some things are simply too important to sell. The FIFA World Cup belongs to football. It always will. And so long as Europe has a voice, it will never be for sale.”

It needs to be said that UEFA have not been slow to commercialise European football but that is another story.

They have been gunning for Infantino for some time, certainly since he launched the expanded Club World Cup.

And with this disgraceful, ill-judged, avaricious, mood-ignorant plot of his, Infantino has left himself open to be taken down.

UEFA have taken their chance with cold brutality. Infantino has to go.
