World.title: Ex-finance minister buried in Sokoto
World.content:
The remains of former Nigeria’s Minister of Finance, Alhaji Abubakar Alhaji, were buried on Thursday at Hubbare Royal Cemetery, Sokoto.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the late elder statesman held the traditional title of Sardaunan Sokoto.

His burial was conducted in line with Islamic rites, following a funeral prayer led by Sheikh Bello-Akwara, Chief Imam of Sultan Bello Juma’at Mosque.

The prayer was attended by Vice-President Kashim Shettima, who represented President Bola Tinubu at the ceremony.

Also present were Minister of Labour and Employment, Alhaji Maigari Dingyadi, and Minister of Budget and Economic Planning, Sen. Atiku Bagudu.

Sokoto State Governor, Ahmed Aliyu, was represented by his deputy, Alhaji Idris Gobir, at the funeral.

The Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Sa’ad Abubakar, Speaker of the state House of Assembly, Tukur Bala Bodinga, and other dignitaries attended.

After the funeral, Shettima visited the Sultan and other relatives to offer condolences over Alhaji’s death.

The Vice-President prayed for the repose of the deceased’s soul and comfort for his family.

Alhaji died on Thursday at Nizamiye Hospital in Abuja, ending a distinguished public service career spanning several decades.

NAN recalls that he served as Nigeria’s Minister of Finance from 1985 to 1986 during a critical period.

He was also a former Secretary to the Government of the Federation and Nigeria’s High Commissioner to the United Kingdom.

Before his political appointments, Alhaji had a remarkable federal civil service career, rising to become a Permanent Secretary.

He was widely regarded as one of Nigeria’s foremost technocrats, contributing significantly to national economic management.

The late Sardaunan Sokoto played a key role in shaping economic policies and managing relations with international financial institutions.

His contributions came during a challenging era in Nigeria’s economic history, leaving a lasting legacy in public administration.

World.title: John Stones joins Inter Milan on free transfer
World.content:
Stones

England centre-back John Stones has joined Inter Milan on a free transfer after spending 10 years with Manchester City, the Italian champions announced on Thursday.

The 32-year-old left City when his contract expired at the end of last month, while playing for England at the World Cup where he helped them to a third-placed finish.

Stones has signed a two-year deal with Inter, a club statement said.

He played five times for England at the recent World Cup in the United States, Mexico and Canada, making his 94th international appearance in the semi-final loss to Argentina.

Stones was a key player for Manchester City during their golden era under former manager Pep Guardiola, winning six Premier League titles, three FA Cups, three League Cups and a Champions League crown with the club.

His final few seasons at the Etihad Stadium, though, were hit by injuries, and he only made nine Premier League appearances last term.

Stones could make his Inter debut when they start their Scudetto defence against Monza at the San Siro on August 22.

AFP

World.title: 2027: INEC assures Nigerians votes will count, urges politicians to obey electoral rules
World.content:
By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin

ILORIN — The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has assured Nigerians that votes cast during the 2027 general elections will count, pledging to conduct credible polls that reflect the will of the electorate.

Head of Voter Education and Publicity, INEC Kwara State, Dr. Adejumo Peter, gave the assurance on Thursday in Ilorin during a seminar organised by the Correspondents’ Chapel of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ).

He said the commission would do everything within its constitutional mandate to ensure that the outcome of the elections reflected the wishes of the people.

Peter dismissed the practice by some politicians of allegedly stockpiling Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), describing it as outdated and ineffective.

“INEC has introduced measures that make it impossible for anyone to use another person’s PVC to vote. That is why politicians have resorted to vote-buying.

“Many politicians are still living in the past because stockpiling or carting away PVCs cannot guarantee electoral victory,” he said.

He reiterated INEC’s commitment to conducting elections based on the principle of “one person, one vote.”

“INEC in Kwara will follow the rules and procedures laid down by the commission. We will ensure that elections are conducted on the basis of one person, one vote.

“At the end of the exercise, the outcome of the elections will reflect the will of the people,” he said.

Peter also urged politicians to conduct their campaigns peacefully and in accordance with the law, advising them to focus on presenting their manifestoes rather than resorting to violence.

“I urge politicians to play by the rules. They should campaign and present their manifestoes to the electorate. They should shun violence before, during and after the elections.

“Let us conduct elections peacefully, like sportsmanship. They should also accept the outcome of the elections,” he added.

Speaking on the theme, “Dissecting the Amended Electoral Act 2026: Innovations and Implications for Nigeria’s 2027 General Elections,” the Head of INEC’s Legal Unit in Kwara State, Atata Abdulfatai, described the amended Electoral Act as a major milestone in Nigeria’s electoral evolution.

According to him, the legislation introduces reforms aimed at improving transparency, strengthening internal party democracy and expanding the use of technology in the electoral process.

He, however, noted that the law also raises legal and practical issues relating to constitutional consistency, enforcement of campaign finance limits, judicial jurisdiction over party affairs and the grounds for election petitions.

“The success of these innovations will depend not only on their legislative design but also on effective implementation, institutional capacity and judicial interpretation,” Abdulfatai said.

World.title: FG won’t negotiate with criminals — Tinubu
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu says his administration will not negotiate with criminals, insisting that Nigeria will intensify intelligence-driven operations to defeat terrorism, banditry and other security threats.

Read Also: Tinubu to governors: Build roads, not flyovers, white‑elephant projects

The president stated this on Thursday while receiving traditional rulers from Oyo State, led by the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, at the Presidential Villa, Abuja.

Tinubu commended the armed forces for their role in recent rescue operations and acknowledged the support of traditional rulers in strengthening security efforts.

“I agree with you that we should commend the men and women of the armed forces for their excellent performance.

“On behalf of them, I accept your message, and I will forward the same message to them.”

Tinubu said recent security challenges had prompted a review of the country’s security architecture and operational strategies.

“That event (Oyo school abduction) teaches us new methods, opens our eyes and challenges us to examine and re-examine our security architecture, strategy, map and operations,” he said.

The President said the Federal Government approved the expansion of the Nigerian Army from eight to 12 divisions to improve response time and strengthen operational effectiveness.

“From eight divisions, we are now moving to 12 divisions to shorten the response time and give that response the teeth that is needed for us to defeat terrorism and banditry.”

Tinubu reiterated his administration’s refusal to negotiate with criminal groups or accede to their demands.

“We refuse to negotiate for ransom. These criminals wanted us to release from detention members of their criminal gangs that were already arrested.

“That was one of their conditions outside the money they were looking for, and we said no deal. We are not going to negotiate with criminals,” he said.

According to him, many of the criminals had committed murder and other serious crimes and must face justice.

The President said insecurity in neighbouring Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger Republic had compounded Nigeria’s security challenges.

Tinubu said that the Federal Government was strengthening forest guards and pursuing the establishment of state police with safeguards against abuse.

“There will be state police, and that state police will have guardrails against abuses. We will protect it from abuses, and you traditional rulers too will have a role to play more.”

He assured that forest guards would be equipped and empowered to confront criminal elements operating in forests nationwide.

“They are not just to chase antelopes and animals. We are going to have them chase the criminals and deal with them in various forests.”

The President emphasised the importance of intelligence gathering and urged traditional rulers to encourage vigilance among their subjects.

“The mention of intelligence is very important, and I want you to take it to our people to be extra vigilant, know their neighbourhoods, know their areas and report strange people.”

Tinubu also urged governors to deploy increased federal allocations to infrastructure and security-enhancing projects.

He assured the delegation that security conditions were improving and pledged to continue investing in security agencies.

“The security challenge is getting better. We are getting a hang of it much better. Any time you come across some of our soldiers and police officers, please pat them on the back and say thank you. They are doing a good job,” Tinubu said.

Earlier, Ladoja commended Tinubu for his handling of the recent abduction incident in Oyo State, particularly the decision not to pay ransom.

“The fact that you did not pay ransom, the fact that you stood your ground shows that we now have a government that knows what is to be done. We cannot thank you enough for that feat,” he said.

The traditional ruler also urged the Federal Government to sustain security presence in forest reserves and continue ongoing infrastructure projects across Oyo State.

Vanguard News

World.title: ‘I had major surgery days ago’ — Ayra Starr reveals health scare
World.content:
Ayra Starr

By Adegboyega Adeleye

Grammy-nominated Afrobeats star Ayra Starr has disclosed that she recently underwent major surgery, apologising to fans for her reduced presence on social media while assuring them she is on the road to recovery.

The 24-year-old singer shared the update via her Instagram Story on Thursday, explaining that although she initially expected a quick recovery, the procedure turned out to be more complicated than anticipated.

“Hey Mobstarrs, I’m sorry you’re not seeing as much of me as I would like. I had major surgery a few days ago. I was hoping it would be a quick recovery but it was more complicated than they expected,” she wrote.

The ‘Rush’ hitmaker, however, did not reveal the nature of the surgery or disclose further details about her health.

Despite the setback, Ayra Starr reassured fans that she only needs time to recuperate before returning to work.

“I just need a bit of rest and I’ll be back!!!” she added.

The singer also urged her supporters to continue promoting her forthcoming project, Starrgirl, asking them to spread the word and place their orders.

“Starrgirl is coming so soooon. I need everyone out there spreading the word. Tell your friends, your family, your neighbours! Order Starrgirl ASAP!!! Love you guys.”

Born Oyinkansola Sarah Aderibigbe, Ayra Starr rose to prominence in 2021 with her breakout hit “Bloody Samaritan”. Since signing with Mavin Records, she has established herself as one of Africa’s biggest music exports, earning several local and international awards, including Grammy nominations.

World.title: ‘I never wanted P-Square back’ — Mr P opens up on fallout
World.content:
By Enitan Abdultawab

Nigerian singer, Peter Okoye, popularly known as Mr P, has claimed that his much-publicised reunion with his twin brother and former P-Square bandmate, Paul Okoye (Rudeboy), was never a genuine reconciliation, describing it instead as a “fake reunion.”

In a lengthy video on his official Instagram page, the singer made the revelation while recounting the events that led to the brothers briefly coming back together after years of public feuding.

The pair first split in 2017 before reuniting in 2021, only for the relationship to deteriorate again amid fresh disputes involving their elder brother and former manager, Jude Okoye.

According to Mr P, the reconciliation began shortly after he returned to Nigeria from Atlanta, when he received a message from his caretaker informing him that Paul had apologised and was seeking forgiveness.

“It was a fake reunion. I came back from Atlanta. Before we descended, I got a message from my caretaker that I should forgive Paul because he had apologised,” he said.

Mr P said he tried reaching his brother by phone without success. However, upon arriving home, he found members of Paul’s team waiting at his residence.

He said his wife later told him that Paul had visited their home around 4 a.m. and appeared visibly shaken.

“My wife came back and held me and told me that Paul came to the house at 4 a.m. and was scared. She recorded the situation. She said Paul kept saying he was tired,” he recalled.

According to the singer, he was encouraged to make the next move since Paul had already reached out.

“I was told that since Paul had made the first move, I should make the second move. I walked to Paul and we hugged.”

He said the reconciliation quickly spread within the family after Jude Okoye’s wife called to inform Jude that the brothers had settled their differences.

Despite the emotional reunion, Mr P insisted he never intended to revive P-Square as a music group.

Recalling what happened the following day, he said Paul told him he wanted to focus on rebuilding the iconic duo, but he declined.

“I posted a video of my new song. He asked about it, and I asked if he had plans. He said he wanted to focus on P-Square. I told him we are back as brothers, but I am not part of P-Square.”

Mr P said Jude later suggested they record a video announcing the reunion so fans could celebrate their reconciliation.

“Jude then called and asked that we make a video so that fans could contribute for us. I did not believe in it. We did it, but we did not make the introduction as P-Square.”

While many fans celebrated the reunion, Mr P said he remained unconvinced because of something Paul had told him during their party that night.

“I did not celebrate, but Paul did. I was still thinking about what Paul said that night. He said, ‘Peter, I do not care if you like what I am about to say or not, but fk Rudeboy, fk Mr P, bring back P-Square.'”

Mr P maintained that his priority had always been restoring family ties rather than reviving the music group.

“He said that when I never wanted P-Square. I just wanted us to come back as family.”

World.title: Tinubu to governors: Build roads, not flyovers, white‑elephant projects
World.content:
–Urges state chief executives to channel more revenues into security-critical infrastructure

—Says some criminal elements involved in Onire kidnap not Nigerians

—Explains why govt refused to negotiate with abductors of Onire pupils

By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu on Thursday urged state governors to prioritise roads and other essential infrastructure instead of constructing flyovers and “white‑elephant” projects, saying better connectivity is vital to reducing insecurity, unlocking economic opportunities and improving Nigerians’ quality of life.

Tinubu gave the advice while receiving traditional rulers from Oyo State, led by the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Adewolu Ladoja, during a courtesy visit to the Presidential Villa, Abuja.

The President said fiscal reforms have increased states’ resources and urged governors to invest those funds in projects that deliver real benefits for citizens rather than costly prestige schemes with little public value.

Extending roads into underserved communities, he said, will boost economic activity and allow security agencies faster access when responding to emergencies. Tinubu argued that strategic infrastructure is indispensable as the country intensifies efforts to defeat terrorism, banditry and other violent crimes.

“The money going to the states today is four to five times what they used to receive. Nobody is borrowing to pay salaries anymore, and pensioners are receiving their entitlements,” he said, urging governors to do more with the increased revenue.

“You should help us communicate to these governors. If you had this money during your own time or during my time, it would have been different. Instead of building flyovers where there is no significant traffic, build roads and arterial networks that improve access, enhance quality of life and enable security agencies to reach vulnerable communities quickly.”

Tinubu said infrastructure planning should be driven by the needs of the people and national security priorities, noting that accessible road networks are critical for rapid deployment of security personnel and delivery of essential services.

He highlighted his administration’s broader security reforms, including plans to expand the Nigerian Army from eight to 12 divisions, establish state police with constitutional safeguards, and strengthen the Forest Guard to tackle criminals operating in forests.

“As we emphasise security, each event teaches us new methods and challenges us to re‑examine our architecture, strategy and operations,” he said.

“We refused to pay ransom. We have the geography of the forest, and in answer to it, we are moving from eight divisions to 12 to shorten response times and give our forces the teeth needed to defeat terrorism and banditry.”

Tinubu warned against negotiating with criminals, saying some abductors demanded the release of already‑detained gang members in addition to ransom.

He also said some perpetrators are non‑Nigerians, linking cross‑border insecurity to instability in neighbouring Sahel countries.

“We are enhancing the capacity of the forest guards. They will not only protect wildlife; they will pursue criminals in the forests. Intelligence is important, and I urge people to be vigilant, know their neighbourhoods and report strangers,” he said.

He added that state police will include safeguards to prevent abuse and that traditional rulers will have roles to play.

He congratulated the traditional rulers on the success of the rescue got Oriire pupils in Oyo state.

“I think we succeeded with your support, prayers, and I agree with you that we should commend the men and women of the armed forces for their excellent performance.

“On behalf of them, I accept your message, and I will forward the same thing and the same message on.

“As we emphasise the question of security, that each event teaches us new methods, opens our eyes, challenge us to examine and re-examine our architecture, our strategy, our map and operations.

“And you will have seen we’ve given a geographical and numerical answer to the challenges. We refused to pay ransom. We have the geography of the forest. We know what it is, and in answer to it, you’ve seen that from eight divisions. Now we are now moving to 12 divisions to shorten the response time to give that response time the teeth that is needed for us to defeat terrorism and banditry.

“It is very necessary, and we are doing so. We have equally embarked upon what was missing, several decades of fears and uncertainty about what to do about security at the local level will be corrected. “

President Tinubu highlighted the importance and advantages of state police in curbing criminal activities in the state.

He also said that mechanisms have been put in place to guard against abuses.

“There will be state police, and that state police will have guardrail from abuses. We will protect it from abuses, and you traditional rulers too will have role to play more,” he said.

Speaking earlier, the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Adewolu Ladoja, thanked the President for the federal government’s response to recent kidnappings in Oyo State. He said the refusal to pay ransom marked a turning point and showed the government’s resolve.

“We were apprehensive after that first major kidnapping in Oyo State, but between you and your security people, you have made a turning point. The fact that you did not pay ransom shows we now have a government that knows what it is doing,” he said.

Oba Ladoja urged sustained security presence in the forest that spans Oyo to Niger State — from Iseyin and Igboho through Kishi to Kwara and Baruten — to prevent criminals from regrouping. He also commended the President’s infrastructural projects in Oyo, noting 10 ongoing projects valued at over N2 trillion and improved road networks that promise progress by the end of Tinubu’s term.

World.title: Tinubu’s infrastructure, human capital investments will drive $1tn economy — APC chairman
World.content:
Yilwatda

ABUJA — National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Prof. Nentawe Goshwe Yilwatda, has said the administration of President Bola Tinubu is making strategic investments in infrastructure and human capital development to achieve its target of building a $1 trillion economy.

Yilwatda stated this while receiving the Governing Council of the Federal University of Health Sciences, Otukpo, Benue State, led by its Pro-Chancellor, Prof. Muhammad Audu, at the APC National Secretariat in Abuja.

According to a statement issued on Thursday by his Special Adviser on Media and Information Strategy, Abimbola Tooki, the APC chairman said ongoing investments in roads, bridges, rail transportation, deep seaports, education and other critical infrastructure were designed to boost productivity, attract investments, create jobs and stimulate sustainable economic growth.

He said the Tinubu administration had adopted a deliberate approach to infrastructure development, stressing that efficient transportation networks remained essential to achieving long-term economic expansion.

Yilwatda disclosed that the Federal Government was working towards developing five major deep seaports across the country, including the Badagry Deep Sea Port in Lagos State, Olokola Deep Sea Port along the Ondo-Ogun axis, Ibom Deep Sea Port in Akwa Ibom State, Bakassi Deep Sea Port in Cross River State and Bonny Deep Sea Port in Rivers State.

“These are not isolated infrastructure projects. They are part of a larger economic strategy. We are building the infrastructure that will support the one-trillion-dollar economy that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has set as a target for Nigeria,” he said.

He added that the government was also constructing coastal highways and other road networks to link the ports and improve the movement of goods and services nationwide.

“We are building seven coastal roads to connect the five deep seaports. The government is deliberate about this. We want to ensure that our transportation infrastructure supports trade, investment and economic activities across the country,” he said.

Yilwatda also highlighted the strategic importance of the railway project linking Nigeria to Maradi in Niger Republic, saying it would strengthen regional trade and enhance Nigeria’s competitiveness as a logistics hub.

According to him, the rail project would facilitate the movement of people and goods while increasing cargo throughput at Nigerian seaports by providing landlocked Niger Republic with easier access to the country’s maritime infrastructure.

The APC chairman said there were currently 81 federal road projects in the North-Central zone and over 260 road and bridge projects across the six geopolitical zones.

He added that the Federal Government had recently approved 27 major road projects valued at about N3.9 trillion across 15 states as part of efforts to improve connectivity, ease transportation and stimulate commerce.

“Our objective is to improve connectivity across the country so that Nigerians can travel from one part of the country to another within a reasonable period. Better roads mean better commerce, easier access to markets, improved access to healthcare and education, and greater opportunities for investment,” he said.

On the economy, Yilwatda said the administration’s tax reforms were aimed at promoting fairness by ensuring lower-income earners paid less tax while higher-income earners contributed proportionately more.

He also said the government’s foreign exchange reforms had improved market management by addressing distortions associated with the parallel market.

According to him, Nigeria’s economic indicators were showing positive signs, citing Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth of about four per cent and improved investor confidence.

He further claimed that the country had attracted significant investment commitments, including a reported $20 billion investment by Shell, which he said would create jobs and stimulate economic activities across multiple sectors.

Yilwatda stressed that the administration’s economic reforms were being complemented by investments in education and healthcare.

He commended the Governing Council of the Federal University of Health Sciences, Otukpo, for its contribution to the training of healthcare professionals, describing the institution as a strategic investment in Nigeria’s future.

He also welcomed recent measures by the Federal Government to improve the welfare of university lecturers, expressing confidence that better remuneration and improved working conditions would strengthen the education sector and reduce industrial disputes.

Earlier, the Pro-Chancellor of the university, Prof. Muhammad Audu, appealed to the APC chairman to facilitate access to President Tinubu and the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, to enable the institution present its development plans and seek support for critical infrastructure projects.

Responding, Yilwatda assured the delegation that the request would receive due attention, noting that strengthening institutions such as the Federal University of Health Sciences, Otukpo, aligned with the administration’s commitment to human capital development.

World.title: Ex-gov Okowa Named WPU Patron, Commends NELFUND Initiative
World.content:
Omon-Julius Onabu in Asaba

Former Governor of Delta State, Dr Ifeanyi Okowa, has commended the Federal Government on the introduction of the National Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), saying the determination of the Tinubu administration to sustain the initiative has led to at least 1.6 million students in tertiary institutions across the country enrolled and benefiting from the educational intervention scheme.

Okowa made the remarks while playing host to the national leadership of the Working People United (WPU) at his residence in Asaba.

The ex-governor, who is the South-South Coordinator of Renewed Hope Ambassadors, is also the Delta North Senatorial Candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC).

He described NELFUND as “a component of the critical reforms being implemented by President Bola Tinubu to revamp Nigeria’s economy which was stuttering.”

Although skeptical students had hitherto reportedly waved off the loan fund as “a scam,” the story has since changed as scores of thousands of students had enrolled in the scheme and benefiting, he pointed out.

Okowa appealed to Nigerians to support the second term bid of President Tinubu, saying his programme of reforms were “beginning to positively addresss some fundamental socio-economic and political issues”, citing as examples the policies of “State Police, deregulation of electricity generation sub-seector and removal of oil subsidy.”

He expressed optimism that Nigerians would soon begin to appreciate the pragmatic efforts of the Tinubu administration in refocusing the country. and called on WPU to rally support for the government ahead of 2027 polls.

Earlier, the National Coordinator of WPU, Comrade Williams Akporeha, told Dr Okowa that the group was in Asaba to inform him of its objectives and to inaugurate Delta State chapter.

He said that membership of the Working People United body comprised public and private sector workers as well as self-employed persons across all cadres and sectors, including artisans.

Specifically, Akporeha explained that the group was concerned about governance and politics in the country, and assured Okowa of their support for his senatorial ambition and also for victory for Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and President Tinubu.

Highpoint of the visit was the conferment of Patronship of WPU on Dr Ifeanyi Okowa.

World.title: Ogboru Condoles With Amaechi Over Mother’s Death
World.content:
Omon-Julius Onabu in Asaba

Delta State gubernatorial candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Chief Great Ovedje Ogboru, has commiserated with the party’s Vice-Presidential Candidate, Hon. Rotimi Amaechi, on the death of his mother, Dame Ezzine Mary Oduah Amaechi.

In a press statement, made available to THISDAY in Asaba, on behalf of his family and the ADC in Delta, Ogboru described the loss “painful and heartbreaking”, saying that he “received the news of Dame Ezzine Mary Amaechi’s passing with profound shock and sadness”.

The late matriarch lived a worthy and impactful life and left behind cherished memories for her family and all who knew her, he said.

The death of a mother is an irreplaceable loss, Ogboru observed, stressing that Dame Ezzine Mary Amaechi departed at a time when her love, prayers, and wise counsel were still greatly needed by her family.

He urged the Amaechi family to take solace in the remarkable legacy their mother left behind, including her true maternal devotion with values, sacrifices and commitment to her family, which he hoped would continue to inspire future generations.

Nonetheless, the ADC governorship hopeful prayed that God would grant the departed eternal rest and comfort Hon. Amaechi and every member of the deceased’s family during this sad period of mourning.

He also urged members of the ADC across the country to stand in solidarity with the party’s vice-presidential candidate and his family in their momentofgrief over the passing of their beloved mother.

World.title: Illicit Drugs: Delta Police Arrest 22 Suspects, Rescue Two Minors
World.content:
Omon-Julius Onabu in Asaba

The police in Delta State said that they arrested at least 22 suspects, made up of 19 men and three women, during raids on certain illegal drug spots in the southern and central parts of the state.

Two minors, whose identities were undisclosed, were also rescued from the illicit drug dens during the series of operation, the state police command spokesman, Mr Bright Edafe, a superintendent of police, said in Asaba.

Edafe said in a statement, “The Delta State Police Command has recorded another significant breakthrough in its sustained campaign against illicit drug trafficking and related crimes with the arrest of twenty-two (22) suspects and the rescue of two minors during an intelligence-led operation across Ozoro and Abraka.

“On Tuesday, July 2026, at about 1500 hours (3.pm local time), the Deputy Commissioner of Police, Department of Operations, led operatives of the command on a coordinated raid of identified illicit drug dens and criminal hideouts at Ofagbe Community, Ozoro, Ekrejeta, and the NUT Area, Abraka, following credible intelligence.

“The operation led to the arrest of 22 suspects, comprising 19 males and three females, for offences relating to the sale, possession, and distribution of illicit drugs.

“During the operation, operatives also rescued two minors who were found in a suspected drug den allegedly operated by their father. The children have been taken into protective custody.”

Edafe further said that the minors would be handed over to the relevant authorities of the Delta State Government “for appropriate care and safeguarding” as investigation into the matter continued.

He noted that the Delta State Commissioner of Police, Mr Yemi Oyeniyi, “described the use of minors in environments associated with illicit drug activities as deeply disturbing”.

Oyeniyi assured that the state police command would leave no stone unturned towards “dismantling drug networks and protecting vulnerable persons,” he said.

Nevertheless, the police commissioner chared parents, guardians and community leaders to remain vigilant and continue supporting the police with credible information, assuring that the command will sustain intelligence-led operations to rid Delta State of illicit drug activities and other forms of criminality.

World.title: Oborevwori Inaugurates Political Appointees, Charges Them on Integrity, Accountability
World.content:
Omon-Julius Onabu in Asaba

Delta State Governor, Hon. Sheriff Oborevwori, has inaugurated new appointees with a charge to public office holders to uphold the highest standards of integrity, professionalism and accountability in the discharge of their duties.

Their appointments was intended to strengthen governance and advancing equitable development across the state.

The governor gave the charge during the swearing-in of Mr Brave Enodeh and Mr Moses Ogodo as Commissioners and members of the State Executive Council; Mr Cosmas Igbenije as a member of the Governing Board of the Delta State Oil Producing Areas Development Commission (DESOPADEC); and Chief Joseph Ojobu, Chief James Obeuwou and Mr. Fun-Ebi Edonyabo as members of the Delta State Judicial Service Commission.

Oborevwori noted that Enodeh and Ogodo were appointed following the resignation of two former commissioners who resigned to contest elections into the Delta State House of Assembly.

He stressed the need for the new appointees to demonstrate leadership, integrity, professionalism and unwavering commitment to duty in order to strengthen democratic institutions in the state.

He said their responsibilities extend beyond policy formulation to ensuring transparency, accountability and fairness in the conduct of the commission’s affairs.

Oborevwori said, “Your actions should inspire public confidence and reinforce our administration’s commitment to the MORE Agenda”.

Congratulating Mr. Igbenije on his appointment to the DESOPADEC Governing Board, Oborevwori urged him to justify the confidence reposed in him through discipline, dedication and commitment to the development of oil-producing communities.

He recalled that the tenure of the current DESOPADEC Governing Board was recently extended by one year to ensure continuity in the implementation of ongoing programmes and the effective discharge of the commission’s statutory responsibilities.

According to him, the board has recorded significant achievements in the provision of roads, classroom blocks, markets, health centres, electricity infrastructure, water projects and other community development initiatives across oil-bearing communities.

The governor expressed confidence that the board would consolidate on its achievements by expanding infrastructural development and deepening human capital development, while urging members to continue involving host communities in decision-making so that projects reflect the aspirations of the people.

To the newly inaugurated members of the Delta State Judicial Service Commission, Oborevwori said thatvonly men and women of proven integrity and unquestionable character could be entrusted with the constitutional responsibility of overseeing the appointment, promotion, discipline and welfare of judicial officers.

He urged the commission to discharge its responsibilities with fairness, impartiality, transparency and the fear of God to sustain a corruption-free, independent and effective judiciary.

The governor restated his administration’s commitment to inclusive governance and assured Deltans of his government’s continued partnership with the judiciary to strengthen the justice sector and make it a model for other states.

Responding on behalf of the appointees, Mr. Brave Enodeh thanked Governor Oborevwori for finding them worthy to serve in his administration, pledging the commitment of the new appointees to the governor’s vision of accountable and people-driven governance in line with the M.O.R.E. Agenda.

World.title: Infrastructure, Blue Economy to Headline Delta 2026 Summit
World.content:
Omon-Julius Onabu in Asaba

Secretary to the Delta State Government (SSG), Dr Kingsley Emu, on Wednesday in Asaba, asserted that the state was deliberately positioning itself as Nigeria’s burgeoning investment hub by leveraging on large-scale systematic infrastructure development, abundant natural resources, reliable power supply and strategic maritime assets.

Briefing newsmen on the forthcoming Delta State Economic and Investment Summit 2026 slated for 3rd-5th August in Asaba, Emu explained that the Oborevwori administration has laid a solid foundation for industrialisation through sustained investments in roads, bridges, power and transport infrastructure.

The government has constructed and rehabilitated over 2,600 kilometres of roads and more than 20 bridges, opening up rural communities, reducing transportation costs and connecting economic corridors across the state, he said.

The SSG identified as one of the pillars of the economy, the Delta Special Economic Zone, which offers investors access to some of the cheapest and most reliable power supply in Nigeria due to its proximity to the OB-3 gas pipeline.

Dr Emu said, “The infrastructure has been provided. Government has created the enabling environment. Investors can come into Delta and enjoy competitive energy costs that many other states cannot offer.”

Emu disclosed that the state already operates an independent power infrastructure supplying about 8.5 megawatts of electricity to government facilities and public institutions, while ongoing electricity sector reforms would further expand access to affordable power for industries.

He also highlighted Delta’s strategic maritime advantages, noting that the state boasts of four seaports, two airports and a 163-kilometre Atlantic coastline, making it one of Nigeria’s most strategically located investment destinations.

According to him, the administration intends to unlock the vast economic opportunities within the blue economy by promoting aquaculture, commercial fishing, fish feed production, cold-chain logistics, seafood processing and marine transportation.

He noted that Delta possesses one of West Africa’s largest concentrations of fish ponds around the Ekpan and Ugborikoko axis, where fish farming has transformed livelihoods and created sustainable employment for thousands of residents.

Beyond the blue economy, Emu said Delta is richly endowed with commercially viable deposits of coal, lignite, kaolin and silica, which present significant opportunities for mining, manufacturing and power generation.

He explained that coal mined in parts of the state currently supplies major cement manufacturers, while proposals were underway for coal-based electricity generation to support industrial expansion.

The SSG said the state government had spent the last three years engaging investors across China, Brazil and other strategic markets to market Delta’s investment opportunities.

He disclosed that direct investment engagements in São Paulo had yielded positive results, with Brazilian companies expected to participate in the summit, while Chinese businesses had also indicated strong interest.

Emu said the state had developed comprehensive investment prospectuses and launched a dedicated summit website to facilitate investor engagement before and after the event.

He expressed confidence that the summit would mark a turning point in Delta’s economic transformation by attracting investments capable of deepening industrialisation, expanding exports and creating employment for the state’s youthful population.

“The opportunities are enormous. We have the resources, the infrastructure, the connectivity and the political will. What we seek now is partnership with investors who are ready to grow with Delta,” he said.

World.title: Oborevwori Mourns Delta Journalist, Dave Okpogadie
World.content:
Omon-Julius Onabu in Asaba

Delta State Governor, Hon. Sheriff Oborevwori, has expressed deep sorrow following the death of seasoned journalist and State Correspondent of News Direct, Comrade Dave Okpogadie, describing his passing as a huge loss to the journalism profession and the state.

Okpogadie died on Saturday after a courageous battle with jaw cancer that lasted for about two years.

In a statement by his Chief Press Secretary, Sir Festus Ahon, Governor Oborevwori extended his heartfelt condolences to the deceased’s family in Emevor, the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), Delta State Council and the entire media community..

He described the late Okpogadie as a consummate professional whose dedication, integrity and commitment to journalism earned him the respect and admiration of colleagues and the wider society.

He noted that the late journalist’s courage, resilience and unwavering faith throughout his prolonged illness served as an inspiration to many who stood by him during his difficult journey.

Governor Oborevwori prayed for the peaceful repose of the soul of the departed media veteran and asked God to grant his family, friends, colleagues and members of the NUJ Delta State Council the fortitude to bear the irreparable loss.

Meanwhile, a delegation led by the Chairman of NUJ Delta State Council, Comrade Churchill Oyowe, in company with the Asaba Correspondents Chapel Chairman, Comrade Ifeanyi Olannye and comrades Omon-Julius Onabu,, Efe Ogbo and Onomiguren Agbamu of Indigenous Chapel on Sunday, July 19, 2026, visited David Okpogadie’s residence at Azagba-Ogwashi in Aniocha South Local Government Area, to condole with relatives, including his sisters. who were still in his place.

Comrade Oyowe condoled the family and extended the union’s regrets and pains over Dave Okpogadie’s demise, assuring the family that the NUJ state council would be there to give the needed support to ensure a peaceful rite of passage for its late member..

However, he urged the family not to delay the burial process given his age and the fact that Okpogadie left behind an aged mother.

Comrade Okpogadie, who until his death on July 18, 2026, was a state correspondent of News Direct, having hitherto been was the state correspondent of ITV/Radio.

World.title: Shettima, Ministers, Sultan, Others Attend Burial of Ex-Finance Minister Abubakar Alhaji in Sokoto
World.content:
Onuminya Innocent in Sokoto

Vice President Kashim Shettima, on Thursday led a federal government delegation to Sokoto for the funeral of former Minister of Finance and Sardaunan Sokoto, Alhaji Abubakar Alhaji.

Alhaji Abubakar Alhaji died on Thursday at a hospital in Abuja. He was buried later in the day in Sokoto in accordance with Islamic injunctions.

The funeral prayer was held at the Sultan Bello Juma’at Mosque and was led by the Chief Imam of the mosque, Sheikh Muhammad Bello Akwara.

Shettima represented President Bola Ahmed Tinubu at the burial. He was accompanied by key members of the Federal Executive Council.

Also in attendance were the Minister of Labour and Employment, Alhaji Muhammad Maigari Dingyadi, and the Minister of Budget and Economic Planning, Senator Atiku Bagudu.

The Deputy Governor of Sokoto State, Engineer Idris Muhammad Gobir, represented Governor Ahmed Aliyu Sokoto, who is currently out of the country.

Prominent traditional and political figures also graced the occasion. They included the Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar, and the Speaker of the Sokoto State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Tukur Bala Bodinga.

Dignitaries from across the country converged on Sokoto to pay their last respects to the late elder statesman, who held one of the most revered traditional titles in the Sokoto Caliphate.

Tributes at the burial described Alhaji Abubakar Alhaji as a patriot, administrator and bridge builder. Speakers noted that his contributions to national development and to the Sokoto Sultanate spanned decades.

Alhaji Abubakar Alhaji served as Nigeria’s Minister of Finance and as Nigeria’s High Commissioner to the United Kingdom in the 1990s.

Prayers were offered for the repose of his soul. Dignitaries prayed to Allah to forgive his shortcomings and grant him Aljannah Firdaus.

World.title: Olaopa Proffers Path to Gainful Retirement
World.content:
The Chairman, Federal Civil Service Commission, Prof. Tunji Olaopa, has proffered measures that could be adopted for a gainful retirement after service.

Olaopa spoke at a senior citizens’ summit organised by the High-Tech Centre for Women & Youths (HTCNWY) in Abuja on Thursday.

Giving the keynote address at the programme with the

theme “Upskilling Seniors in Cottage Technologies for Sustainable Development & Energize Commercialisation Now”, Olaopa said that

the event resonated with him, being a senior citizen himself and given his experience of sudden retirement at the top level of the civil service after 30 years.

He said that the experience taught him the lesson of the need for proper preparation for transition to retirement life or, better still, gainful post-retirement endeavours.

Olaopa who was represented on the occasion by his Technical Special Assistant, Mr Chike Ogbechie, said that one of the areas of interest in his quest for reforms in the public service was that the wealth of talent, knowledge and capacities left in public servants are kept dormant and thus wasted in retirement.

For him, there is also the concern that except the cases of a few well- endowed and self-funded parastatals of government, the pensions of the vast majority of public service retirees are meagre and cannot sustain their lives meaningfully.

According to him, with the apparent extension of longevity due to improved healthcare, the need for the accumulation of assets and continued income generation for old-age care has become heightened.

“This is more so as the era of children as investment against old age is becoming outdated”, he said.

He noted that

studies on competencies in the public service have shown that for the majority of employees, skills acquired while in service are generally bureaucratic and peculiar to their employing organization and may not be relevant and marketable in the wider economy. He stated that the same observation had been made in respect of employees in staff function of large business organisations, and that even employees who belong to definite professions or technical vocations and who have some value to offer in the service sectors have found it difficult to transition into private business or self-employment without preparation.

Thus , for him, it is imperative to create a system whereby public servants, nay all career employees in all sectors, are to be prepared for post-retirement endeavours.

He listed the objectives of such a system to include keeping the retirees meaningfully engaged, for personal satisfaction, good health and longevity; enabling them to engage in substantial economic activities to at least augment their pensions; harnessing their capacities in contribution to the economy; and providing them the opportunity to mentor younger ones in their areas of competence and success.

He said that under the Federal Public Service Reforms, good practices around the world had been looked at and one of the findings was that it was feasible to give employees skills in entrepreneurship, through social assistance schemes, as part of a terminal benefit package. He said that the idea was practicalised by the Bureau of Public Service Reforms in 2006, through the one-week pre-retirement training for personnel exited in the rightsizing exercise of the Reform Programme. He said that the process was supposed to be adopted by all ministries, departments and agencies as a matter of course, but for one reason or the other it has not been operationalized universally. But he noted that in the Armed Forces, there has traditionally been the more structured preparation of discharged personnel at the Armed Forces Resettlement Centre. But he stated that these schemes had not been as successful as now envisioned. According to him, the practice in the civil service has so far been more of a re-orientation and motivational courses of short duration, carried out mostly in a short while before disengagement date and have no real skilling and practical content.

He suggested a wide spectrum of lessons that retirement preparation should cover: Skills in cottage industries, e.g. soap making; agriculture, including crop farming, livestock, fish farming, snail farming; small-time rental property and land investment; services like business centre/cyber café, laundry, restaurant, tailoring, facility rentals services; educational services like founding and running of schools and private lessons;

founding and running of cooperative societies;

financial investment and

entrepreneurship training; preparation of business plans; and accessing finance.

He said that the training should include hobbies like recreation, healthy living, community/religious services.

According to him, some of these require some period of period practice and exposure, which may not be ordinarily allowed in the current rules and regulation regime of the public service. Thus, to him, there is therefore a need for an intentional policy to bring about an impactful and sustainable retirement preparation system. He thus proffered a review of the Public Service Rules and staff conditions of service to liberalise the rules prohibiting private business by public servants while in service, especially as they affect officers who will retire in a few years’ time. He also urged the introduction of innovations in the rules of work to allow for flexitime, working from home and other elements of the new normal, to enable advanced-age employees to practise post-retirement business activities. He urged the creation of a

documented policy on retirement preparation,

engaging positively with training institutions, public entrepreneurship/employment agencies, NGOs like HTCNWY in retirement preparation programmes as MDAs may not be capable or disposed to conducting such programmes by themselves.

He also urged the creation of enablers for the success of retirees’ enterprises and endeavours, such as special windows for financial credit or grants, tax exemptions, targeted security protection, special preferential treatment by security/law enforcement agencies for retirees’ enterprises, among others.

Olaopa urged relevant NGOs like HTCNWY to proactively initiate moves on the above propositions for an effective and sustainable public-private system.

World.title: No home: Stellenbosch FC exiled to Durban
World.content:
The venue change comes after a shortage of available stadiums in the Western Cape. As a result, Stellenbosch will travel further than AmaZulu for a fixture they were scheduled to host.

GAVIN HUNT FRUSTRATED BY VENUE ISSUES

The club’s usual home ground, Danie Craven Stadium, is unavailable as it is being prepared for an international rugby tournament.

Athlone Stadium is also unavailable. It is being used by New Zealand’s All Blacks during their South African tour. Meanwhile, DHL Stadium is hosting a Currie Cup fixture between the DHL Stormers and the Sharks.



The lack of available venues forced the Premier Soccer League to move the match to Durban.

Head coach Gavin Hunt has expressed his frustration over the situation. The experienced coach believes the ongoing stadium problems have disrupted the club’s preparations.

Hunt also said the team could be forced to spend almost two months without playing a true home match. The situation will increase both travel demands and costs for the club.



STELLENBOSCH FC START SEASON HOMELESS

The venue problems come during a busy period for Stellenbosch FC.

The club has lost several key players ahead of the new Betway Premiership season. Thapelo Mokobodi has joined Orlando Pirates, while winger Langelihle Phili has reportedly completed a move to Kaizer Chiefs.

Those departures leave Hunt with the task of rebuilding his squad before the season gets into full swing.



Despite losing home advantage, Stellenbosch will hope to make a winning start when they face AmaZulu in Durban. The Cape side has enjoyed positive results in KwaZulu–Natal during previous tournament relocations and will be looking to continue that record.

World.title: One dead as Sea Point fire destroys top-floor flat (VIDEO)
World.content:
A man has died and a firefighter has been injured after a fire ripped through a top-floor apartment in Sea Point on Thursday afternoon. Image: Screengrab

A man has died and a firefighter has been injured after a fire ripped through a top-floor apartment in Sea Point on Thursday afternoon.

The blaze broke out at a residential building on High Level Road, prompting a large-scale response from City of Cape Town Fire and Rescue Services.

Dispatched to the scene

Fire crews from several stations were dispatched to the scene, where they encountered a challenging fire that caused the roof of the building to collapse.



According to City Fire and Rescue Services spokesperson Jermaine Carelse, emergency medical personnel performed CPR on an adult male who lived in the top-floor apartment, but he could not be revived.

“Medical staff performed CPR on an adult male who lived on the top floor, however CPR was terminated,” Carelse said.

Firefighters used a turntable ladder to direct water onto the flames from above as they battled to bring the blaze under control.



Investigation

Reports from the scene indicated that one firefighter was also taken to hospital after sustaining injuries while responding to the incident.

The fire was not yet contained at the time of the City’s latest update, with crews continuing to work to extinguish the blaze and prevent it from spreading further.

The cause of the fire has not yet been established, and an investigation is expected once the scene has been declared safe.



Authorities are expected to provide further updates as firefighting operations continue.

World.title: ‘Increase the working age to 70’: South Africans clash over pension age
World.content:
Team of construction workers in safety gear collaborating on a project outdoors in South Africa. Image: Pexels

A story on pensioner hardship published by The South African sparked a heated debate after a commenter suggested raising the retirement age to 70.

Tracey Ahmad argued that pensioners shouldn’t receive government support at 60 if they are still physically and cognitively able to work, suggesting the retirement age be pushed to 70 instead so they continue contributing to the economy. The comment drew five replies as South Africans pushed back.

A lifetime of contribution for pensioners

Erick Mabuela disagreed, saying it’s painful that senior citizens who worked their whole lives now earn less in retirement. He argued grant payments should match a basic living wage, pointing out many pensioners paid tax throughout their working years.



The suggestion landed in the same thread where Gail Mills described going to bed hungry most nights on her current pension, adding weight to arguments that pensioners are already struggling, raising questions about whether pushing retirement to 70 would help or hurt.

South Africans remain split on whether the answer lies in raising the retirement age or increasing the grant amount itself.
