El presidente de Ceuta había tratado de presionar al Gobierno central en su llamamiento esta mañana: “Hay que abordarlo desde esa perspectiva, como una emergencia nacional a través de una acción decidida, enérgica, proporcional, contundente, inmediata y que esté coordinada a través de un mando único”. Según sus cifras: en la última semana “han entrado 1.500 personas”, lo que “significa el equivalente casi al 2% de toda la población de Ceuta”. Y ha hablado de un ritmo de unos 300 al día, “y subiendo”.

Las cifras de la Presidencia de la ciudad autónoma indican que al menos, de todos los que han llegado, unos 700 son menores y más de 1.000 jóvenes esperan a las puertas del centro de acogida porque las instalaciones solo tienen plazas para algo más de 500.

Vivas había precisado que ha reclamado esta petición al Gobierno de España, con quien mantiene un “contacto permanente”, tanto “a través de la Delegación como de distintos ministros”. “Y espero que esa petición, sin defecto, haya encontrado comprensión”, había pedido el presidente de Ceuta, quien insistió también en que se actúe con acciones que tengan “la energía que requiere una crisis y una emergencia de esta envergadura, de esta magnitud y de esta naturaleza”.

En este contexto, había reivindicado la prioridad de “atender la saturación de los centros de acogida”, tanto en los de adultos, que son competencias del Estado, con “recursos provisionales y de emergencia”; como en los de menores que, en este caso, pertenecen a la ciudad autónoma, pero también necesitan “el apoyo financiero del Estado” para poderlo hacer. “Estamos en una situación de absoluta emergencia humanitaria y social”, recalcó.

02:26 Entrevista presidente de Ceuta Decenas de inmigrantes ilegales a su llegada a Ceuta, este jueves. Foto: Joaquín Sánchez | Vídeo: cadena ser

Dicho esto, Vivas también ha puesto el foco en “intensificar la colaboración” con Marruecos por “si se puede cortar esta entrada masiva”, además de reforzar efectivos y medios de las Fuerzas y Cuerpos de Seguridad del Estado, tanto en el ámbito fronterizo como en la seguridad ciudadana.

Sobre este punto, el Gobierno central ha respondido que, “el Gobierno de Marruecos está cooperando de manera leal y permanente con España y colaborando estrechamente para afrontar esta situación. La intervención de las fuerzas de seguridad marroquíes está deteniendo la llegada de numerosas personas que intentan acceder a Ceuta desde territorio marroquí”.

Vivas también ha hecho hincapié, “por todos los medios”, en modificar la ley tras la sentencia del Tribunal Supremo contra las devoluciones en caliente de los inmigrantes que intentan llegar a nado. El rechazo exprés solo es aplicable, según dirimió el tribunal a principios de este mes, “para aquellos que intentan hacerlo superando los elementos de contención fronterizos establecidos, como las vallas”.

El presidente de Ceuta ha afirmado que los flujos de entrada son “diarios”, con cifras que rondan unas 300 personas migrantes llegando a Ceuta al día. “Si esto no se corrige, si no se aplican de manera decidida, enérgica y contundente, a la vuelta de un mes estaremos como en mayo de 2021″, ha avisado, en relación con la crisis migratoria que vivió la ciudad aquel año. Los fantasmas de 2021, cuando al menos 5.000 inmigrantes lograron cruzar en un día bordeando el espigón, se despiertan ahora también con las declaraciones del presidente, recuerdan cómo entonces la llegada se produjo sin que las autoridades marroquíes opusieran ninguna resistencia y tras varias semanas en que Marruecos decidió tensar la cuerda diplomática con Madrid.

World.title: Máxima alerta en Ceuta tras el cruce descontrolado de miles de personas desde Marruecos deja al menos nueve muertos
World.content:
El audio de esta noticia utiliza una voz sintética generada por Inteligencia Artificial y podría tener algunas inconsistencias.

La Guardia Civil y los medios de emergencia, superados, solo se ocupan de los heridos

Miles de personas han cruzado sin control de Marruecos a Ceuta el mediodía de este jueves, caminando en tierra firme primero y sorteando a nado el espigón que marca la frontera. La madrugada, que había sido tranquila, con decenas de entradas a nado, se ha desbordado a mediodía. Los marroquíes eran una manifestación de miles de personas que entraban mojados y victoriosos como si celebraran un mundial. Se abrazan, piden ropa limpia para secar el móvil, gritan de alborozo, los unos. Otros, con los niños en brazos, siguen el camino buscando quizá el centro de acogida. La Guardia Civil y los medios de emergencia, superados, solo intentan ocuparse de los heridos. Al menos nueve personas han muerto intentando llegar. El Gobierno ha movilizado a última hora de la tarde a las unidades del Ejército de Tierra desplegadas en Ceuta para apoyar a los efectivos del instituto armado y el presidente Pedro Sánchez viajará este viernes a la ciudad autónoma.

Algunos marroquíes llegan exhaustos, moribundos casi, pero los más afortunados han cruzado en tromba la carretera que circula en paralelo al mar sin pararse a mirar el tráfico. “¡Viva España!“, gritan y tiran las chancletas al aire. En pleno asfalto, algunos migrantes se arrodillan para besar el suelo. Han llegado a tierra española, pero nadie sabe cómo se va a atender una emergencia humanitaria como la que está viviendo la ciudad autónoma en estos momentos. El centro de acogida lleva días sin dar abasto, con las puertas cerradas, sin plazas. Centenares, que por momentos serán miles, se arremolinan allí, en los alrededores. La multitud ha acabado con cualquier posibilidad de ordenar la acogida. Con los pies y las rodillas ensangrentadas de pegar contra las rocas, los muchachos, jóvenes en su mayoría, siguen su camino, descalzos. Han llegado.

Más información Centenares de inmigrantes llegan a nado a Ceuta, en imágenes

Esta última oleada llega tras días de emergencia en que Ceuta ha pedido ayuda a las autoridades nacionales. No se trataba de un repunte; la situación se asemeja más a la grave crisis de 2021, cuando unos 5.000 marroquíes cruzaron la frontera en un solo día, tensionando las capacidades administrativas españolas y las relaciones diplomáticas con el país vecino.

La madrugada no fue tranquila; llegaban decenas, pero más despacio, con el tiempo suficiente para que les ofrecieran agua y los guardias civiles, atentos y humanitarios en todo momento, los fueran reuniendo y acompañándolos hasta sus instalaciones con el objetivo de llevarlos al centro de acogida temporal. No todos se fiaban de los uniformados y algunos huían barrancos arriba. Antes del mediodía, los agentes ya habían dejado marchar de sus instalaciones en la frontera de El Tarajal a todos los migrantes acogidos de madrugada, centenares. Estos también han salido a la carrera, otra vez entre risas y vítores.

No estaban retenidos, solo recogidos en un intento de ordenar la situación, pero ellos no lo entienden, como tampoco entienden el español en el que les habla la policía (y estos, a su vez, no comprenden el árabe en el que les responden). Los inmigrantes llegaban cansados, pero felices de tocar la costa. El mar y la playa se llenan de flotadores, aletas y trajes de neopreno. Como ayer y antes de ayer, y quizá mañana.

Es una jornada más de una crisis que presiona a la ciudad autónoma desde hace por lo menos una semana. Las cifras de los últimos 10 días, cuando se hablaba de unas 2.000 llegadas, se han quedado de repente ínfimas. Juan Jesús Vivas, presidente de la ciudad, ha solicitado al Gobierno que declare la emergencia nacional y asuma el mando único. En una declaración solemne, ha pedido calma a la población y ha recordado a sus convecinos que no es la primera vez que Ceuta vive algo así y siempre lo ha hecho con entereza. “Juntos y unidos saldremos adelante”, ha concluido.

La alegría se va acabando cuando alcanzan el Centro de Estancia Temporal de Inmigrantes (CETI), donde centenares de jóvenes deambulan sin saber muy bien qué les espera. Preguntan a quien pasa por allí para qué sirve la pulsera que les han puesto, si podrán salir a la península, cuándo les darán comida o quién les puede curar una muñeca hinchada. Camiones de basura han llegado esta mañana al CETI, que está saturado de desperdicios y al borde de una crisis de higiene. Las puertas están cerradas y un caño de agua les sirve para asearse un poco. Allí las caras ya no son las mismas. Hay cansancio, incertidumbre y desesperación. Furgonetas de la policía, de la Cruz Roja y de abastecimiento alimentario se abren camino como pueden por la cuesta arriba que lleva al CETI.

00:52 Centenares de personas entran a nado por las costas de Ceuta Llegada de inmigrantes a nado a Ceuta, es imágenes. Foto: Joaquín Sánchez

El supuesto efecto llamada que, según algunos, ha supuesto la sentencia del Tribunal Supremo del 9 de julio que impide devolver de inmediato a los que entran a nado sin vulnerar los muros fronterizos, en contra de lo que se piensa, quizá no es tal efecto llamada. Cuando se les pregunta por ello, no saben de qué les hablan. El rechazo exprés solo es aplicable, según dirimió el tribunal a principios de este mes, “para aquellos que intentan hacerlo superando los elementos de contención fronterizos establecidos, como las vallas”.

No todos han llegado victoriosos, sin embargo. Algunos han muerto en el mar. Se dieron algunas cifras, que las organizaciones cifran en más de 30 fallecidos en lo que va de año, sin que hayan podido contabilizar los cadáveres de estas últimas oleadas. Los que llegan al CETI lo certifican y lo relatan con horror.

World.title: Las imágenes de la llegada masiva de inmigrantes a la frontera de Ceuta con Marruecos: a nado y saltando las vallas
World.content:
La llegada masiva a pie y a nado de migrantes a Ceuta

Las imágenes de la llegada masiva de inmigrantes a la frontera de Ceuta con Marruecos: a nado y saltando las vallas

Entre la oleada de personas que ha cruzado a territorio de España y ha superado los medios de la Guardia Civil hay niños, jóvenes y familias

World.title: Marruecos se inhibe ante la llegada de miles de jóvenes a Ceuta
World.content:
“Es un fracaso para Marruecos ver a una chica haciendo la señal de la victoria tras haber pasado a Ceuta, es el fracaso de la política de este país”. Jadiya Inani, responsable de Migraciones de la Asociación Marroquí de Derechos Humanos (AMDH, organización de izquierda) se refiere a la imagen de una joven llamada Farah, que celebra su llegada a Ceuta enfundada en un traje de neopreno, difundida de forma viral en las redes sociales del país magrebí.

Oficialmente, las autoridades de Rabat se inhiben sobre la crisis de la frontera ceutí, sin precedentes desde la llegada a la ciudad autónoma de miles de migrantes irregulares en mayo de 2021. Centenares de familias siguen con inquietud el paso masivo de jóvenes por la frontera, sin saber el paradero de sus hijos. Fuentes en la frontera constatan que la policía marroquí mira para otro lado ante el cruce irregular de la frontera.

“Es una crisis esencialmente marroquí”, explica Inani, veterana activista en defensa de los derechos humanos. “Miles de jóvenes quieren huir del país a causa de la difícil situación económica y social. Más de 1,5 millones de ellos, de entre 15 y 25 años, ni estudian ni trabajan según las estadísticas públicas, y han caído en situación de vulnerabilidad”, advierte.

Considera también que es una crisis migratoria para con España y la UE, que en su opinión han endurecido las condiciones de emigración legal y externalizado el control de los flujos migratorios en los países del sur, donde son más bajos los estándares de derechos humanos y la libertad de expresión se ve constreñida.

“No es la primera vez que esto ocurre en Ceuta”, puntualiza. “Además de la grave crisis de mayo de 2021, en septiembre de 2024 se produjeron varios intentos de asalto a la valla de Ceuta”, recuerda. En esa última ocasión fueron frenados por un gran despliegue de seguridad marroquí por vía terrestre. Ahora las entradas masivas han comenzado a través del mar.

Más información Centenares de inmigrantes llegan a nado a Ceuta, en imágenes

“Cientos de familias buscan a sus hijos desaparecidos en el norte de Marruecos sin encontrar una respuesta”, señala la responsable de migraciones de la AMDH. “No hay cifras oficiales de desaparecidos, pero algunos medios hablan de centenares de jóvenes que han partido desde Marruecos y que no han podido llegar a nado hacia Ceuta. Sin embargo”, matiza, “muchos han sido rescatados por barcos de la Marina Real, que está colaborando en el control de la crisis”. Inani lamenta que en Marruecos se esté tratando con sordina la crisis como si fuera un suceso, en vísperas de las elecciones legislativas convocadas en septiembre.

“En lugar de encontrar una situación estable de estudios o trabajo para continuar su vida con dignidad en Marruecos, los jóvenes huyen a Europa, a pesar de que saben que en muchas ocasiones no son bien recibidos”, destaca. Los jóvenes se echan al agua y abandonan sobre la arena su calzado y sus enseres, señalan observadores desde Findeq (Castillejos) en el lado marroquí de la frontera ceutí. Apenas 40 kilómetros más al sur, en Mdiq (Rincón), el rey Mohamed VI celebra este jueves el 27º aniversario de su reinado con grandes fastos. En un discurso a la nación difundido la noche del miércoles, el monarca no mencionó la crisis de la frontera ceutí.

Mundial de Fútbol de 2030

El Gobierno de Marruecos parece tener otras prioridades, a las que dedica miles de millones, como organizar el Mundial de Fútbol o la demolición de barrios populares enteros para construir nuevas infraestructuras ligadas a eventos internacionales del deporte”, cuestiona la política oficial. Sostiene que la sanidad, la educación, el empleo y la vivienda han quedado relegados, y que así lo reconocen organismos de Naciones Unidas.

“Por eso se echó a la calle el otoño pasado la generación Z (de 15 a 30 años), para reivindicar necesidades clave”, argumenta. “Muchos de ellos se encuentran ahora entre rejas o perseguidos por la justicia, a veces solo por haberse expresado en las redes sociales”.

La reciente sentencia del Supremo que prohíbe las devoluciones en caliente de los migrantes irregulares que llegan a nado desde Marruecos se ha multiplicado en un efecto llamada en las redes sociales que ha tenido impacto también sobre decenas de menores. Se conectan a través de grupos en las aplicaciones de mensajería digital para coordinar los horarios de irrupción por los puntos que presentan menor vigilancia. El paso masivo de cientos de jóvenes contribuye a saturar los controles de las fuerzas de seguridad restantes.

“La avalancha por la frontera volverá a repetirse cada vez que los jóvenes vean una oportunidad de escapar”, concluye con un penoso augurio la activista marroquí Jadiya Inani. Esta última se produce unan semana después de la visita del presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, a Argelia, país vecino con el que Marruecos mantiene un antiguo contenciosos por el Sáhara que perturba el equilibrio regional en el Mediterráneo occidental.

World.title: La UEFA y sus federaciones nacionales acuerdan boicotear las competiciones de la FIFA por querer privatizar el Mundial
World.content:
Gianni Infantino, presidente de la FIFA, y Aleksander Ceferin, presidente de la UEFA, durante la 50.ª reunión del Congreso Ordinario de la UEFA en Bruselas , el 12 de febrero de 2026

El organismo rector del fútbol europeo toma la decisión de negar la participación de las selecciones en los Mundiales por unanimidad hasta que Infantino deje sin efecto su propuesta de privatizar la Copa del Mundo

La UEFA y sus 55 asociaciones nacionales han acordado por unanimidad no participar en las competiciones de la FIFA, tras la reunión convocada de urgencia para este jueves al mediodía. El órgano de gobierno del fútbol europeo, presidido por Alexander Ceferin, respondió con el boicot a la propuesta del presidente de la FIFA, Gianni Infantino, que el martes pasado presentó un proyecto para vender una participación de la Copa del Mundo a inversores particulares seleccionados por una empresa muy próxima a la familia de Donald Trump, el presidente de Estados Unidos.

El choque entre la unión de federaciones de Europa y la unión mundial de federaciones, dos organizaciones sin ánimo de lucro domiciliadas en Suiza que regulan y administran gran parte de los beneficios del juego más popular del planeta, alcanza su punto culminante. La medida adoptada este jueves amenaza con una fractura sin precedentes en la historia de un campeonato que desde 1930 fue conquistado por Europa en 13 de sus 22 ediciones. De profundizarse el conflicto, las consecuencias adquieren repercusiones impensables. Por ejemplo, que las selecciones de España y Portugal no participen en la próxima Copa del Mundo, prevista para 2030, principalmente, en estadios de España, Portugal y Marruecos. Que ayer Infantino se encontrara en Rabat para asistir a la celebración del 27 aniversario del ascenso al trono del rey Mohammed VI parece todo menos una coincidencia.

“La UEFA y sus asociaciones nacionales no participarán en competiciones de la FIFA”, rezó el comunicado oficial. “La UEFA y sus 55 asociaciones se plantan como uno solo. Por unanimidad y de manera inequívoca rechazamos la propuesta de la FIFA de transferir la propiedad del Mundial y de otras competiciones de la FIFA a inversores privados”.

“Ninguna de las 55 selecciones nacionales de la UEFA participará en ninguna de las competiciones de la FIFA mientras estas propuestas permanezcan en pie”, concluyó el texto, “a menos que estas propuestas sean abandonadas en su totalidad y se presenten garantías de que la FIFA nunca más abrirá su gobernanza o sus competiciones a la propiedad privada”.

El martes pasado Infantino presentó un proyecto que incluía la creación de una empresa subsidiaria que acogería los derechos del Mundial previa venta de una participación por valor de 4.000 millones de dólares a inversores privados. Estos inversores serían seleccionados por Thrive Capital, empresa propiedad de Joshua Kushner, hermano de Jared Kushner, el yerno de Trump.

Infantino propuso a las 221 federaciones nacionales que integran la FIFA que aceptaran el plan y a cambio les prometió multiplicar la financiación. El presidente de la FIFA, que hace alarde de su amistad con Trump, repitió que creía en los procesos “democráticos”. Pero exigió velocidad. El miércoles, presentó un ultimátum a las 211 federaciones nacionales. Si antes del 19 de septiembre respondían afirmativamente, recibirían 40 millones de dólares cada una; si se negaban, la financiación se les quedaría en 2,7 millones de dólares, un 75% menos.

“Intimidación”

El comunicado de la UEFA criticó la forma de lo que parece un chantaje. “Las asociaciones nacionales de todo el mundo han sido abordadas con un ultimátum”, dice el escrito; “o aceptan la captura irreversible de la mayor competición del fútbol o aceptan las consecuencias. Esto no es una decisión democrática, es gobernar mediante la intimidación. Un acto de coerción impropio de una institución encargada de velar por el fútbol mundial".

“Es irresponsable e indefendible”, apunta, “que una propuesta tan significativa para el fútbol haya sido concebida en secreto y sacada a la luz de repente sin ningún procedimiento comprensible de consultas con los actores encargados de velar por el juego. No se trata solo de un profundo fallo de liderazgo, sino de la abdicación del deber de la FIFA de custodiar el fútbol mundial”.

La UEFA y la CONCACAF, la organización de asociaciones de fútbol de Norteamérica, Centroamérica y el Caribe, se han opuesto más o menos frontalmente a Infantino. Nada se sabe, sin embargo, de la CONMEBOL, la organización que engloba al fútbol de Sudamérica, ni tampoco de la confederación de África. Gobiernos y federaciones de Francia, Reino Unido e Italia se han manifestado en contra del plan de Infantino. Otro tanto ocurrió este martes en la Comisión Europea, en donde el comisario europeo de Juventud, Cultura y Deporte, Glenn Micallef, se opuso enérgicamente a la privatización del Mundial e incluso advirtió que estudiaría medidas legales para exigir responsabilidades a la FIFA.

Las manifestaciones en Europa contrastan con el silencio ibérico. Ni el Gobierno español ni la federación española de fútbol, organizadores del Mundial 2030, se han pronunciado por el momento. Este periódico se ha puesto en contacto con la oficina del presidente de la federación española, Rafael Louzán, sin obtener respuesta, de momento. Solo Javier Tebas, el presidente de la Liga, que además es ejecutivo de UEFA, se ha pronunciado vehementemente contra la empresa que promueve Gianni Infantino.

World.title: La Justicia investiga a la portavoz de Vox en el Parlamento de Cantabria por el uso de un bolígrafo espía
World.content:
El juez aprecia indicios de un presunto delito de descubrimiento y revelación de secretos tras analizar audios hallados en un dispositivo localizado en el despacho del grupo parlamentario

La Justicia da un paso más en la investigación abierta a raíz del uso de un bolígrafo espía en el seno del grupo parlamentario de Vox en Cantabria, totalmente fracturado. Se trata de un caso denunciado por dos diputados y dos asesores de la formación y que ahora salpica directamente a la portavoz, Leticia Díaz. El titular del Juzgado de Instrucción número 2 de Santander ha acordado dirigir el procedimiento contra la portavoz en la cámara autonómica al apreciar indicios de un presunto delito de descubrimiento y revelación de secretos.

La decisión se recoge en un auto dado a conocer este jueves por el Tribunal Superior de Justicia de Cantabria (TSJC), en el que el magistrado acuerda citar a la dirigente en calidad de investigada tras el análisis del contenido almacenado en el dispositivo, que fue presuntamente utilizado para grabar conversaciones de los diputados de Vox denunciantes y con los que la actual portavoz mantiene un evidente enfrentamiento desde el inicio de la legislatura.

Más información Una jueza propone sentar en el banquillo a dos ultraderechistas por atacar con explosivos la sede del PSOE de Santander durante una charla

Según la resolución, el bolígrafo contenía 25 archivos de audio y en tres de esas grabaciones aparece una mujer cuya voz ha sido identificada por tres personas como la de la portavoz parlamentaria.

Esperaban grabar “grandes cosas”

De acuerdo con el instructor, el contenido de esas conversaciones permite concluir, de forma indiciaria, que la dirigente conocía la existencia del bolígrafo grabador, sabía cómo funcionaba y mostró interés por los resultados que pudiera ofrecer. En una de las grabaciones, según recoge el auto, puede escucharse una referencia a que del dispositivo podrían obtenerse “grandes cosas”, una expresión que el magistrado incorpora a su argumentación para justificar la ampliación de la investigación.

La resolución judicial no se limita al contenido de los audios. El juez considera relevante el contexto interno en el que se produjeron las grabaciones. En el auto recuerda que existía una situación de enfrentamiento político dentro del grupo parlamentario de Vox que afectaba tanto a los diputados como a los asesores de la formación. Esa rivalidad interna ya había aflorado públicamente y constituye uno de los elementos que el instructor tiene en cuenta para valorar los indicios existentes.

Otro de los aspectos subrayados por el magistrado es la relación profesional entre la portavoz y el asesor que ya se encontraba investigado en la causa. Según recoge la resolución, los propios denunciantes reconocieron que ese trabajador desempeñaba en aquellos momentos su labor casi en exclusiva para la portavoz parlamentaria. A juicio del instructor, esa circunstancia, unida al contenido de las grabaciones y al contexto de enfrentamiento interno, justifica la necesidad de incorporarla formalmente al procedimiento.

La investigación se inició a raíz de la denuncia presentada por dos diputados y dos asesores de Vox. Los denunciantes acudieron a la Justicia después de localizar un bolígrafo grabador sobre la mesa de trabajo del asesor posteriormente investigado, en el despacho que compartían varios trabajadores del grupo parlamentario.

Según hicieron constar en su denuncia, sospechaban que el dispositivo podría haberse utilizado para registrar de forma oculta conversaciones mantenidas en el despacho con el objetivo de perjudicar a determinadas personas en el marco de las discrepancias internas existentes en la organización.

Diputados de Vox enfrentados

La crisis estalló hace dos años con la división del grupo parlamentario en torno a dos bloques enfrentados, liderados por la portavoz Leticia Díaz y, por otro lado, los entonces diputados Cristóbal Palacio y Armando Blanco, una situación que obligó incluso a la dirección nacional a intervenir y supervisar la actividad del grupo.

Ahora, la investigación sobre el denominado caso del ‘bolígrafo espía’ vuelve a situar el conflicto en primer plano.

Esta decisión judicial va a tener un efecto relevante a la hora de elegir a la persona que encabece la candidatura autonómica de Vox en Cantabria, una formación que actualmente preside la concejala del Ayuntamiento de Santander Laura Velasco, pero que no tiene un liderazgo definido, más allá de la portavocía parlamentaria que ejerce Leticia Díaz.

World.title: Aquella tarde con Manolo
World.content:
No mejoraba los diálogos porque quisiera dejar su huella, los mejoraba porque entendía a los personajes mejor que nadie

Texto en el que el autor aboga por ideas y saca conclusiones basadas en su interpretación de hechos y datos

Todos los guionistas tenemos pánico a que un actor nos llame diciendo que quiere mejorar el guion. Y eso es porque no hay tantos actores como Manolo Solo.

No quiero que parezca que digo esto porque se nos acaba de ir. No lo diría si no tuviera pruebas. Fue hace un par de años, estábamos preparando la serie Celeste y Manolo tenía dudas con algunas frases de Tony, el paparazzo que interpretó en la primera temporada. Me dijo que fuera a su casa. Ni siquiera a una cafetería. Directamente a su casa.

Hoy pienso mucho en él, pero sobre todo en aquella tarde en la que le visité. Estábamos en su salón, junto a su perro. Manolo empezó a leer los guiones y a decir sus frases en voz alta. Pero no las decía como estaban escritas, las decía de otra manera. A su manera. Las decía mejor. Empecé a cambiar las líneas que estaba diciendo Tony. Porque en aquel momento ya no era Manolo Solo el que las decía.

Aquella tarde fue la primera vez que le dije algo que luego le dije muchas más veces. Le dije que era buen guionista. Aquella tarde todavía no éramos amigos, pero tal vez fue el día en que empezamos a serlo. Para mí, si me metes en tu salón y me dejas acariciar a tu perro, lo siento pero ya tenemos una amistad.

Y entonces surgió el problema. Dejó de ser Tony para volver a ser Manolo. Había una frase que se le atascaba. En un momento del guion, Tony se despedía por teléfono diciendo “Te como la cara”. Manolo no la veía. Me decía que para él un “Te como la cara” no se podía decir así como así, que era una frase que escondía mucho sentimiento. Buscamos alternativas. Estuvimos un rato. Yo ya no sabía qué más proponerle. Creo que lo notó porque me dijo que no me preocupara. Que la defendería como yo la había escrito.

Eso me dijo. Nos habíamos hecho amigos.

Aquella tarde entendí que Manolo no mejoraba los diálogos porque quisiera dejar su huella, los mejoraba porque entendía a los personajes mejor que nadie. Manolo se puede marchar tranquilo porque se lleva una carrera llena de roles increíbles, pero yo estoy peor sin él. Me da mucha rabia que lo perdamos justo cuando le llegaban los protagonistas. Tanta rabia como darme cuenta ahora de que Manolo tenía razón aquella tarde en el salón de su casa.

“Te como la cara” no es una despedida cualquiera. Es una frase que solo se puede decir bien cuando realmente quieres mucho a alguien.

Hasta siempre, Manolo.

Te como la cara.

World.title: One person dies, six injured in crash between lorry and minibus
World.content:
One person has died and six others have been seriously injured in a head-on collision between a minibus and a lorry in Overijssel.

The crash happened on the N48 near Balkbrug, around 20km east of Zwolle, at around 11.30am on Thursday. All the victims were sitting in the minibus, which had Belgian numberplates.

Fire appliances, ambulances and an air ambulance were called to the crash site. Six passengers were taken to different hospitals in the area, while the seventh was pronounced dead at the scene. The lorry driver was unharmed.

The road is likely to be closed for several hours while police carry out investigations and the road is cleared of debris.

World.title: University launches ethics probe into Red Bull professor’s work
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Utrecht University has begun an investigation into its pharmacology department after a professor was accused of not declaring payments for research from companies, including energy drinks manufacturer Red Bull.

Joris Verster published several papers on energy drinks and alcohol in his capacity as associate professor, without disclosing that he was also paid as a consultant for Red Bull and US-based Sen-Jam Pharmaceuticals.

The university does not prohibit consultancy work, but academics are required to disclose any relevant secondary activities when they publish papers under conflict of interest rules.

The investigation follows reports in several Dutch and international media outlets, including Trouw, De Groene Amsterdammer and Investico, that Verster’s research was published without any reference to his paid work for Red Bull and Sen-Jam.

Verster set up a private company, NeuroClinics, for his consultancy work, which frequently overlapped with his academic research.

Hangover pill

He carried out a study into a hangover pill produced by Sen-Jam which concluded, based on a questionnaire circulated around his students, that the medicine did not encourage people to consume more alcohol.

Mariëtte van den Hoven, professor of medical ethics at Amsterdam’s UMC medical centre, said Verster’s methods amounted to a conflict of interest “by using the university to promote your personal goals.”

Another study, published in 2010, concluded that drinking a can of Red Bull improved driving performance, based on observing drivers for four hours in a simulator. It was publicised under the heading “Can Red Bull fuel better driving?”

Verster also published research that disputed claims that mixing energy drinks with alcohol were damaging to people’s health and could lead to aggressive behaviour or unsafe sexual practices.

His conclusion was that combining the drinks meant users consumed less alcohol and were less prone to reckless behaviour.

Sick leave

Verster himself, who has been on sick leave since the start of May, told Trouw he had always been transparent about his private work.

“I have been a consultant for many companies and stated it in all my papers, even when it concerned a minor role,” he said. “I informed Utrecht University about my work as a consultant and the university approved it.”

World.title: Eighth species of American crayfish found in Dutch rivers
World.content:
A new species of crayfish has been found in Dutch rivers, the eighth type to establish itself in the Netherlands after being introduced in the upper Rhine.

The calico crayfish (Faxonius immunis), originally from North America, was spotted in Gelderland by ecologist Pim Lemmers, who first encountered the creatures in a nature reserve near Karlsruhe decades ago.

“I’d been expecting them and looking out for them for a while,” he told NOS. “Last year I found a crayfish pincer and I knew straight away that it might be a significant one.“

The discovery of the pincer, together with the results of DNA samples, are enough to confirm that the crayfish have made it to the Dutch river system.

The water authority in Rivierland has reported the presence of the crayfish to the food standards regulator NVWA, which will in turn notify the European Union, and triggered the protocol for dealing with invasive exotic species.

The Dutch agriculture ministry has set up a working group to investigate how the crayfish can be prevented from spreading. Crayfish damage the local environment by eating indigenous plants and animals and digging in river banks.

“We’re at a very uncertain stage, because are they just in the Klompenwaard area of the Rhine or are they already in our regional waters? Can we keep them out of the waters?” said José Vos, senior policy adviser for the water board.

World.title: Post-Covid fatigue not just caused by inactivity, study finds
World.content:
Patients with post-Covid syndrome suffer muscle damage that cannot be fully be explained by inactivity, research led by scientists at Amsterdam’s Vrije Universiteit (VU) has found.

The team compared the blood and muscle tissue of patients with long Covid and chronic fatigue (ME) with a group of healthy people who spent 60 days in bed as part of a study simulating the effects of space travel.

The post-Covid and ME patients had suffered from energy dips that caused them to avoid exercising or spend long periods in bed, which has a degrading impact on the skeletal muscles.

But the researchers, led by Rob Wüst, a movement scientist at the VU, found differences in the colour of the muscle fibres between the two groups, indicating that the post-Covid patients had a much lower oxygen capacity.

“As skeletal muscle characteristics differ between patients and healthy individuals after bed rest, physical inactivity cannot solely explain the lower exercise capacity and skeletal muscle adaptations in long Covid and ME/CFS patients,” they wrote in a paper published in Nature Communications.

The healthy individuals from the space programme still had bright red fibres, which are still oxygen-rich, while the patients had white fibres, which become exhausted much faster.

Rapid tiredness

The researchers said the difference could explain why post-Covid and ME sufferers become tired so quickly even after modest levels of exercise or exertion. “The redder the fibres, the more stamina a person has,” Wüst explained.

Lung specialist Merel Hellemons, of the Erasmus MC teaching hospital in Rotterdam, told the Volkskrant that the findings were a crucial development in understanding how to treat patients with conditions such as post-Covid syndrome.

“Many patients hear that they need to move more or that being less active is bad for them,” she said.

Wüst said patients should still be encouraged to be more mobile to avoid damage to their muscles, skeletons and cardiovascular system caused by inactivity. “The question is: what is possible? We need more tailored solutions,” he said.

World.title: Profits at KLM up in 2026 despite fuel cost increases
World.content:

Dutch airline KLM booked a higher-than-expected profit in the first half of the year, despite the rise in fuel prices caused by ongoing conflicts in the Middle East.

The company reported revenue of €6.9 bn in the six months to June, an 8% increase compared to the same period last year.

The airline benefited from a decrease in flights from competitors like Qatar Airways and Emirates because of the unrest in the region.

“The measures we are implementing are having a positive impact on our results,” CEO Marjan Rintel said in a statement.

Those measures included passing on higher fuel prices to customers, particularly on long-haul flights.

Yesterday, the Air France-KLM airline group announced they had put in an offer for a stake in Portugal’s TAP airline. Lisbon said last year that it was seeking a major international airline to buy most of the 49.9 percent stake that it planned to sell.

German airline Lufthansa also submitted a bid.

World.title: Man who strangled partner jailed after new forensic method used
World.content:
A man has been convicted of attempting to kill his partner in the first case to use new techniques to detect signs of strangulation in domestic violence.

The 33-year-old man from Rozenburg grabbed the woman by the neck as an argument turned violent last November. Police were alerted by neighbours and pulled the man away from his victim, who later said she was “turning blue”.

She was examined by a medical specialist using a new procedure developed in Rotterdam to gather forensic evidence faster in suspected cases of strangulation.

The doctor said the attack could have been fatal if it was prolonged, a detail that allowed prosecutors to argue that the attack should be classed as attempted manslaughter.

The procedure was introduced last December to try to detect strangulation, which is seen as an early warning sign of femicide, in domestic abuse investigations before the victim’s injuries heal and the evidence disappears.

200 referrals

The medical agency FARR, based in Rotterdam, anticipated receiving 200 inquiries a year, but was called on 150 times in the first three months. In 92% of cases doctors concluded the injuries could have been caused by strangulation. Nine in 10 victims were female and 78% of inquiries were related to domestic violence.

“It’s a huge number,” the agency’s managing director Geranda Zeelenberg told NOS. “Previously we hardly ever saw these people. They were probably always there, but the research we’ve begun has increased awareness of these cases.”

The man from Rozenburg was sentenced to 360 days in prison for attempted manslaughter, including 169 days suspended, and a community service order of 150 hours, in line with the prosecution’s demands.

His lawyer told the court he had no recollection of the events on the night of the attack because he had been taking alcohol and amphetamines, but argued that he had attacked her to try to force her to have sex rather than attempting to kill her.

World.title: Middle East conflict adds to pressure to fill Dutch gas reserves
World.content:
The Netherlands is lagging behind its European partners in filling its gas reserves for the winter, just as a key supplier in the Middle East has announced further restrictions on supplies caused by the conflict between the US and Iran.

QatarEnergy extended “force majeure” restrictions on its LNG cargoes until the end of September, affecting a total of 24 cargoes to European customers.

The company signed a contract to supply up to 3.5 million tonnes of liquified gas to the Netherlands per annum, which came into force this year, but the invocation of force majeure has put this commitment in jeopardy.

The Netherlands’ gas reserves are currently at 36.6% capacity, well below the EU average of 56%.

Following Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, which triggered a spike in prices, the EU set a target of reaching 90% capacity by November 1. Since then European nations have had to find alternatives to Russian gas.

The Netherlands achieved this level for the first three years, but in 2025 it peaked at just 74% and at the start of April this year the four Dutch storage facilities were at less than 5% capacity.

Energy minister Stientje van Veldhoven said last month she was “confident” that the gas reserves would be filled for the winter, but admitted that the government needed to be “vigilant”.

Demand for gas has also increased during the summer as more consumer and businesses install air conditioning, putting more pressure on energy.

The Dutch government also has agreements to buy gas from Norway and the United States, or could resort to the open market.

The wholesale price of gas on the TTF market, operated by Gasunie, has risen by 50% since mid-June as a result of ongoing attacks by Iran and the US on facilities in the Middle East and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: Sitting targets: thieves make off with 88 museum cafe chairs
World.content:

Thieves walked off with all of the chairs from the Bonnefanten Museum café in Maastricht in the early hours of Monday.

Café manager Freek Joosten told local news network L1 that camera footage showed the perpetrators making several trips carrying stacks of chairs at around 4am.

The designer seats are valued at more than €21,000.

The chairs were tied down with iron cables and the grounds are monitored by multiple cameras. The museum has reported the theft to the police.

The museum, which sits on Avenue Céramique in the Limburg capital, specialises in visual arts.

The terrace was recently renovated and the chairs were from designer Fermob Luxembourg. The thieves also took a waste container.

Visitors are still welcome in the café. Joosten has temporarily reallocated the chairs from his catering business to use on the terrace.

Police have asked anyone who saw anything unusual in the vicinity on the night of July 26 to 27, or who may have camera footage, to contact them.

Poland’s government has appointed a marketing and branding expert to develop a unified strategy for promoting the country abroad, saying the move will help boost tourism, support Polish products and attract foreign investment. Barbara Mróz-Gorgoń, a professor at Wrocław University of Economics, noted that her appointment signals “a shift” from simple promotional activities to “managing the reputation of our great country”. The move comes as Poland seeks to capitalise on its economic success, including growth in tourism and continued investments. But the government says that current promotion efforts lack a single strategy and are fragmented. Czas na markę Polska! Witamy na pokładzie prof. Barbarę Mróz – Gorgoń 🇵🇱 pic.twitter.com/PPX2eWTRSm — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) July 29, 2026 Last year, Poland’s sport and tourism ministry appointed Mróz-Gorgoń, who also advises companies and institutions on branding strategy and founded a think tank dedicated to promoting Poland, to an interministerial team tasked with developing a comprehensive new branding strategy for Poland. The government said, however, that efforts to promote Poland were so far fragmented and lacked a single strategy, which is why it created the post of commissioner for promotion of the Poland brand. As the first specialist to take the position, Mróz-Gorgoń will be tasked with preparing a strategy to build a national brand and help implement it, coordinate activities to help grow tourism, support investments, and improve Poland’s position on the world stage. “We will create one programme resulting in the joint promotion of our country’s brand,” said Tusk. According to the government, this will come at no further cost, but ensure that existing funds will be spent in a more “coherent and effective way”. Mróz-Gorgoń, meanwhile, noted that “the Poland brand is not the property of the government. It is created by entrepreneurs, artists, athletes, local governments and millions of Poles at home and abroad”. Developing this brand “means more investment, recognition of our brands and products abroad, and it also provides greater strength in international relations,” she continued. The growth has coincided with the international expansion of its firms, more foreign investments, and a rapidly expanding tourism sector. Last year, the sport and tourism ministry announced that it wants tourism to contribute 9% of GDP annually within a decade, from about 5% now, and for Poland to become a leader in the sector in central and eastern Europe. Foreign direct investment in Poland grew from just under 15.5 billion zloty in 2003, a year before the country joined the European Union, to around 61.3 billion zloty last year, according to figures from the National Bank of Poland (NBP). Various state and private companies – such as delivery giant InPost, insurer PZU, and train manufacturer Pesa – are establishing themselves abroad by buying some of their rivals. The international success of some Polish athletes – including football player Robert Lewandowski and tennis star Iga Świątek – has also helped Poland improve its international recognition. Prime Minister Donald Tusk said on Thursday that Polish airspace had been violated during a massive missile attack by Russia on western Ukraine overnight, adding that there were no casualties or immediate threat to civilians. A suspected Russian Kh-101 cruise missile crashed in eastern Poland, around 100 km from the Ukrainian border, prompting the deployment of police counter-terrorism officers and other security services to the site. The fall of the object, which is reported to have caused a powerful explosion, left a crater about 10 metres wide and scattered fragments in a field between Tarnawa-Kolonia and Tokary in Lublin province, about 2 km from the nearest buildings, according to local police. World.title: Record number of Poles opposed to Ukraine’s EU membership
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Support for Ukraine joining the European Union has fallen sharply in Poland, with opposition reaching a record high of 40%, a survey carried out by the Polish state research agency CBOS shows. The figures show that 50% of Poles still support Ukraine’s EU membership, but that is a significant decline from 74% in October 2023, when the question was last asked, and from a record 90% in March 2022, shortly after Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The shift comes as public sentiment towards Ukrainians in general in Poland has deteriorated in recent years. The latest CBOS poll shows that, among those who support Ukraine’s EU accession, most favour a gradual process, with 41% of all respondents saying Ukraine should join the EU but “without undue haste”. “Only 9% of respondents currently support Ukraine’s earliest possible EU membership, which is the lowest figure in the history of these surveys,” CBOS reported. Meanwhile, opposition to Ukraine’s EU membership has increased by 23 percentage points since October 2023, reaching its highest level in the history of CBOS surveys. People with right-wing political beliefs are most likely to be opposed to Ukraine’s accession (53%), while the age group with the highest percentage of people opposed is those aged 18-24 (58%). The survey also found that a majority of Poles expect the war in Ukraine to end with territorial concessions from Kyiv – 55% of respondents said they believed Ukraine would lose some territory, a view that has remained dominant since December 2024. Compared with the previous survey, however, pessimism has eased. The proportion of respondents who expect Ukraine to lose part of its territory fell by 8 percentage points, while the number expecting Russia to take control of the entire country declined from 8% to 6%. On Western support for Ukraine, 39% of respondents said the military, financial and humanitarian assistance provided by countries in the West was sufficient. Meanwhile, 27% said aid was excessive, while 22% said it was insufficient. Russia has published purported archival documents relating to massacres of Poles by Ukrainians in WWII. Kyiv had warned that Russia was planning to release the files in order to stir tensions, while Polish media note that the material contains nothing new https://t.co/CI0cfAlDle — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 6, 2026 Ukrainians are Poland’s largest foreign national group, with almost 1.6 million living in the country, but recent polls have shown growing hostility towards them, fuelled in part by anti-Ukrainian rhetoric from far-right parties and a tougher stance towards Kyiv from some opposition politicians. In its annual survey of attitudes towards national and ethnic groups, CBOS found earlier this year that the proportion of Poles who said they disliked Ukrainians increased by five percentage points this year, the largest rise recorded among all groups surveyed, reaching 43%. Tensions between the two countries have also been heightened by disputes over historical issues and a series of recent incidents targeting Ukrainians in Poland. The number of reported hate crimes against Ukrainians in Poland is up 30% so far this year, police data show. The figures come following recent high-profile cases of verbal and physical attacks against Ukrainians, who are Poland's largest immigrant group https://t.co/pcTsJddDz7 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 17, 2026 The number of reported hate crimes against Ukrainians rose by 30% in the first half of 2026 compared with the same period a year earlier, according to newly reported police data. Last weekend, three men were filmed violently attacking a Ukrainian woman and her partner outside a shop in Wrocław, apparently because of her accent. Two of the assailants have since been detained by police, while their victims required treatment in hospital. In response, Prime Minister Donald Tusk called for Poles to “wage war on violence”, saying that the perpetrators of such acts “have become emboldened precisely because they now have political role models, political patrons, and political support”. World.title: Newly sworn-in judge of Poland’s constitutional court stages boycott over blocked colleagues
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! A newly sworn-in judge of Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) has said he will refuse to sit on the court until four other judges appointed by parliament earlier this year, but blocked by the president, are allowed to take their seats. It is the latest development in a months-long dispute between the opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki and the government, which considers the TK to be improperly staffed and therefore illegitimate. Although Nawrocki swore in Sławomir Patyra, who was appointed by the ruling majority in parliament in June, as a TK judge on Tuesday, he continues to refuse to swear in four other judges appointed by parliament earlier this year. Po złożeniu przysięgi Patyra ogłosił, że zamierza odmówić orzekania. To gest solidarności z czwórką sędziów, od których prezydent nie chce przyjąć przysięgi https://t.co/jdbKusQ3H9 — OKO.press (@oko_press) July 28, 2026 Shortly after his swearing-in ceremony at the presidential palace on Tuesday, Patyra arrived at the TK headquarters in Warsaw, where he was accompanied by four other judges appointed by parliament this year, including two whom Nawrocki has refused to swear in. There, he announced that his decision not to sit on the court was a matter of loyalty to the constitution and his belief in judicial ethos. “I cannot imagine taking an oath today to uphold the constitution, only to start breaking that constitution tomorrow,” he said. Patyra told journalists that he would “submit a declaration of refusal to adjudicate” due to his solidarity with judges who are “unlawfully deprived of the chance to participate in the work of the tribunal”. He added that, along with the other judges chosen this year, he is “fully mobilised to restore the Constitutional Tribunal to its proper, constitutional, systemic form”. Under Polish law, when a vacancy emerges among the 15 positions on the TK, the lower house of parliament, the Sejm, chooses who should fill it. However, to take office, the judge must swear an oath before the president. In April, after the Sejm had chosen six candidates to fill vacancies on the court, Nawrocki took the unprecedented step of inviting only two of them to be sworn in. He argued there were doubts over the legality of how all six had been chosen, but decided to accept two to ensure the TK had the necessary quorum to function. Those two have been able to take up their seats on the court, but the other four remain in limbo. Although they arranged their own private swearing-in ceremony without the presence of Nawrocki, TK’s chief justice Bogdan Święczkowski has refused to accept them. In May, the European Court of Human Rights ordered that the quartet be allowed to take up their positions. But the TK – where judges appointed under the former Law and Justice (PiS) government retain a majority – issued its own ruling endorsing Nawrocki’s right not to swear in the new judges. The European Court of Human Rights has ordered Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) to accept four judges whom opposition-aligned President Nawrocki refused to swear in. The decision was welcomed by the government but rejected by the TK itself https://t.co/9NxInPdYk9 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 6, 2026 On 11 June, the Sejm then chose another judge, Patyra, to fill a newly opened vacancy on the court. In his case, the legal doubts Nawrocki had expressed regarding the previous appointments, which in some instances were made more than a year after the vacancies had arisen, did not seem to apply. Yet for weeks the president refused to confirm whether he would swear him in. That prompted Patyra to write to Nawrocki in early July and then again later in the month, asking the president to indicate a date on which he could take his oath. After repeated requests, Nawrocki finally decided last week to invite Patyra to the presidential palace. The president’s chief of staff, Zbigniew Bogucki, noted that “there were some doubts” but “the president dispelled them” and added that Patyra was chosen “in accordance with all procedures”. Nowo wybrany przez Sejm Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej uchwałą z dnia 11 czerwca 2026 r. sędzia Trybunału Konstytucyjnego Sławomir Patyra złożył wobec Prezydenta RP ślubowanie. pic.twitter.com/VLMRAIg1Yj — Kancelaria Prezydenta RP (@prezydentpl) July 28, 2026 The TK has been at the heart of the rule-of-law crisis that has developed in Poland over the last decade. In 2015, former PiS-aligned President Andrzej Duda refused to swear in three judges legally chosen by the Sejm. Shortly afterwards, PiS won parliamentary elections and nominated three replacements for those judges, who were sworn in by Duda. Those three judges and their successors have been deemed illegitimate in a succession of rulings by Polish and European courts. Due to their continued presence on the court, the current government, which replaced PiS in 2023, rejects the TK’s legitimacy and refuses to recognise its rulings. Under both Święczkowski, a former member of the PiS government, and his predecessor Julia Przyłębska, a close personal associate of PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński, the TK has been widely seen as issuing rulings aligned with the political interests of PiS. Former Polish Prime Minister Mateusz Morawiecki says that 40 MPs and one senator aligned with him will form their own parliamentary group, deepening a split in the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) after a dispute over party direction and loyalty declarations. The move marks the most serious internal challenge in years to PiS, which ruled Poland from 2015 to 2023, and follows months of tensions between Morawiecki’s more moderate faction and party conservatives who have pushed the group in a hard-right direction. Once formally established, Morawiecki’s caucus would become the third-largest bloc in the Sejm, Poland’s lower house of parliament. Powstanie klub parlamentarny „Rozwój Plus”. Morawiecki zdecydował#PAPInformacjehttps://t.co/IftRdgpIPw — Polska Agencja Prasowa/Polish Press Agency (PAP) (@PAPinformacje) July 29, 2026 One of Morawiecki’s allies, Marcin Horała, told reporters that the creation of the caucus did not mean they were leaving PiS, but “simply setting up a parliamentary group so that we can get on with our work”. He noted, however, that PiS’s parliamentary group “has stopped treating us as its members”. Morawiecki, meanwhile, said that his group remained ready to cooperate with PiS as a “second lung” of the party’s broader political camp, but suggested that the group was moving in a different direction. He said that parts of PiS’s messaging were increasingly influenced by “dissidents and schemers” as well as hardline factions, including Sovereign Poland (Suwerenna Polska), a nationalist group that was previously a junior coalition partner of PiS and often clashed with Morawiecki when he was prime minister. Reacting to Morawiecki’s announcement, party chairman Jarosław Kaczyński said the former prime minister had carried out a planned split of the party despite his efforts to reach a deal. “Until the end I made efforts to reach an agreement, unfortunately Mateusz Morawiecki clearly had his own political plan in mind, carried out on the basis of a split in PiS,” Kaczyński wrote on X. The announcement follows a dispute that began after Morawiecki launched his Development Plus (Rozwój Plus) association in April. The former prime minister insisted the association was intended to complement PiS with a pro-development agenda rather than rival it. However, critics within PiS viewed it as an attempt by Morawiecki to build an alternative power base that could eventually evolve into a separate party ahead of the 2027 parliamentary election. Seeking to end the standoff, the party ordered PiS lawmakers to resign from all outside political associations by last Thursday, or face “consequences” including “the loss of membership in PiS”. On Friday, Kaczyński said that “around 30 MPs” had failed to comply and had therefore effectively resigned from the party, adding that Tuesday’s meeting of the party’s political committee would simply confirm this fact. Poland's right-wing opposition PiS party is set to split after a more moderate faction of over 30 MPs loyal to deputy leader @MorawieckiM refused to sign a loyalty pledge demanded by leader @OficjalnyJK, who says that means they have effectively resigned https://t.co/TuqYpGI5ak — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 24, 2026 On Tuesday, the party announced that instead, the committee had referred the cases of 44 members, who either failed to submit the required declarations or submitted them on the wrong form, to the party’s disciplinary officer for individual review, delaying a final decision. “From a formal and legal perspective, Mr Mateusz Morawiecki has not yet been removed from the list of members,” PiS spokesman Rafał Bochenek said on Tuesday. PiS disciplinary officer Karol Karski told the Polish Press Agency (PAP) he would examine each case individually. “I am open to speaking with each of them so they can present their positions,” Karski said. “At this point, I can initiate proceedings against the individual in question, refer the case to a peer disciplinary tribunal with a motion for punishment – this could include a temporary suspension or expulsion from PiS.” PiS has for the last two decades been the dominant force on the Polish right, including periods leading governments in 2005-2007 and 2015-2023. However, since losing power at elections in 2023, when the party won 35% of the vote, the party has seen its average support in polls fall to around 23-24%, the lowest level in 14 years. Support for PiS has fallen to its lowest in 14 years, as the party grapples with internal division, the rise of far-right challengers, living in President Nawrocki's shadow, and the unpopularity in Poland of PiS ally Donald Trump, writes @danieltilles1 https://t.co/QRScBpEQQG — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 2, 2026 Meanwhile, it has been challenged by the rise of the far right, where two parties, Confederation (Konfederacja) and Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP), now together poll at a similar combined level of support to PiS. In response, Kaczyński in March named a hardline figure, Przemysław Czarnek, as PiS’s candidate for prime minister in next year’s elections. Czarnek was seen as someone who could appeal to far-right voters, while also potentially working with the far right if a coalition was needed after the elections. However, there has been no rise in support for PiS since Czarnek was named, prompting growing concern from more moderate figures within the party, led by Morawiecki. The national-conservative opposition PiS party has named its candidate to be prime minister if it wins next year’s parliamentary elections. Przemysław Czarnek is a hardline conservative who played a prominent role in PiS's campaign against "LGBT ideology" https://t.co/sSJLON00hW — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 7, 2026 They argue that PiS has wrongly disowned many of the successes of its time in office before 2023, and they fear that its rightward shift damages its chances of winning over more centrist voters. Adam Szłapka, the spokesman of the current more liberal government, said Braun was “the ultimate playmaker in this whole game”, who had helped push far-right rhetoric into the political mainstream. “The worst thing about this whole situation is that Poland’s largest opposition party has, in effect, started to adopt Grzegorz Braun’s agenda from A to Z,” Szłapka told broadcaster TVN24. Ostatecznym rozgrywającym w całej tej rozgrywce nie jest ani prezes Jarosław Kaczyński, ani Mateusz Morawiecki, tylko Grzegorz Braun – ocenił w #JedenNaJeden w TVN24 rzecznik rządu Adam Szłapka. World.title: Polish court finds regulation allowing foreign same-sex marriage registration unconstitutional
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) has ruled that a new regulation allowing the registration of foreign same-sex marriage certificates in Poland was partly unconstitutional, saying it went beyond technical administrative changes and conflicted with the constitution’s definition of marriage. The regulation, introduced by the digital affairs ministry after rulings by the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) and Poland’s Supreme Administrative Court (NSA), was due to take effect on 23 August. The government, which considers the court to be improperly constituted, says it will not implement the ruling. The government has issued a regulation allowing foreign same-sex marriages to be entered in the civil registry The decision comes in response to an EU court order and marks a major change in a country that does not allow same-sex unions under domestic law https://t.co/2an5mGtnHl — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 22, 2026 Polish law does not allow same-sex couples to marry or enter into civil unions, and a bill that would have granted such limited rights to unmarried couples was recently vetoed by the opposition-backed president. Until this year, same-sex couples who married abroad were also unable to register their marriage certificates in Poland. After the CJEU ruled that Poland must recognise such marriages, the digital affairs ministry changed civil status forms. Instead of separate fields for “man” and “woman”, the new templates use “man/woman”, allowing registry offices to record both opposite-sex and same-sex marriages. Lawmakers from the national-conservative opposition Law and Justice (PiS) party, however, challenged the regulation, arguing that the digital affairs minister had exceeded his powers because the changes were not merely technical but affected the legal definition of marriage. The tribunal, which is widely seen as being under PiS’s influence, agreed. The tribunal said the new forms allowed relationships that do not match the constitution’s definition of marriage as a union between a man and a woman to be recorded as marriages. It said regulations can only implement existing laws and cannot change matters reserved for the constitution or parliament. The tribunal also said that registering a foreign marriage certificate cannot produce legal effects that conflict with the basic principles of Polish law. It added that changing the constitutional definition of marriage would require amendments to the constitution and related laws. Some legal experts argue that, while the constitution states that a “marriage, being a union of a man and a woman… shall be placed under the protection and care of the Republic of Poland,” that phrasing does not rule out other legally recognised unions receiving state protection. Poland has begun recognising foreign same-sex marriages. But the legal consequences for such couples remain unclear, especially as Polish law does not allow any form of same-sex union We asked five experts for their view on what this will mean in practice https://t.co/h2KHmW8sMI — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 19, 2026 Shortly after the ruling, government members said they would not comply with the tribunal’s decision and that the regulation would enter into force as planned. “The illegal Constitutional Tribunal is once again attempting to obstruct a state that is enforcing the law in force and the rulings of European courts,” digital affairs minister Krzysztof Gawkowski said. “The transcription of foreign same-sex marriage certificates is and will remain legal,” he said, adding that 184 same-sex couples had so far had their foreign marriage certificates transcribed. Katarzyna Kotula, the government official responsible for equality issues, said the TK ruling on the issue of transcriptions “has no legal force whatsoever”. Nielegalny Trybunał Konstytucyjny po raz kolejny próbuje zatrzymać państwo, które wykonuje obowiązujące prawo i wyroki europejskich sądów. Transkrypcja zagranicznych aktów małżeństw jednopłciowych jest i będzie legalna. Rozporządzenie, które przyjęliśmy porządkuje dokumenty i… — Krzysztof Gawkowski (@KGawkowski) July 28, 2026 The TK has been at the heart of the rule-of-law crisis that has developed in Poland over the last decade. In 2015, former PiS-aligned President Andrzej Duda refused to swear in three judges legally chosen by the Sejm. Shortly afterwards, PiS won parliamentary elections and nominated three replacements for those judges, who were sworn in by Duda. Those three judges and their successors have been deemed illegitimate in a succession of rulings by Polish and European courts. Due to their continued presence on the court, the current government, which replaced PiS in 2023, rejects the TK’s legitimacy and refuses to recognise its rulings. Fifteen months since the change of government, Poland's rule-of-law crisis continues – indeed, many Poles think the situation has got worse.@J_Jaraczewski explains the roots of the crisis, what its impact has been, and how it might be resolved https://t.co/7KOCURV3dU — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 17, 2025 Under both Święczkowski, a former member of the PiS government, and his predecessor Julia Przyłębska, a close personal associate of PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński, the TK has been widely seen as issuing rulings aligned with the political interests of PiS. For a long time, the government refused to appoint new judges to the Constitutional Tribunal as the terms of the previous judges expired, with some vacancies remaining unfilled for over a year. In recent months, the government has resumed appointing new judges, but President Karol Nawrocki, an ally of PiS, is refusing to administer the oath of office to some of them. World.title: Residents oppose move to add Polish village to list of protected monuments
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A decision to designate a village as a protected monument has sparked fierce opposition from residents, who have vowed to “fight until the end” against measures they say will limit their ability to renovate and build on their properties. The village in question, Ostaszów in southwestern Poland’s Lower Silesia province, was established in 1936 by Nazi Germany as an agricultural settlement of around 42 farms. At the time, the region still belonged to Germany. The Lower Silesian Provincial Conservator of Monuments argues Ostaszów has “unique, homogeneous historical architecture” requiring state protection, but local officials say that the way the decision was made, despite opposition from residents, shows “the voice of local communities has no significance”. After World War Two, most of Lower Silesia, including the village, became part of Poland. The village’s architecture has remained largely unchanged, with its residential buildings connected to barns, forming unique cohesive farmstead units. Around 250 people live there. Earlier this year, the residents were told proceedings had begun to add the village to the register of protected monuments, reports the Gazeta Wyborcza daily. The provincial conservator said on Friday it had reached a decision. “The unique, above-standard historical, scientific and artistic value of Ostaszów as a monument cannot be questioned,” it wrote in a statement. It noted that a study by a team working under the culture ministry had found that the village was the only preserved settlement of its kind in Lower Silesia. Residents and local officials said they planned to appeal against the decision, arguing it would create additional bureaucracy and interfere with property owners’ ability to decide on building and renovation work. “We have a years-long legal battle ahead of us, but we won’t give up. We will fight until the end. We believe that decisions about the 42 homes in Ostaszów should be made by their residents, not by harmful officials,” residents wrote in a statement quoted by the Polish Press Agency (PAP). “In a cardboard state, the voice of local communities has no significance – only orders and bans count. Our future is to be decided by a heartless official from [the Lower Silesian capital of] Wrocław who does not even have time to meet with the victims of his decisions,” said the village head, Sylwia Mazur. Wieś Ostaszów wpisana do rejestru zabytków. Mieszkańcy będą się odwoływaćhttps://t.co/ZxmH2lbHnb pic.twitter.com/cPdL73PXIH — Dzieje.pl (@dziejepl) July 26, 2026 The conservator noted, however, that until the appeals process is concluded, construction works cannot proceed. It added that it planned to cooperate with locals to “develop principles of renovation and investment procedures in accordance with the regulations on the protection of monuments”. It also urged residents not to spread “scandalous narratives” about the decision leading to an “open-air museum, the impossibility of renovation, and the blocking of investments”. It said other villages in Lower Silesia were subject to similar protections without hindering their development. Gazeta Wyborcza cited some residents saying that the launch of proceedings in January had already forced them to pause work on their properties. Others complained that the decision will increase renovation costs due to strict conservation requirements. The Opole Provincial Conservator of Monuments said that, as of 2021, some 86 villages across Poland had been added to the register of monuments because of their historic layouts. World.title: Poland enters race to host EU-backed AI gigafactory
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Poland has joined the European Union’s plan to build artificial intelligence (AI) gigafactories with a view to hosting one of the bloc’s new computing centres. Deputy digital affairs minister Dariusz Standerski said Poland had completed a key legal step by joining the joint procurement process. The move enables Poland to bid for one of seven AI gigafactory projects planned under the EU programme, potentially attracting investment of more than 10 billion zloty (€2.3 billion) while giving businesses, researchers and public institutions access to advanced AI computing capacity. “On behalf of the Republic of Poland, I have signed the Joint Procurement Agreement, which means that Poland joins the AI gigafactory initiative,” Standerski told daily Rzeczpospolita. Under the proposed model, AI gigafactories will be designed, financed, built and operated by private consortia selected through a European tender organised by the European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU). In the first procurement round, EuroHPC JU plans to select seven projects comprising four medium-scale facilities and three large-scale sites. Poland is bidding for a medium-scale project, which would initially provide computing capacity equivalent to at least 25,000 AI accelerators before expanding to at least 75,000. The EU and its member states will support the projects by committing to purchase computing services during the initial years of operation, providing demand certainty for investors. “Poland and the EU will each buy 17% of the power, and the remaining two thirds will be made commercially available by a private consortium; Poland will commit to purchasing its own pool for five years,” Standerski said. Standerski also told the newspaper that companies’ interest in the project is “enormous”. “This means that, from the very first day the gigafactory is operational, part of its computing capacity will already have been sold,” he added. Poland’s government will spend 1.9 billion zloty (€437 million) equipping the majority of schools with so-called AI labs before the start of the next school year. The money will fund laptops, AI software and interactive displays, among other equipment https://t.co/outNQIGCv0 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 19, 2026 Standerski said the government would not designate a site for the facility, with the final location to be determined by the winning consortium through the European procurement process. He said the government had previously identified 10 locations across Poland capable of hosting. Last week, the deputy minister also said Poland was preparing to sign an agreement with the Czech government, under which cooperation would involve mutual purchases of computing capacity between the two countries. He also said Lithuania had committed to a one-sided arrangement to buy computing power from a Polish AI gigafactory. Częstochowa will become the first city in Poland to use the Polish Large Language Model to support the use of AI in providing municipal services. It will help write letters, analyse inquiries from residents, and summarise long documents https://t.co/SLrmVg9VBz — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 11, 2025 Earlier this month, Poland’s government approved a resolution enabling the country to participate in the European AI Gigafactory programme, committing more than 400 million zloty towards what the government says would be the largest computing centre in the country’s history. The government also pledged to purchase AI services worth €100 million between 2028 and 2033, with a matching contribution from the European Union. According to the government’s timetable, the European procurement process is expected to begin later this year. Bidding consortia will have 15 weeks to submit proposals, contracts are due to be awarded in early 2027 and the facilities are scheduled to become operational in 2028. 🚀 Droga do Gigafabryki AI otwarta.
