World.title: Iraq denies launching strikes from its territory against neighboring nations
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The military spokesperson for the Iraqi commander-in-chief, Sabah al-Numan, confirmed on Thursday that neither a foreign nor local body has presented proof that recent regional drone attacks were launched from Iraqi territory.

In a statement to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA), al-Numan urged accusing parties to submit reliable proof, saying that Baghdad has yet to receive such data.

The development comes following statements made by the Saudi Ministry of Defense, alleging that drone attacks targeting key oil infrastructure in the past few days originated in Iraq.

The Iraqi official indicated that the government will neither tolerate unilateral military acts from within its borders nor accept foreign violations of its territorial sovereignty.

Al-Numan’s remarks come a day after the United States and Saudi Arabia launched coordinated airstrikes targeting several bases of Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), killing and injuring many fighters.

The joint operation targeted several logistical and weapons storage locations in different provinces in Iraq, escalating the current regional battle.

The PMF described the joint US-Saudi strike as a dangerous escalation and a clear breach of Iraqi sovereignty.

World.title: Iraqi oil flows to continue via Turkey’s Ceyhan as renewal deal is discussed
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Turkish sources told Reuters that crude oil shipments from northern Iraq to the Turkish port of Ceyhan will continue while the two countries seek an arrangement to extend the pipeline’s operation for another 12 months.

On July 27, a bilateral agreement that had been in place for decades ended. Despite expectations, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi did not sign a 12-month renewal deal during his meeting with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan in Ankara on Tuesday.

According to a Turkish official, oil flows via the Iraq-Turkey pipeline, which is Baghdad’s only operational export pipeline, will continue while negotiations for a renewal deal are still in progress.

Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar recently announced a 12-month extension agreement between the two countries.

During a joint press conference in Ankara, Erdogan stated on Tuesday that Turkey hopes to finalize a comprehensive energy cooperation agreement as soon as possible.

An extension is intended to provide additional time for discussions on a complete accord. Turkey aims to fully utilize the 1.5 million barrels per day pipeline and consider expanding it to oil fields in southern Iraq.

Turkish data suggests that the pipeline currently transports approximately 170,000 barrels per day.

World.title: Turkey seeks comprehensive energy cooperation deal with Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan stated that Turkey hopes to finalize a comprehensive energy cooperation agreement with Iraq following discussions with Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi in Ankara.

Erdogan said that Turkey’s state-owned oil and gas company, TPAO, will operate at Iraq’s Kirkuk oilfield, which is now being developed by British Petroleum (BP), during a joint press conference following a signing ceremony that had been expected to extend the Kirkuk-Ceyhan oil pipeline deal for another year, according to Reuters.

The agreement to renew the decades-old pipeline contract, which regulates shipments along the strategic route, expired on Monday.

After signing three agreements, Erdogan noted that additional deals were anticipated. However, his ministers promptly briefed him on stage, and the two leaders continued with their statements without announcing any further agreements.

The agreement between Iraq and Turkey regarding the crude oil pipeline expired on July 27.

“Our goal is to complete an energy cooperation deal that benefits both parties as quickly as possible,” Erdogan said.

Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar said in a statement on X that TPAO has bought a 15 percent stake in BP Energy Company of Kirkuk Limited (BPECKL), enabling the Turkish business to operate in the sector.

Bayraktar explained the TPAO will cooperate with BPECKL to raise oil production at the Kirkuk field, which has reserves estimated at three million barrels.

World.title: Iraq’s oil exports to India fall as New Delhi diversifies import sources
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi oil exports to India fell in the first half of 2026, as Indian refineries diversified their crude import sources to minimize the geopolitical risks associated with shipping via the Straits of Hormuz.

According to officials at Indian refining companies and the Indian Ministry of Petroleum, the goal of this measure is to improve supply security.

The drop in Iraqi supplies to India comes at a time when the global oil market is under increased pressure due to security worries along critical maritime routes. This pressure is causing consumers in Asia to split their purchases among many producing countries.

Iraqi oil remains a vital resource for India due to supply security and the high quality of Basra crude.

Indian refiners confirmed they have secured their crude oil requirements until the end of September and have begun arranging purchases for the fourth quarter of the year, despite persistent concerns about the impact of any interruptions to shipping routes on global supply chains.

Meanwhile, Russia remained India’s top crude oil supplier in the first half of the year, while imports from the UAE and Brazil increased.

India’s purchases from Iraq and the United States fell as New Delhi attempted to diversify its supply sources and reduce the risks associated with reliance on a single source.

Indian refiners have warned that increased shipping risks and higher insurance costs, along with declining discounts on Russian oil, are affecting profit margins.

Experts anticipate that continuing instability in the Middle East will raise oil prices and pose new hurdles for Asian oil-importing countries.

World.title: Six Iranian advisors killed in US-Saudi attack on Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – A joint US-Saudi attack on targets in Iraq killed six Iranian advisors on Wednesday, according to two Iraqi officials who spoke to the Associated Press (AP).

A meeting that was set for Thursday in Saudi Arabia between Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman was called off due to recent attacks by armed groups targeting Saudi Arabia.

Al-Zaidi ordered an emergency meeting of Iraq’s National Security Council following the coordinated attacks on the country.

The Iraqi Security Media Cell said in a statement that the meeting was ordered in response to the evolving security situation and the airstrikes that targeted several Iraqi provinces early on Wednesday.

The US Central Command (CENTCOM) announced on Wednesday that US forces, in cooperation with Saudi armed forces, carried out precision airstrikes targeting sites linked to Iran-backed militias in Iraq.

The coordinated airstrikes were in retaliation for a series of drone attacks targeting US interests and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.

CENTCOM said in a statement that the strikes, carried out on July 28, targeted logistics sites and weapons depots allegedly used by Iranian-backed groups. It added that these groups were directed by the Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) to attack US forces and Saudi oil facilities.

US and Saudi fighter jets carried out the strikes, an operation described by CENTCOM as a strong response to more than 30 drone attacks that the IRGC had conducted in the past few days.

Headquarters and sites belonging to the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) in several Iraqi provinces were targeted by the US-Saudi airstrikes in the country.

World.title: US-Saudi strikes test Iraq’s fragile security balance
World.content:
Baghdad – US-Saudi strikes on Iraq killed at least 20 militants, including several Iranians, on Wednesday, according to the Hashed al-Shaabi, an armed Iraqi alliance that includes pro-Iran groups.

The United States and Saudi Arabia said they had struck Iran-backed armed militants in Iraq in response to attacks on US forces and Saudi oil facilities.

Washington and Tehran are Iraq’s main allies, but their enmity has long turned the country into a proxy battleground and left successive governments struggling to maintain a delicate balance between the foes.

The Hashed al-Shaabi, also known as the Popular Mobilisation Forces (PMF), said that at least 20 fighters “were martyred and another 32 wounded according to a preliminary toll”.

Two Hashed officials told AFP that five Iranian advisors were among those killed in a strike in the central province of Diyala.

AFP correspondents saw coffins wrapped in Iranian flags during a funeral organised by the Hashed al-Shaabi in Baghdad for those killed.

The Hashed alliance was created in 2014 to fight jihadists before it was formally integrated into the Iraqi armed forces.

It now includes brigades belonging to Iran-backed groups reputed for acting unilaterally.

US President Donald Trump said the strikes were coordinated with the Iraqi government, according to Fox News.

They follow growing US pressure on Baghdad to disarm pro-Iran armed groups, which have frequently targeted US facilities in the country and have long called for the withdrawal of US troops.

Iraq’s new Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, who came to power this year with Washington’s blessing, vowed to ensure those groups would hand over their weapons, but has faced pushback from some powerful factions.

Earlier this month, Zaidi visited both the United States and Iran.

– ‘Inevitable response’ –

The strikes came after Riyadh said its forces had intercepted drones targeting oil facilities, blaming the Iran-backed groups in Iraq.

The most active pro-Iran armed groups are united under an alliance known as the Islamic Resistance in Iraq, which has acted in support of Tehran during the Middle East war, claiming hundreds of attacks against US bases in Iraq and across the region.

The Islamic Resistance in Iraq said “our response to the American enemy is inevitable, and may target its tools in Saudi Arabia”.

But the group added that it would only retaliate after the Arbaeen day of pilgrimage, which falls on Tuesday.

The Arbaeen marks one of the most significant events in the Shia Muslim calendar, during which pilgrims, many from Iran, flock to Iraq to visit the holy shrines.

The pro-Iran groups denied attacking Saudi Arabia and they haven’t claimed any attacks since the US-Iran war resumed earlier this month.

– Violation –

Iraq denounced the US-Saudi strikes and said it rejects “all acts of aggression, regardless of the party responsible or the justifications presented.”

The Ministerial Council for National Security said it would “confront any violation of Iraq’s sovereignty, and prevent any source from using Iraqi territory to threaten neighbouring states”.

It reaffirmed its commitment to ensure the state’s monopoly over weapons.

Zaidi’s government has given those groups that Washington designates as terrorist organisations until September 30 to disarm.

Oil-rich Iraq has been trying to move past decades of war and unrest, but it remains vulnerable to regional and internal flare-ups.

World.title: Iraq condemns US-Saudi strikes, vows tighter control over armed groups
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq condemned U.S.-Saudi airstrikes on Wednesday that targeted Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) sites, calling the attacks a violation of its sovereignty, and announced new measures to tighten state control over security and prevent Iraqi territory from being used to threaten neighboring countries.

Following the attacks, Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi presided over an emergency meeting of the Ministerial Council for National Security, which the government said killed and injured many Iraqis.

As regional tensions rose, Al-Zaidi cancelled a planned visit to Saudi Arabia on Thursday.

In a statement published after the meeting, the council said that the strikes happened when Baghdad was already in talks with US and Saudi authorities over suspicions that Iran-aligned armed organizations operating from Iraq committed drone assaults on Saudi land.

“The government was actively engaging with the relevant parties to verify and address the concerns raised by both the Saudi and US sides,” the statement stated, adding that the military action hampered such efforts.

The council authorized a comprehensive security strategy aimed at strengthening state authority across Iraq, combating breaches of Iraqi sovereignty, and prohibiting any party from exploiting Iraqi territory to threaten neighboring nations.

The steps reflect Baghdad’s efforts to guarantee that no armed organization may launch assaults from Iraqi soil that could pull the nation into larger regional wars, while also confirming the government’s goal of bringing all security actions under state control.

The council also directed the Foreign Ministry to take legal and diplomatic measures under international law and the United Nations Charter to record the attacks and protect Iraq’s legal rights.

The government condemned the attacks but emphasized that responding to security threats and enforcing the law is solely the responsibility of Iraq’s constitutional institutions.

“The government rejects all acts of aggression, regardless of the party responsible or the justifications presented,” the statement read.

The council underlined Baghdad’s commitment to addressing regional conflicts via diplomacy while maintaining efforts to keep all armaments under state control.

It also restated Iraq’s commitment to carrying out the security agreement guiding the departure of the US-led international coalition by the end of September 2026.

The emergency conference occurred hours after US President Donald Trump claimed that the midnight attacks were coordinated with the Iraqi government, something Baghdad has not officially verified.

Iraqi authorities have openly opposed the operation, emphasizing the political sensitivity of the attacks.

The events highlight Al-Zaidi’s increasingly precarious situation, as he seeks to boost Iraq’s connections with the US and Gulf Arab governments while retaining relations with Iran.

His decision to cancel the Saudi visit underlines the gravity of the problem, as Baghdad seeks to temper regional tensions while preventing Iraqi land from becoming a battlefield for opposing forces.

The government’s current security strategy also suggests a renewed desire to prevent armed groups from operating outside official control, as Baghdad wants to reassure neighboring nations that Iraq will not be used as a springboard for assaults that endanger regional peace.

World.title: Uptime Institute partners with T964 to expand Iraq’s digital infrastructure
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Uptime Institute, based in the United States, and Iraqi digital infrastructure company Tech964 Holding Limited (T964) have formed a strategic partnership to help develop Iraq’s digital infrastructure, marking the latest technology agreement to result from Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s investment-focused visit to Washington.

The agreement, signed earlier this month at the U.S.-Iraq Business Summit hosted by the US Chamber of Commerce, names T964 as Uptime Institute’s business partner in Iraq to promote international data center standards, professional training, and the development of resilient digital infrastructure.

The agreement is part of Baghdad’s larger effort to diversify its economy beyond oil by increasing digital infrastructure, attracting technological investment, and bolstering industries including cloud computing, artificial intelligence, financial technology, and cybersecurity.

T964, one of Iraq’s major private digital infrastructure businesses, has announced that it would collaborate with the Uptime Institute to implement internationally recognized standards for the country’s expanding network of data centers, as well as increase technical competence and operational best practices.

The partnership is anticipated to help establish carrier-neutral data centers, telecommunications infrastructure, cloud services, and AI-ready digital platforms, all of which the government believes are important to modernizing public services and stimulating private-sector investment.

The pact follows a series of technological ties announced during Al-Zaidi’s tour to the United States, during which Iraq inked more than 50 agreements totaling more than $60 billion in the energy, banking, infrastructure, industrial, and technology sectors.

Improving digital infrastructure has become a key component of Iraq’s long-term economic plan, as the country strives to lessen reliance on oil earnings and establish a knowledge-based economy capable of attracting foreign technology businesses while also encouraging homegrown innovation.

The alliance also underscores increased US private-sector interest in Iraq’s digital economy, especially as demand for secure data centers, cloud computing capacity, and AI infrastructure in the Middle East grows.

Iraq has increasingly prioritized digital infrastructure for foreign investment alongside energy and transportation, with officials claiming that internationally certified data centers and modern telecommunications networks will be critical to supporting e-government services, digital banking, e-commerce, and artificial intelligence, as well as strengthening Iraq’s role as an emerging regional technology hub.

World.title: Jammu and Kashmir: Properties of 5 Pakistan-based terrorist handlers attached in Reasi
World.content:
JAMMU: J&K Police attached properties of five Pakistan-based terrorist handlers in Reasi district on Thursday to prevent their misuse for terror financing in the Union Territory.

The attachment â linked to a case registered at Mahore PS under the provisions of BNS, Unlawful Activities Prevention Act, and Egress and Internal Movement Control Ordinance Act â was carried out by a police team led by Mahore SDPO Parul Bhardwaj in the presence of the executive magistrate and local witnesses, a spokesperson said.

One kanal is approximately 5,445sqft, while one marla measures around 272.2sqft.

âDuring investigation, credible evidence established that the accused had exfiltrated to Pakistan to attain terrorist training. They were currently operating as terrorist handlers from across the border, actively promoting, facilitating, and coordinating activities of ultras. The accused allegedly planned to use the assets to facilitate, finance, and sustain terror acts,â the spokesperson said.

World.title: Calling registered AYUSH doctors 'quacks' has no legal basis: NCISM
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In a move likely to intensify the debate over the status of traditional medicine practitioners, the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM) has warned that calling duly registered AYUSH doctors "quacks" or "bogus doctors" has no legal basis and could violate their legal and constitutional rights.

The commission said it had come to its notice that qualified practitioners holding recognised degrees in Ayurveda, Unani, Siddha and Sowa-Rigpa were being subjected to harassment, defamation and false characterisation through public notices, print and electronic media, social media platforms and other public forums.

The NCISM said practitioners registered with the appropriate State Medical Councils for Indian Medicine and recognised under the Indian Medicine Central Council Act, 1970, and the NCISM Act, 2020, are legally recognised medical practitioners.

It said the NCISM Act provides the statutory framework for regulating education, ethics and professional practice in Indian systems of medicine and confers legal rights and responsibilities on registered practitioners.

"There is no legal basis for describing such registered practitioners as 'quacks' or 'bogus doctors'," the commission said, adding that any individual, institution, media organisation or authority publicly using such terms may be acting contrary to the legal recognition granted under the NCISM Act, 2020, and may be infringing upon the practitioners' professional and constitutional rights.

Reiterating its position, the commission said all duly qualified and registered practitioners of the Indian System of Medicine are legally recognised healthcare professionals and are entitled to the rights, protections and professional respect accorded to them under the law.

The NCISM's stand is also consistent with the Centre's responses in Parliament, where the Ministry of AYUSH has repeatedly distinguished between unrecognised persons posing as AYUSH practitioners, who are liable for penal action under the law, and duly qualified and registered practitioners recognised under the NCISM Act.

World.title: Woman injured during NEET protest discharged from RML after 10 days
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The 21-year-old woman who was critically injured during a protest over the NEET examination in Delhi on July 20 was discharged from Dr Ram Manohar Lohia (RML) Hospital on Thursday after making a satisfactory recovery following 10 days of treatment.

According to medical records, Sakshi had sustained grievous injuries, including head, chest and abdominal trauma. She also suffered swelling and congestion of the face with a bluish tinge, multiple contusions on both shoulders, the upper chest and the right thigh, and a patterned abrasion on the left forearm suspected to be consistent with a shoe-sole mark.

World.title: 'Can pellet guns be used against peaceful protesters under any circumstances?' CJP slams SC
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on Thursday sharply challenged the Supreme Courtâs observations on the use of pellet guns during student protests. CJP spokesperson Saurav Das accused the court of failing to rigorously examine whether the police action against peaceful demonstrators on July 20 was justified.

Responding to the hearing on petitions related to the Delhi protest crackdown, Das said the courtâs position raised serious questions about the use of force against non-violent protesters and who authorised it.

âThe Supreme Court has stated that pellet guns may be used in exceptional circumstances. First, did the peaceful protesters actually create such exceptional circumstances on July 20th?... There was no situation that warranted the use of pellet guns....

The Supreme Court should have rigorously examined whether the circumstances truly justified an action that caused a person to lose their eyesight. The second point is: Can pellet guns be used against peaceful protesters under any circumstances?.

.. Ultimately, the Home Minister was responsible for supervision and issuing orders... The Supreme Court, too, needs to give serious and strict consideration to these matters, rather than simply rubber-stamping or endorsing such measures,â Das said.





His remarks came after the Supreme Court heard a petition challenging the Delhi Policeâs use of pellet guns during the July 20 march from Jantar Mantar to Parliament, during which several protesters were injured, and some allegedly suffered permanent loss of eyesight.

The CJP has maintained that the march was peaceful and that the police response was disproportionate.

According to the party, police attempted to stop the procession through a lathi charge and the firing of pellet guns.

Das sought to place responsibility squarely on the government rather than on procedural justifications for the use of force.

âThe opposition is doing its job. Its role is precisely to ask questions and hold the government accountable. I saw that a discussion was taking place in Parliament. There ought to be a discussion on who issued the orders on July 20th, and who will answer for the conduct of the police towards the protesters and the brutality inflicted upon them? Naturally, the Home Minister should provide an answer regarding this matter,â he said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The remarks came as the CJP has continued to question the handling of the July 20 protests in both political and legal forums. Earlier, Das had also criticised a separate Supreme Court interim order in a batch of PILs related to the protests, arguing that it could allow governments to continue investigations against protesters despite what he described as the Centreâs assurance that FIRs would be withdrawn.

For the CJP, the debate has moved beyond crowd control and entered the realm of public accountability. The party insists that the central question is not simply whether pellet guns can be used in exceptional circumstances, but whether the events of July 20 ever met that threshold in the first place.

World.title: From LPG to Rabi fertilisers: PM Modi reviews Middle East crisis preparedness
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday chaired a high-level meeting of the Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS) to review the ongoing conflict in Middle East and assess India's preparedness to deal with its impact.

The meeting reviewed the geopolitical situation, the availability of fuel and fertilisers, the safety of Indian citizens and the diaspora and measures to protect Indian seafarers operating in conflict zones. This was the fourth special CCS meeting held on the issue.

During the meet, several top cabinet ministers including Amit Shah, Rajnath Singh and NSA chief Ajit Doval were also present.

The Cabinet Secretary briefed the committee on the steps taken to ensure uninterrupted supplies of petroleum products, including crude oil, LPG and LNG.

According to the briefing, India has diversified its LPG procurement sources and that the stock position of major petroleum products remains adequate.

The government said sufficient crude oil supplies have enabled public sector refineries to operate at utilisation levels of over 100%, ensuring continued production of petrol, diesel and other fuels. It also highlighted ongoing efforts to expand piped natural gas (PNG) connections, strengthen the National Gas Grid, increase LNG import and regasification capacity and improve city gas distribution networks.





The CCS also reviewed fertiliser availability ahead of the upcoming Rabi season. PM Modi further directed officials to take all necessary measures to ensure uninterrupted fertiliser supplies and explore alternate sources wherever required.

The situation of Indian seafarers serving on domestic and foreign-flagged vessels in conflict zones also came up for discussion. PM directed the government to establish a dedicated mechanism to provide timely information, emergency assistance and counselling to seafarers and their families.

Emphasising the need to protect Indian nationals overseas, PM Modi said every effort should be made to safeguard both Indian citizens and the Indian diaspora from the impact of the conflict, according to Press Information Bureau.

PM Modi also stressed the importance of reducing dependence on conventional energy sources and called for greater emphasis on renewable energy, including solar power and other non-fossil fuel-based sources, to strengthen India's long-term energy security.

Calling for a whole-of-government approach, PM Modi directed ministries and departments to continue working in close coordination. He also asked officials to establish a unified monitoring mechanism to regularly track developments in Middle East and ensure quick implementation of measures required to protect the interests of Indian citizens.

The ongoing conflict in Middle East involving the United States, Iran and Israel has affected global energy markets and supply chains. India has also faced concerns over LPG supplies and energy security due to disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz, leading the government to regularly review the evolving situation and preparedness measures.

World.title: NEET-UG 2026 case: CBI links leak to teachers who set paper, did translation work - report
World.content:
NEW DELHI: NEET-UG 2026 was compromised after the same set of individuals was entrusted with both question-setting and translation, exposing a key procedural lapse.

The teachers entrusted with setting and translating the NEET-UG 2026 question paper allegedly memorised the final questions, reconstructed them from memory and shared them with a select group of students attending their private coaching classes, PTI cited as sources revealed.

The paper setters â chemistry teacher P V Kulkarni, physics teacher Manisha Gurunath Mandhare and biology teacher Manisha Sanjay Havaldar â were responsible for both preparing the question paper and translating it into Marathi, giving them prolonged access to the final version ahead of the May 3 examination.

Although the experts were kept in a sanitised environment during the paper preparation process, they were allowed to return home each day, the statement reads.

During this period, they allegedly reconstructed the questions from memory and shared them with a select group of students, marking them as "very important" without revealing they were from the upcoming NEET examination.

CBI may recommend changes

Investigators said the questions later spread beyond the coaching classes after local beautician Manisha Waghmare allegedly obtained the reconstructed question bank from some students. She allegedly typed the questions into a paper-like format and sold them to Dhananjay Nivrutti Lokhande, who circulated them through a network of middlemen across multiple states in exchange for lakhs of rupees.

The agency has informally conveyed the issue to the National Testing Agency (NTA) and is likely to recommend separating the two responsibilities in its formal recommendations.

The incident came into light after one aspirant received the purported question paper and alerted the NTA, which cancelled the NEET-UG 2026 examination on May 12.

The Union education ministry subsequently handed the probe to the CBI, which arrested 13 people, including the three subject experts, Waghmare, coaching institute associates and alleged middlemen.

World.title: One-day scientific conference held at Cancer Institute (WIA)
World.content:
The Department of Onco Physiotherapy at the Cancer Institute (WIA) organised “REGAIN 2026 – Head and Neck Cancer Rehabilitation”, a one-day scientific conference, on July 30 as a part of the birth centenary celebrations of oncologist V. Shanta and in commemoration of World Head and Neck Cancer Day.

According to a press release, the event also paid tribute to the birth anniversary of Muthulakshmi Reddy, India’s first woman medical doctor and founder of the Cancer Institute (WIA). Arvind Krishnamurthy, the institute’s Deputy Medical Director, inaugurated the conference in which around 210 delegates from across the country participated. It featured nearly 25 scientific deliberations by experts, covering recent advances in multidisciplinary rehabilitation for patients with head and neck cancer.

Institute’s Vice Chairman E. Hemanth Raj; Associate Director R. Swaminathan; head of the Department of Onco Physiotherapy S. Vijay; and Chief Physiotherapist and Scientist D M.S. Satish took part, the release said.

World.title: Two arrested for stealing mobile phones from truck drivers in Madhavaram
World.content:
Two men were arrested for allegedly stealing eight mobile phones from truck drivers who were asleep on the terrace of a transport company in Madhavaram.

According to the police, one of the truck drivers, Kapil, 33, from Thanjavur, returned to the transport company where he worked after unloading goods in Vijayawada on Monday, and slept on the terrace with other truck drivers.

When Kapil woke up early on Tuesday, he found that his mobile phone and those of seven other truck drivers had been stolen. Based on his complaint, the Crime Wing of the Madhavaram Police Station registered a case and launched an investigation.

The probe revealed that the suspects had arrived on a motorcycle and stolen the mobile phones.

The police arrested the accused identified as Jagan, 22, of Periamet, and Sham, 21, of Ezhil Nagar, Kodungaiyur. All the eight stolen mobile phones were recovered from the accused and the motorcycle used in the offence was seized.

World.title: Minister Vijay Balaji inaugurates projects in Vellore
World.content:
Minister of Handlooms and Textiles M. Vijay Balaji inaugurated facilities including health centres, an out-patient block, additional school buildings and anganwadi centres in Vellore on Thursday.

The Minister also opened additional buildings in government schools at Virinchipuram, Chinna Allapuram and K.V. Kuppam. An anganwadi centre was opened in Karigiri village near Katpadi. As part of environmentally friendly measures, 20 e-carts for garbage collection were also flagged off in Gudiyatham town.

Accompanied by officials and Collector P.S. Leela Alex, Mr. Balaji inspected the newly opened facilities. “The new health sub-centre and other health facilities will help residents, especially in remote villages and tribal hamlets, get basic health care services. Expectant mothers will be monitored by staff in these health facilities,” M. Vijay Chandran, District Health Officer (DHO), Vellore, said.

The new health centre, which was built at a cost of ₹45 lakh at Murukambattu village near Gudiyatham town, was a long-standing demand of residents. At present, they trek at least 8-10 kms to reach Gudiyatham, the nearest town that has a government taluk hospital for health services. “The new health centre at Murukambattu village will help senior citizens and women. The new facility should have regular staff to attend to emergencies,” said G. Sivakumar, a resident.

The new health centre will have two beds for inpatients, an outpatients block, a separate cabin for Village Health Nurse (VHN), a common visitors hall, laboratory facilities, and a pharmacy with adequate stocks. Adequate parking space for ambulances and other vehicles will also be provided.

Officials said that health sub-centres will focus on the health of expectant mothers, children, immunization programmes and other government health schemes in remote villages. The VHN was also trained to treat minor illnesses like fever and cold. The health centre will work between 8 a.m. and 3 p.m. on all days except on Sundays.

As per norms, a group of villages should have more than 5,000 residents to get a new sub-health centre. At present, the district has 48 primary health centres and 235 sub-health centres.

A block-level public health testing unit was also opened at Melpadi tribal village, that comes under Anaicut panchayat union in Jawadhu Hills. The new facility, built at a cost of ₹55 lakh, will help testing biological samples provided by residents.

World.title: Categorise English as native language in NEP 2020: Anglo Indian Federation
World.content:
The Anglo-Indians Welfare Federation of India (AIWFI) has urged the Union government to categorise English as a native language.

In a letter to the Prime Minister and the Union Minister for Education, the federation said, “English is the medium of instruction in all subjects in most schools across the country along with an additional native language. The categorisation of English overnight as a foreign language amounts to violation of the students’ rights.”

The Union government has been implementing the three-language criteria since July 1 in the country from Class 9 onwards.

President of the federation Augustine Roy Rozario added that the categorisation of English as a foreign language will affect the five lakh Anglo-Indians settled in the country. “They have adopted English as their mother tongue and will be compelled to learn their main subjects in two or three native Languages in addition to the English language which could ultimately lead to the destruction of their Mother tongue.” he said.

Rozario urged the Union government to categorise the English Language as one of the native languages in the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, to enable students to continue their education.

World.title: Anna Salai elevated corridor Project receives Tokio Marine Group award for innovative and futuristic design
World.content: The Mount Road Elevated Corridor Project Team has received the Japan International Award 2026 from the Tokio Marine Group for Innovative and Futuristic Design. A release said, the project successfully addresses one of the most complex challenges in modern urban transportation engineering — designing an elevated corridor over operational underground metro tunnels and stations, while ensuring uninterrupted metro services and maintaining structural stresses, settlements, and deformations within limits. M. Krishnaprabhu, Senior Bridge Design Engineer of the project consultant NKAB, received the award.

World.title: ‘No truth to reports of OPS contemplating switch to TVK’
World.content:
Former Chief Minister O. Panneerselvam is not planning to quit the DMK and join the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), sources close to him said on Thursday, dismissing speculation about a possible switch as “baseless”.

The sources said Mr. Panneerselvam continued to enjoy cordial relations with the DMK leadership and remained in touch with party president M.K. Stalin.

“He has informed the party leadership of his position. Mr. Panneerselvam is also expected to make his stand clear publicly in a day or two,” they said.

A former DMK Minister, who met Mr. Panneerselvam a few days ago, also said the latter had categorically denied reports linking him with the TVK.

Speculation over Mr. Panneerselvam’s political future surfaced after six AIADMK MLAs resigned their Assembly seats and joined the ruling TVK.

However, sources close to the former Chief Minister said there was no basis for reports suggesting that he was considering a similar move. There were also claims that his son and former MP, O.P. Raveendranath, was in favour of joining the TVK.

World.title: Residents oppose setting up of sewage treatment plant at Jawadhu Hills in Vellore
World.content:
Residents of Pennathur village, which comes under Anaicut panchayat union near Vellore Corporation, have been opposing the setting up of a new Sewage Treatment Plant (STP) in the village, fearing ground water pollution in surrounding farming villages.

At a public hearing organised by the district administration on the proposed plant, residents said that more than 700 families reside in the village in the foothills of the Jawadhu Hills. Most of the families depend on agriculture and dairy farming.

The new STP will be built to treat sewage water in Mettupalayam hamlet to treat waste and other contaminated water collected from households in the town. “The new treatment plant should be built away from the village to prevent pollution of groundwater in the area. As most of the farmers depend on borewells and lakes, such pollution will ruin their livelihood,” said V. Ramu, a farmer.

Affected residents said that two lakes and a few ponds in the village provide farmers with much-needed water for irrigation. Residents said that the establishment of the sewage treatment plant near water bodies and farmland will affect water quality in the area. Pollution of groundwater and surface water will impact farming in these villages, which covers at least 800 acres under cultivation.

Also, water for household consumption comes from these water bodies in the villages. Local panchayats have sunk deep borewells around the lakes to pump water to Over Head Tanks (OHTs) in these two villages for domestic consumption.

Panchayat officials said that the proposed plant will be set up on a three-acre plot at the border area of the village under the Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM) at a cost of ₹5.8 crore. The new plant will treat wastewater, mainly from households in the town and surrounding villages for a nominal fee from each household. Recycled water will be used to water plants on stretches.

At present, panchayat officials said that most of the existing storm water drains in the town are used to discharge sewage from houses, which flows into nearby lakes and ponds, resulting in pollution. The new plant will stop the discharge of sewage into drains.

World.title: Stolen red sanders recovered near Arakkonam: four persons held
World.content:
Four persons were arrested by Tirupattur town police after they recovered red sanders stolen from a government depot at a car shed near Arakkonam town in Ranipet on Thursday.

Police said that the arrested persons were identified as B. Chitti, 37, a resident of Chittoor (A.P), S. Poovarasan, 25, from Tiruttani, R. Ajith, 24, a native of Tirupattur, and G. Satyaraj, 58, the owner of the car shed.

Initial inquiry revealed that on July 18, forest staff at Government Sandalwood Depot in Tirupattur town found that 55 logs of red sanders, weighing 1.75 tonnes, were stolen. The missing red sanders logs have been estimated around ₹50 lakh.

Based on a complaint by forest officials, a case was registered by Tirupattur town police. Subsequently, M. Mahendran, District Forest Officer (DFO), Tirupattur, suspended five forest staff who were on duty at the depot.

Police said that based on a tip-off, two special teams conducted searches in a car shed of a house near Arakkonam town, and seized 133 logs of red sanders weighing around four tonnes, including 1.75 tonnes of red sanders stolen from the government depot.

Investigations found that car shed owner Satyaraj rented-out the shed to Poovarasan for car parking. They told police that Chitti and Ajith were also involved in the incident.

Police said arrested persons were lodged at Central Prison in Vellore. Further probe is under way.

The government depot is used to store sandalwood and red sanders that were seized from smugglers during surprise checks at border areas on Tamil Nadu-Andhra Pradesh. Later, the seized wooden logs were used to make incense sticks.

World.title: Iran war: Why Gulf nations are turning to China, not US, to reopen Strait of Hormuz
World.content:
The war in West Asia between the United States and Iran continues to escalate after five months of hostilities, and the Gulf Arab states are now looking to China and not Washington to utilise its economic leverage over Tehran to help reopen the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea, a report stated.

It is also being viewed as a way for the Gulf countries to test the waters as to how far Beijing is ready and able to pressure Iran. The push for a bigger Chinese role by the Gulf states is triggered by “frustration,” Gulf sources told Reuters.

Though the US-Israel joint war against Iran has hurt the Gulf’s regional foe but has also restricted the Middle East countries’ vital oil and energy exports as the Strait of Hormuz remains choked.

Iraqis inspect damaged structures at the site of an airstrike on a Popular Mobilization Forces base in Mosul, Iraq. (AP Photo) Iraqis inspect damaged structures at the site of an airstrike on a Popular Mobilization Forces base in Mosul, Iraq. (AP Photo)

Why China is being seen as a key player

After Iran and its allies in Iraq and Yemen threatened to block the Bab el-Mandeb waterway in the Red Sea, along with Hormuz, the Gulf states looked towards Chinese administration, noting that the war has exposed America’s limitations, sources told news agency Reuters. China remains the world’s largest buyer of oil, revealing its enormous power over global oil prices.

After the war broke out in February, China’s crude oil imports plunged due to soaring prices. In June, Chinese oil imports were down by over 40 per cent, in comparison to last year. Interestingly, the decline in oil imports hasn’t affected China’s domestic economy.

China steps up diplomatic outreach

Dozens of calls and meetings have been conducted between China’s Foreign Minister Wang Yi and his counterparts, who are seeking a ceasefire in the region as the conflict enters its sixth month. Meanwhile, China’s special envoy Zhai Jun has held talks in Gulf Arab capitals as well as Tehran, Reuters reported.

“China has maintained close communication with all parties, and has consistently worked to stop the fighting and promote peace,” Beijing’s foreign ministry said in a statement.



Beijing’s economic ties with Gulf and Iran

Seeking help from China to pause the West Asia conflict comes from the position of Beijing, which has been both a major buyer of oil from the Gulf and reportedly the biggest trading partner of Iran.

“There’s huge respect between the Gulf and China, and they are a big trading partner, so any issue is raised in a very quiet manner,” the source told Reuters.

Iran maintains Hormuz stance

Iran has reiterated that it will maintain its control over the Strait of Hormuz after being attacked by the US military amid talks that were ongoing over the nuclear programme.

World.title: Watch: Thousands swim into Spain’s Ceuta from Morocco. Why the border collapsed today
World.content:
Thousands of migrants streamed into Spain’s territory of Ceuta in the North African enclave from Morocco on Thursday, triggering local officials to call on Madrid to declare a national emergency and send the military to restore the border frontier.

Ceuta leader says resources overwhelmed

The territory’s leader, Juan Jesús Vivas, said the influx of migrants from Morocco is overwhelming the resources and called on the government in Spain to intervene in the matter, BBC reported. The report added that Spain’s Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska is expected to visit Ceuta on Friday.

Thousands of migrants from Morocco poured over the country’s border with Spain and into the country’s African enclave of Ceuta after swimming around border barriers to reach the territory. The latest wave comes after more than 1,500 migrants arrived in Ceuta by sea over the past… pic.twitter.com/kETfPOPTbO — Fox News (@FoxNews) July 30, 2026

Declining the requests of Ceuta’s local officials to announce a national emergency over the migrant crisis, Spain’s interior ministry said it would guarantee the safety of citizens and the integrity of the nation’s border.

‘Absolute chaos’: Border officials

“The situation is absolute chaos. It’s not possible to give precise numbers, but there are thousands of migrants crossing,” said Rachid Sbihi, head of the association that represents Spain’s Civil Guard officers in Ceuta, adding that the border has “totally collapsed,” AP reported.

Sánchez es un traidor, un corrupto y un indecente. Actúa como el enemigo del pueblo español. La emergencia nacional solo puede resolverse echándole y sentándole en el banquillo.#Ceuta pic.twitter.com/yLicTcD6hU — Santiago Abascal 🇪🇸 (@Santi_ABASCAL) July 30, 2026

Videos show migrants swimming into Ceuta

Videos of the migrants entering the Spanish territory on Thursday have gone viral on social media, showing them using inflatable rings and other devices to float and swim into Ceuta, while others were seen running through a gate located in the border fence.

The scene appeared to be reminiscent of the migrant crossing in May 2021, when around 10,000 people from Morocco and sub-Saharan Africa entered the Spanish territory of Ceuta.

2,000–3,000 reported to have crossed

According to a Guardia Civil spokesperson, the migrants were “massively entering from the sea” through the Tarajal breakwater. Reuters, quoting Spain’s state television TVE, reported that 2,000 to 3,000 people had crossed into Ceuta.

Migrants cross from Morocco into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta. (AP Photo) Migrants cross from Morocco into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta. (AP Photo)

Why Ceuta remains a migration hotspot

Ceuta is situated on Morocco’s northern coast and is separated from Spain by the Strait of Gibraltar, and has long been a hub for migrants who are trying to reach Europe.

For migrants who are seeking better financial opportunities or an escape from violence in their home country, Spain becomes the focal point of entry to Europe.



Several migrants who are successful in reaching Ceuta, or its sister city Melilla, are returned immediately by the authorities. A few of those held in migrant shelters are processed and can apply for asylum in Spain, AP reported.

Deaths reported amid latest crossing

The escalation of migrant influx at the border between Spain and Morocco comes after a surge in migrants trying to reach the small exclave, and a vast majority doing so via swimming.

An AP report stated that at least three people were killed while trying to enter Ceuta by sea.

World.title: Leave of all officials cancelled; 24×7 control rooms in each affected district: Gujarat Government
World.content:
Ravi also instructed the District Collectors to regularly share updates with the media so that citizens receive accurate information regarding the rainfall situation and the measures being undertaken by the administration.

LEAVE of all officials in the 13 rain-affected districts of Gujarat has been cancelled with immediate effect, with one Class I officer deployed round-the-clock for supervision while 24×7 control rooms remain operational in each district, officials said on Thursday.

The decisions were taken in a review meeting on Thursday – in view of heavy rain alert – at the State Emergency Operation Centre (SEOC) in Gandhinagar under the chairmanship of Additional Chief Secretary for Revenue Department Jayanti Ravi to ensure that the administrative machinery remains fully prepared and alert.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a forecast of heavy to extremely heavy rainfall from July 31 to August 2, issuing a high alert for 13 districts – Surat, Vadodara, Ahmedabad, Bhavnagar, Bharuch, Anand, Narmada, Tapi, Dang, Chhota Udepur, Panchmahal, Dahod, Mahisagar and surrounding areas.

World.title: ‘No substantial change in case’s circumstances’: Second bail plea of ex-PU professor accused of wife’s murder also rejected
World.content:
The Chandigarh district court on Thursday dismissed the second regular bail application of former Panjab University (PU) professor Bharat Bhushan Goyal, who is accused of murdering his wife, holding that the examination of the prosecution’s first witness and filing of the chargesheet did not constitute a “substantial change in the circumstances” to justify his release.

Additional Sessions Judge Dr Harpreet Kaur observed that Bharat Bhushan’s earlier bail application had already been dismissed on merits and that the grounds raised in the second plea were insufficient for reconsideration.

“The present second regular bail application has been filed by the applicant solely on the ground that challan has been presented and the material witness… has been examined. The same cannot be treated as substantial change in the circumstances of the case,” the court said.

Referring to the Supreme Court’s judgment in Virupakshappa Gouda and another versus State of Karnataka, the court further observed, “Filing of chargesheet does not in any manner lessen the allegations made by the prosecution. Rather the filing of the chargesheet establishes that after due investigation, the investigating agency having found material has placed the chargesheet for the trial of the accused”.

“At the stage of consideration of bail application, the court is not expected to undertake a meticulous examination of the evidence or record finding on its admissibility or evidentiary value as the same are matters to be determined during trial,” the court said.

Holding that there was “no material change” in the circumstances of the case after the dismissal of first bail application coupled with the seriousness of the allegations, nature of the offence, and the stage of proceeding, the court said it did not find “any justifiable ground” to enlarge the accused on regular bail.

According to the prosecution, the FIR was initially registered on the complaint of Bharat Bhushan himself, who claimed that unknown persons had entered his PU residence on the intervening night of November 3-4, 2021, and murdered his wife, Seema, after tying her hands, legs and mouth. During investigation, however, the Central Forensic Science Laboratory (CFSL) reportedly found that the iron mesh door had been cut from inside the house. The prosecution further relied on a Brain Electrical Oscillation Signature (BEOS) profiling report, following which the PU professor was arrested on December 8, 2025.



Seeking bail, counsel for Bharat Bhushan, submitted that the accused had been falsely implicated and that circumstances had changed after the dismissal of his first bail plea. The defence argued that after the dismissal of the first bail application, the case was committed to the sessions court and after framing of the charges, the statement of Dr Parul Goyal (daughter of the accused) was recorded. After recording her statement, no other witness is left whom the applicant can influence. Her examination constitutes a “substantial change in the circumstances”, the counsel argued.

The defence further contended that the investigation in the present case has not been conducted in a “fair manner”, arguing that the brain mapping tests are not admissible in evidence and therefore cannot be considered as legally admissible evidence. The counsel also claimed that there is no direct evidence to connect the accused with the alleged offence and since he is in custody for a period of more than seven months, he is entitled for the grant of bail.

The counsel also submitted that the accused was willing to comply with any conditions imposed by the court.

Opposing the plea, the prosecution argued that there was no change in circumstances since the rejection of the earlier bail application. The state counsel submitted the allegations against the accused are grave in nature and prosecution has collected sufficient scientific evidence, including brain mapping test report, which prima facie supports the prosecution case.

World.title: Appoint Polar Ambassador, become full member of Arctic Council, suggests panel
World.content:
The Parliamentary committee on External Affairs in its report has recommended that India should appoint a Polar Ambassador and urged the government to seek “full-fledged membership” of the Arctic council so that India can engage in its activities more effectively.

India is currently one of the 13 observer countries of the Arctic Council, which comprises of 8 nations that have landmass in the region. The observer countries do not have decision making powers. They also can’t make financial contributions or undertake research in the arctic directly.



The committee, in its recommendations said: “…it is imperative that India also has such an Ambassador at a level equivalent to other countries exclusively to deal with polar regions. Creating such a position will not only help India project the importance given to these regions in its foreign policy architecture but will also help put across its policy stance in relation to polar areas or pursue polar diplomacy in a more effective manner.”

World.title: Vidya Balan on why she stopped trying to fit Bollywood’s beauty standards: ‘I was 26’
World.content:
Vidya Balan opens up about gaining weight, feeling insecure, and trying to fit into a younger image in Bollywood. (Source: Vidya/Instagram)

For an actor celebrated today for her bold choices and self-assured screen presence, Vidya Balan’s early years in the film industry were filled with doubt, criticism, and deep insecurity.

In an interview, Vidya once opened up about how external pressure and internal conflict affected her emotionally and physically. She shared:

“What people don’t understand about weight—but what I’ve understood through my work with my healer over the years—is weight is also protection. When you feel insecure, a lot of times you put on weight.”

The Emmy-nominated actor, who made her Bollywood debut with Parineeta at age 26, revealed that being told she wasn’t “young enough” for certain roles had a lasting impact on her self-esteem.

World.title: 2020 Delhi riots larger conspiracy case: Umar Khalid moves HC for third time seeking bail
World.content:
For the third time, student activist Umar Khalid has moved the Delhi High Court, seeking bail in the larger conspiracy case of Northeast Delhi riots in 2020. He has been booked under the stringent Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA).

Khalid’s appeal challenging the trial court’s July 4 decision to dismiss his bail application is listed for hearing before a bench of Justices Prathiba Singh and Vikas Mahajan on Friday.



The HC had earlier rejected his bail plea twice – in October 2022 and September 2025. Both times, the Supreme Court had upheld the HC order.

Khalid, arrested in September 2020, was booked under UAPA for being one of the “masterminds” of the riots that had left 53 people dead and more than 700 injured. Besides him, activist Sharjeel Imam, among others, was also booked in the case.

World.title: ICC unveils venues of 2027 ODI World Cup
World.content:
The International Cricket Council (ICC) on Thursday unveiled the venues of next year’s ODI World Cup with twelve grounds across South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia chosen. The venues were unveiled after a ceremony in Johannesburg which saw eight cities across South Africa, three in Zimbabwe and Namibia’s capital Windhoek unveiled as co-hosts for the tournament.



South Africa’s venues are Wanderers Stadium (Johannesburg), Centurion (Tshwane), Newlands Cricket Ground (Cape Town), Kingsmead Cricket Ground (Durban), St George’s Park (Gqeberha), Mangaung Oval (Bloemfontein), Boland Park (Paarl) and Buffalo Park (KuGompo City, formerly known as East London). Zimbabwe will host matches in Harare Sports Club (Harare), Queens Sports Club (Bulawayo), Fale Mosi-oa-Tunya International Cricket Stadium (Victoria Falls) and the matches in Namibia will be held in Namibia Cricket Ground (Windhoek).

World.title: Govt increases petrol price by Rs1.09, HSD price by Rs2.42
World.content:
The government on Thursday increased the prices of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.09 and Rs2.42 per litre, respectively.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs336.15 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs393.04 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs110 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs96 per litre on diesel.

The Petroleum Division’s notification said the new prices would be applicable for July 31 (Friday).

The diesel price has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

The daily pricing decision was rejected by the All Pakistan Dealers Association, which said it would consider a protest plan this week.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Naqvi urges 'all political parties' to settle issue of more provinces, says current 'system' has collapsed
World.content:
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Thursday urged all political parties to “settle” various national-level issues, including the question of creating new provinces.

Addressing the Pakistan Economic Summit 2026 being held in Islamabad, Naqvi said there was “only one solution” to improving the country’s overall condition: “You will have to take [the matter of] administrative units, provinces or whatever you may call it, to the public.”

The interior minister argued: “All political parties should sit together in a single room, whether for a day, a month or a year. They will have to settle every issue of their country, including new units and provinces.”

“Unless they do so, unless they sit together and change this, this country will remain in the same condition, regardless of how many seminars and functions you hold.”

Various political parties have demanded the creation of more provinces or administrative units for better governance.

The Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) — an ally of the PML-N-led ruling coalition — has been demanding that Karachi be designated a province separate from Sindh.

However, the PPP, which rules Sindh and is also an ally of the PML-N government at the Centre along with MQM-P, has strongly opposed the suggested move.

On the other hand, the PPP and the PTI have long advocated for a South Punjab province.

At the outset of his speech, Naqvi said, “Whether you agree or not, the system we have been living under has collapsed.”

He contended that there would be no change in the country’s conditions if the same “system” remains.

The minister emphasised that ordinary citizens wanted to be able to afford necessities and have interactions with the government, which were not being provided.

He further said: “The condition of this federal government is such that we make our budgets in the negative, and we discuss how much debt we have to incur this year.”

“[…] We will take more debts, but we will not correct things,” he pointed out.

Asserting that he was the “biggest supporter” of democracy, Naqvi highlighted that there were multiple systems even within democracy. “But we say, no matter what, we have to keep running and dragging this,” he added.

The minister said Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts, which were even hailed globally, were “simply firefighting”. “Until you correct the basics of this country while adhering to the spirit of democracy, this will remain the same,” he said.

Noting that Islamabad was a “very busy city”, Naqvi said, “Unless units are made and they take ownership, and a new leadership comes, this will not happen.”

He went on to remark that giving “stipends and tablets to youngsters” would not make them happy, as the youth wanted merit-based job opportunities and a “corrected system”.

“We are not able to give the youth that,” the interior minister said.

“If these ‘cockroaches’ get united, they can turn everything upside down,” he quipped, referring to a term often used for Gen-Z in the wake of recent student protests in India.

Noting that all business chambers and associations were present at the summit, the minister said he considered them to be “those who run the political system” and fund it.

“One gives funding of Rs500 million before elections, or the other gives Rs100m or Rs50m.”

He also said that those attending the summit were “responsible for the current state of Pakistan and where it is today”, noting that certain systems had not worked for the past 70 years.

World.title: Gangster Uzair Baloch’s brother shot, critically injured in Karachi’s Lyari: police
World.content:
KARACHI: The brother of imprisoned Uzair Baloch, chief of the defunct People’s Amn Committee, was shot and critically wounded in Karachi’s Lyari area on Thursday evening, according to police.

Chakiwara police, in a statement, said that Zubair Baloch, 40, was shot and injured on main Chakiwara Road, while two passersby were also injured. They were shifted to Civil Hospital Karachi.

South Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Syed Asad Raza told Dawn that Zubair had been arrested in seven criminal cases in 2012 and was released in January 2025.

He added that Zubair was sitting outside his residence in Singu Lane when armed suspects on a motorcycle opened fire on him and fled the scene.

Zubair sustained multiple injuries, including to his chest and abdomen, and was undergoing surgery. DIG Raza noted that one of the injured passersby was also in serious condition.

The DIG added that the police were investigating the incident from different angles, including gang rivalry and personal enmity.

A social activist from the area told Dawn, on the condition of anonymity, that Zubair had joined a “political party” a few months ago and had raised its flags in his area.

The activist also mentioned rumours in Lyari that some gangsters who had fled to Dubai and Iran after the Karachi operation had returned following the US-Iran war, and that residents were fearful of a possible resurgence of the past gang war in the area.

They added that the attackers had covered their faces and fled when a nearby shopkeeper returned fire.

Earlier in March, an anti-terrorism court (ATC) rejected bail applications of Uzair Baloch in seven cases pertaining to murder, police encounter and possession of explosives.

Uzair, along with others, had been charged with attacking law enforcers with firearms and explosives in 2012 within the jurisdiction of the Kalakot police station.

World.title: Renewed Middle East tensions pose downside risks to inflation, external sector: finance ministry
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Anticipating the new fiscal year to begin with double-digit inflation, the government on Thursday expressed concern over renewed geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, saying they posed downside risks to inflation and the external outlook.

“Renewed geopolitical tensions in the Middle East pose downside risks to inflation and the external outlook,” the Ministry of Finance said in its Monthly Economic Update & Outlook (July 2026), while assuring that the external sector would remain resilient, supported by government measures to facilitate exports and sustain the strong momentum in remittance inflows.

“Overall, prudent macroeconomic management, fiscal discipline, ongoing structural reforms, stronger industrial activity and improved external buffers are expected to sustain the recovery in economic activity while preserving macroeconomic stability,” the finance ministry said, adding that macroeconomic stabilisation had largely been achieved in FY2026.

It said the economy was expected to maintain its growth momentum in the current fiscal year, supported by “improving macroeconomic fundamentals, continued expansion in the manufacturing sector, fiscal consolidation, resilience in agriculture and a stable financial environment”.

Manufacturing activity was likely to maintain its positive trajectory, underpinned by stable energy availability, easing financial conditions, improving domestic demand and continued export-oriented production, the ministry said.

“Inflation, however, is expected to remain elevated in the near term, with CPI inflation projected in the range of 9-10 per cent in July 2026.”

At the same time, it also warned that normalisation of global energy prices remained contingent on a durable and lasting peace agreement between the US and Iran.

Among high-frequency indicators, the US Weekly Economic Index (WEI), which measures real-time economic activity, stood at 2.9pc for the week ended July 18, while its 13-week moving average stood at 2.87pc.

Likewise, the ministry said the Composite Leading Indicator suggested that Pakistan’s major export markets (OECD economies such as the UK and the US) remained broadly aligned with their long-term potential of 100, indicating continued support from external demand, although renewed geopolitical tensions could pose downside risks.

The ministry said the government’s focus on poverty alleviation and social protection continued during the fiscal year that had just ended.

In June 2026, the Bureau of Emigration and Overseas Employment registered 38,410 workers for overseas employment, reflecting continued opportunities for Pakistani workers in international labour markets, it said.

The finance ministry noted that Pakistan’s economy entered FY2027 with an improved macroeconomic environment, as the stabilisation gains of FY2026 continued to support economic recovery and strengthen prospects for sustainable growth.

“In FY2026, average CPI inflation remained within the targeted range despite elevated global oil prices and supply chain disruptions.

“Large-scale manufacturing rebounded and agriculture maintained moderate growth despite weather-related challenges.

“Improved revenue mobilisation and prudent expenditure management further strengthened the fiscal position. The external sector remained broadly balanced, with the current account recording a marginal deficit of $140 million. Record-high workers’ remittances and higher foreign exchange reserves helped offset the import recovery associated with the strengthening of domestic economic activity.”

Meanwhile, it said IT exports reached a record $4.6 billion (up 20.6pc from last year), underscoring Pakistan’s growing potential in technology and digital services. Keeping in view these positive developments, S&P Global Ratings recently upgraded Pakistan’s long-term sovereign credit rating to B from B-, indicating improved institutional capacity, sustained implementation of reforms, improved fiscal performance and a significant rebuilding of foreign exchange reserves.

“With these gains continuing to advance the foundations for sustained economic growth, real GDP growth is targeted at 4pc in FY2027, based on the government’s continued advancement of the reform agenda through deepening financial markets, broadening the domestic investor base, strengthening debt sustainability and enhancing the country’s presence in the global capital market,” the ministry said.

Nevertheless, it warned that renewed US-Iran hostilities once again posed downside risks through global energy prices, trade and financial market volatility.

However, stronger macroeconomic fundamentals, improved external buffers, government readiness and continued policy vigilance have enhanced Pakistan’s capacity to manage such shocks effectively, the ministry concluded.

World.title: ECP refuses to recognise Achakzai as PkMAP chief over failure to hold intra-party polls
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Thursday refused to recognise National Assembly Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai as chairman of the Pakhtunkhwa Milli Awami Party (PkMAP) over the party’s failure to hold intra-party elections.

A full five-member bench of the commission, headed by Chief Election Commissioner Sikandar Sultan Raja, heard the matter.

Two other cases related to the party were also fixed for hearing. It was learnt that not only Achakzai’s leadership but also certain “controversial” amendments made to the party’s constitution and PkMAP’s account details were under question.

At the initial hearing last week, the ECP bench had observed that a decision would first be made regarding the party’s counsel, Aimal Mandokhail. On Thursday, the chief election commissioner said an order would be issued regarding the power of attorney.

Raja made the remarks after asking the lawyer who had signed the power of attorney submitted to the commission.

Mandokhail replied that party chairman Achakzai had signed the document, but the chief election commissioner pointed out that there was currently no party head, as no intra-party election had been conducted so far.

He added that the power of attorney would be placed on record, but an order would be issued on whether or not it was acceptable.

Mandokhail has sought to represent the party in the three cases, but this is now subject to the ECP’s order on the power of attorney.

It was learnt that PkMAP had conducted intra-party elections on December 21, 2022, and since the term of office-bearers was fixed at three years, new elections were mandatory by December 21, 2025.

Raja said the commission had reminded the party to hold elections on October 1, 2025, and issued a show-cause notice on January 15, 2026. In response, the party sought a 180-day extension, which was granted.

However, a subsequent request for another 180-day extension was rejected, with the commission clarifying that intra-party elections must be completed by June 19, 2026, in any case. The party neither held the elections nor submitted a proper response to the ECP.

World.title: PM Shehbaz briefed on digitisation of consular services for overseas Pakistanis: PMO
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The foreign ministry briefed Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on enhanced consular services for overseas Pakistanis, including the digitisation of systems for services such as document attestation and foreign payments, the PMO said on Thursday.

According to a statement issued by the PMO, PM Shehbaz chaired a meeting in Islamabad, where he was briefed on the progress of these initiatives by officials from the foreign ministry, the interior ministry, the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA), the IT ministry, Pakistan’s ambassadors posted in various countries and other senior officials.

The meeting was attended by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, alongside Federal Ministers Ahsan Iqbal Cheema, Attaullah Tarar, Chaudhry Salik Hussain and Shaza Fatima Khawaja; Minister of State Aoun Chaudhry, Special Assistant Tariq Bajwa, and other senior officials.

The briefing covered enhanced services at Pakistani embassies for overseas Pakistanis, the digitisation of the document attestation process, a further simplified mechanism for complaints, and the introduction of digital systems for various services, as well as payments to Pakistan from abroad, the statement said.

“Overseas Pakistanis are our valuable asset, and providing them with all kinds of facilities is the government’s top priority,” it quoted the prime minister as saying.

The meeting was informed that, for the convenience of overseas Pakistanis, a QR code-based system has already been introduced to simplify the processes regarding the power of attorney, purchase and sale of property, and attestation of documents.

The prime minister welcomed the digitisation of the complaints registration system through QR codes, directing that these codes be prominently displayed at Pakistani embassies and missions abroad to improve public access.

He instructed that a special awareness campaign be launched for overseas Pakistanis so that a greater number of people would be able to use the QR code-based system to register their complaints.

The meeting was informed that an evening shift has recently been launched at the Foreign Office in Islamabad to facilitate citizens. Document attestation services have also been introduced at the Asaan Khidmat Centre in Islamabad.

Alongside the launch of a courier-based document attestation service, the system has also been integrated with the databases of the Higher Education Commission (HEC), Inter Boards Coordination Commission, the National Database and Registration Authority (Nadra), and the National Police Bureau, making the attestation process faster and more efficient”, according to the PMO statement.

The participants were further informed that the attestation process has been converted into a one-step procedure under the Apostille system — which reduces the process to the issuance of one authentication certificate, an “Apostille”, by the designated authority of the country where the document was issued.

The premier was informed that work was progressing rapidly on the next phase to fully digitise this entire system.

With the support of the National Information Technology Board (NITB), a mobile application is being developed through which documents such as birth and death certificates, marriage registration certificates, family registration certificates, and other official documents will also be digitally attested, the statement said.

The briefing followed an earlier meeting at the foreign ministry, chaired by DPM Dar, to review measures for further improving consular services.

Dar was briefed on the “steps undertaken to enhance public facilitation, including plans to digitalise consular services, and the introduction of morning and evening shifts to provide greater accessibility and convenience to citizens,” the FO said on X.

He directed that these services be further strengthened to ensure “efficient, transparent, and timely facilitation” for the public.

In May, the deputy premier highlighted the country’s economic progress and inviting overseas Pakistanis to “honour their roots” and invest in the country, while addressing Pakistani-American community leaders in New York.

World.title: Bilawal warns ‘countdown’ will begin for federal government if it 'steals' AJK election
World.content:
PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari warned on Thursday that a stolen election in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) would start a “countdown” for the federal government.

Polls in AJK are being held in three phases over security concerns, with the first set of polls held in Mirpur division on Monday. Scuffles, violence and allegations of rigging had marred the polling process, with the PML-N and PPP accusing each other of electoral malpractice.

“The PML-N thinks that after its defeat in Gilgit-Baltistan, a defeat in AJK would mean a countdown begins for its government,” Bilawal said while addressing a rally in Muzaffarabad ahead of the August 2 elections. “But this is a misconception.”

“If you steal [the election] … write it down, take my guarantee, that a countdown will start for your federal government,” he warned. “If you steal my mandate, I will come for your throne.”

The PPP scion added that his party had elders who had challenged former leaders, including General Ziaul Haq and Pervez Musharraf, and were experts at “hunting lions”.

He also extended a message to the PTI — which has rejected the AJK elections over alleged rigging concerns — to “start doing politics” and leave behind “boycott politics”.

“Boycotting elections, boycotting Parliament, boycotting committees, boycotting your work, boycotting struggle — if you want to boycott, you might as well just sit at home,” he said, calling on the PTI to contest the elections and conduct themselves as a political party.

“Today I extend my hand towards PTI’s workers, towards its serious politicians,” he said. “To every political party that is tired of rigging, to every political worker who wants to make their own decision, come and join your hands with mine.”

He expressed hope that together they could bring about parliamentary reforms and ensure fair elections in Kashmir and across Pakistan, saying he was ready to work with all political parties on that agenda.
